In version 2.9 the row of the second file takes its place. The custom step, as its program with the macro variables of its controls set in front of it: not checked, the copy was replaced with the NOTE of 0; checked, another copy had 4,654 rows afterwards; checked with the log the table held already, 0 were appended and 1,024 left out. A table the parser of release 2.2.0 wrote, and its log once more. The file of release 2.2.0 wrote 1,024 rows of twelve columns from the log. The parser of this release, with 1 and the same log, appended 1,024 rows: the table held every request twice, once without and once with a transaction_id. A saved file that can not be loaded was measured that day with a copy of the program of 2.8 whose count asked for a file that was not there, on copies that were only their saved file. Without the setting: the ERROR lines of the action, ERROR: The saved table .
could not be loaded and _log_append_table is not set, so nothing was read and nothing was written - the saved file was left as it is., SYSCC 1012, and the saved file as before. With 0: the ERROR lines of the action and SYSCC 1012 - and the table and its saved file replaced by the 1,024 requests of the log all the same. Version 2.9 ends that run with ERROR: The saved table .
could not be loaded, nothing was replaced and the saved file was left as it is. and writes nothing. Measured on the test system on 2026-10-14 with version 2.9 - the code file, and the program of the step with the macro variables of its controls in front of it - in SAS Job Execution jobs, on copies in CASUSER of the same table of release 2.2 (3,630 rows) and with a collected log of 1,024 requests. The ERROR line for a table whose rows can not be counted and the drop of a table an append loaded for itself were added after that pass: the drop ran in a second pass that day (the list after this one), the ERROR line has not run in SAS. The three states. At no table, without the setting, with 1 and with 0: 1,024 rows. At the copy: without the setting the ERROR line with 3630 rows, SYSCC 1012 and the copy as before; with 1 ... 1024 were appended ..., ... held 3630 ..., ... holds 4654 now ..., and the earlier rows with the checksum they had; with 0 the NOTE that the 3630 rows were replaced by the 1024. The same three answers for a copy that was only its saved file, and 1,024 rows in each state for a table without rows. 2, yes, 01 and TRUE: the ERROR line, SYSCC 1012 and the copy as before. The same log once more, with 1: NOTE: 1024 request(s) were read from the log and none of them was written: ...; the table kept its creation and its modified time, and its file its size and its time. With the table dropped from memory and only its file left: the same NOTE, the table loaded and global, and the time of the file as before. A file that holds every request twice: at no table, without the setting and with 1, 2,048 requests read, 1,024 written and 1,024 left out; with 0 at the copy 1,024 rows; with 1 at the copy 1,024 appended and 1,024 left out. A request that was cut off - the two files made by hand of 2026-10-13, with 1: the second gave ... 0 were appended ... and 1 took the place of 1 row(s) of it whose failed was missing: the table held 2 row(s) and holds 2 now. ..., and both rows had the status 200 and failed 0. Requests without a transaction ID, parsed twice: 6 rows, then 3 appended again and 9 rows. Three requests with one transaction ID: 3 rows, and a second run with 1 wrote none of them, with the times of the table and of its file as before. The step, as its program with the macro variables of its controls set: with 1 the file that was cut off and the whole one gave the same two NOTEs, and the log onto a copy appended 1,024 and the second time nothing; with 0 each run replaced the table. A saved file that can not be loaded could be staged only with two changed copies of the program: CAS refused to save a CSV under a .sashdat name (ERROR: Save exportoptions file type and name extension do not match.), and that caslib took no encrypted file. Without the setting, with 0 and with 1 each run wrote its ERROR line - ... could not be loaded and _log_append_table is not set ..., ... nothing was replaced and the saved file was left as it is., ... nothing was appended ... -, SYSCC 1012, and the file kept its 3,630 rows, its size and its time. The DATA steps. In the appends that were looked at, each DATA step on a CAS table ran in Cloud Analytic Services, no WARNING was written, SYSCC was 0, and no _TEMP_LLM_LOGS table or file was left. In a second pass on 2026-10-14, with the code file after those two changes, in SAS Job Execution jobs with test table names in CASUSER: An append that can not build its table, at a table of 2 rows that was only its saved file, whose saved copy held temperature as text: ERROR: Variable temperature has been defined as both character and numeric., and then ERROR: The new table could not be created, ... with the return code 1012, -1 rows written, 2 rows of the table and 1,024 of the log, and 0 rows taken out. SYSCC was 1012, table.tableExists answered 0 afterwards - the table the run had loaded was dropped again -, and the file had the size and the time it had before. The same with a valid table that was only its saved file: loaded from the file, 1,024 rows appended - 2, then 1,026 -, promoted and saved. The three states, on copies of the table of release 2.2 (3,630 rows): without the setting at a promoted copy and at a copy that was only its saved file, the ERROR line with 3630 rows, SYSCC 1012, and the copy and its file as before; without the setting and no table, 1,024 rows, promoted and saved; with 1 4,654 rows; with 0 the NOTE that the 3630 rows were replaced by the 1024. Not measured: the could not be loaded branches with the program as it ships, as no pass could stage a saved file that can not be loaded; a table without a label, which gets Extracted LLM Log Data; and on 2026-10-12 the appends into a table with CHAR text columns and into one with further columns, which ran on 2026-10-11.

Only the lines of a transaction (the transaction_<id> logger) and the Response Data: line name the request they belong to. Every other line is given to a request where the lines around it leave one request it can be the line of, and to none otherwise: The first lines of a request - the headers, the request data, the two Randomly generated lines - are the lines of the request whose request line stands in front of them, as long as no other request line stands in between. A first line that no request is waiting for shows that requests wrote their first lines at the same time: every request since the one whose first lines broke off keeps its request line only. The first line of a transaction belongs to the one request of its model that has all its first lines and no transaction yet. Where two such requests are waiting, the transaction is given to neither: both rows keep their prompts, options, request_id, kind and user_agent and have no transaction_id, status_code, token counts, run time, response or error_text. The lines of the score code (prompt_length:, output_length:, run_time:, response:, answer:, answers:, its ERROR line) and the Response: line are the lines of the one transaction that is running. A request is taken as still running when a later line of the log names its transaction. While a second one is running, such a line is given to neither. failed is missing for a request whose response could not be given to it, and for a request that was running where the lines of its container end. It is not 1 for either reason, within the limits at the end of this section. A request that waits. A request whose first lines are complete and that never gets a transaction stays waiting until its container's part of the file ends. The requests of that model that follow it in the part are then left open, and the NOTE counts them. First lines that broke off where the lines end. Where the first lines of a request broke off at the request line of another one and no request since has a status or an error when the lines of the container end, what stands behind the break - first lines, a transaction, lines of the score code - can be of the request that broke off as well as of a request since: the requests since keep their request line only, and all are counted in the NOTE. A transaction that starts while no request of its model has all its first lines, behind such a break, shows that the request went on, as a first line does that no request is waiting for. Where a request since has ended, nothing is taken back and the request that broke off is read as failed; a file in which it went on while each request since waited for the next one is the same line for line. One line of each kind. The score code writes each of its lines once for a request. A second line of a kind for the one request that is taken as running was written by another request: the request keeps none of the values of the score code and is counted. A Response: line without its Response Data: line behind it is the line of the one running transaction only behind the line of that transaction that follows the score code, or with a status of 400 and above. The SAS log then has NOTE: <n> request(s) were running at the same time as another request - of their container, or of another container whose lines are mixed with theirs in the file. ..., with the number of requests that can have missing values and of those whose failed is missing. Where a part of the file ends. The collected file holds the lines of one container after the other, appended pod after pod and collection after collection, and a part can begin and end in the middle of a request. In a file the collection script of this release wrote, a part ends at the line the script writes in front of the lines of each container and nowhere else: a request that is running or waiting there ends without a response and without an error, nothing that was read goes on in the next part, and a part that begins with a later line of a transaction follows that transaction to its end and gives it to no request. The time of the lines decides nothing in such a file: a line that is older is a line of its container that was written late, and a transaction that has not ended runs until it ends or its part does, so a line of the score code is given to no request while another transaction runs beside it. The time of collection of such a line decides nothing: every line of that shape ends a part, and in a file the script wrote every line of that shape is a line of the script - it puts a backslash in front of a line of a container that starts like its own, which the parser takes off again behind the first line of the script. What stands in front of that first line - lines an earlier release collected, in a file that is appended to - is read as a file without such lines, and ends at it. In a file without such lines - collected before this release, or by a process of your own - the time of the lines goes back where one part ends and the next begins, and that is the one sign of it: a line that is more than one second older than a request that is running or waiting starts the next part. Either way a request that is running where its part or the file ends has neither a response nor an error in the log: the leftover lines of the next part are not added to it, its failed is missing, and a NOTE of its own counts such requests - NOTE: <n> request(s) were running where the lines of their container end - at the end of the file, or at the end of a part of it: where the collection script wrote its line in front of the lines of the next container, or, in a file without such lines, where the time of the lines goes back. The log holds neither a response nor an error for them, and failed is missing for them. Every request whose failed is missing is counted once: in this NOTE where the lines of its container end on it, also where another request ran beside it, and in the NOTE of the requests that ran at the same time where a response could not be given to it. A request whose first lines broke off at the request line of such a request is counted with it. So is, in a file that holds no line of a transaction, a request that had all its first lines and ended at that request line. A request without a Response: line whose container went on with another request is failed = 1. In a file without the lines of the script a part boundary at which the time does not go back by more than one second is not seen; the end of this section has the further limits of such a file. The line of the script is read since version 2.6 of the step, whose code file read a file with nine such lines on 2026-10-13 (The Pass of 2026-10-13). Of what version 2.7 changed here, the backslash and the lines in front of the first line of the script ran in SAS in The Second Pass of 2026-10-13, on staged lines and on a copy of the collected file; the time of collection that decides nothing and which NOTE counts a request are not run in SAS. A line that is one second older. Inside a part a line can be one second older than the line in front of it - it is stamped when it is made and written a moment later - and ends no request. It is the line of its transaction when it names one of this part; a line of the score code or a Response: line that is older by a second is given to no request, and the requests that are running then are counted in the NOTE of the requests that ran at the same time. A transaction is over at a request line only when every later line that names it is more than a second older than that request line. That a container writes a line at most one second late is read from the line format and not from a case: a line that is stamped two or more seconds before a request line in front of it is taken for the start of the next part, and the rows around it lose values and are counted in a NOTE. Behind the first line of the collection script none of this depends on how much older a line is: a line that is older is a late line of its container, whatever its time. The lines of each container have to stay together in the file, as kubectl logs writes them and the collection script appends them. In a file that mixes the lines of several containers - a time-ordered export of a log store - the score lines of a request that ran while a request of another container was running are given to neither, so its token counts, its run time and its response are missing, and the NOTE counts it. A request line for another model does not end a request that is running. A response that holds lines of a log. While a request is the only one that is running, the lines of its response up to the next line of its transaction are kept as text, also where they start like log lines; a line there that names another transaction of the part - the Response Data: line of a request whose Response: line came earlier - ends the response. A request line there, with a Request Headers: line directly behind it or with no further line that starts like a log line behind it up to the next line of the transaction, is read as a request first and decided at the end of the file. It is a request where it gets a transaction, an error, a status or a response of its own, or where a transaction of its model starts behind it that is given to no request. A request line that gets none of them while a request that came later in its part got its transaction - which a container gives a request at once - is read as a line of the response: the file is read once more with it as text, no row is written for it, the response is whole, and the request keeps its status whatever time the quoted lines carry. A request whose container wrote nothing but its first lines there - no transaction, no error, no status - is the same file line for line, so a NOTE counts the request lines that were read that way: NOTE: <n> line(s) that read as a request line stand in the response of another request, in front of the next line of its transaction, and got no line of their own - no transaction, no error, no status and no response - while a request that came later in their part got its transaction. They were read as lines of that response, and no row was written for them. A request whose container wrote nothing but its first lines there reads the same. Where nothing came later in its part, the line can also be a request that came in while the response was written and that the end of the file, or of its part, cut off before its transaction began - two such files are the same line for line, and a test of the repository holds two that are. It is read as a line of the response, no row is written for it, the response is missing, and a NOTE counts such requests: NOTE: <n> request(s) have no response: a line that reads as a request line stands in their response, in front of the next line of their transaction, and nothing behind it in its part says whether it is a line of the response or a request that came in while the response was written and that the end of the part cut off. It was read as a line of the response. A request line that scores nothing (GET) gets no transaction either way and is read the same way. With one more line that starts like a log line behind the quoted request line, and that is no Request Headers: line, the request line is text of the response. A prompt is logged on one line and is always kept as text. This is version 2.6 of the step, and the NOTE that counts the lines read that way version 2.7; neither has run in SAS on a file that is known to hold such a line. Up to version 2.5 one more row was written for a quoted request line, the response ended in front of it, and the runs below were made with that reading. In the six collected logs of the test system (1247 requests) no request started before the one in front of it had ended, so no collected log shows these rules at work. On 2026-10-12 the parser of that day - version 2.3 of the step - ran on the test system on files put together by hand from blocks of the collected log: Two requests of one model - the five first lines of the first, the five of the second, the rest of the first, the rest of the second, with the times in file order: 2 rows with prompts and options, without a transaction_id, status_code and failed missing, and NOTE: 2 request(s) were running at the same time as another request ... 2 request(s) can have missing values, and failed is missing for 2 request(s). Two requests of two models, split behind their third transaction line: both rows with status 200, failed = 0 and their own transaction ids, the first without numbers and response, and the NOTE ending failed is missing for 0 request(s). Split inside the header lines: 2 rows with the request line only - model and timestamp -, failed missing, and the NOTE ending failed is missing for 2 request(s). A response that holds lines of a log. A response with a prompt_length: line and a request line in its middle and a further line that starts like a log line behind them: one row, status 200, failed = 0, and a response of 254 characters that holds both lines. A response of four lines whose third is a request line with one line of text behind it: 2 rows - the request with status 200 and its response cut in front of the request line, 106 characters, and a row with the model of the quoted line and everything else missing - and the NOTE 2 request(s) ... 0 request(s) can have missing values, and failed is missing for 1 request(s). This is the second of the two cases above, which this guide did not name until then. Files whose times were not in file order - the first files made for this run, in which a later block was older than the one in front of it, which is not what a container writes. Two requests of one model gave 2 rows with the request line only, failed = 1 for both and no NOTE. Two requests of two models gave one row with failed = 1 and without numbers, and one with status 200 and the token count, the run time and the response of the other request - 1029 characters that held log lines of the other transaction -, and no NOTE. The rules for the end of a part and for a line that is one second older were written after that run, for the last point and for a line that is stamped a second before the request line in front of it. They are version 2.4 of the step, which ran on the test system later that day (the third run) on these files and on three new ones put together from two real blocks. Of the two files whose times were not in file order, the one with one model gave 2 rows without a transaction and with failed missing and the NOTE of the requests that were running where the lines of their container end; the one with two models gave the first request its transaction id, no status and failed missing, and the second status 200, failed = 0, its own numbers and a response of 87 characters, with two NOTEs. Of the new files, one gave both rows status 200 with their own numbers and no NOTE; one gave a complete row and a row with its prompt length and its response but without a status, with NOTE: 2 request(s) were running at the same time ... 2 request(s) can have missing values, and failed is missing for 1 request(s).; and one a row with failed missing and NOTE: 1 request(s) were running where the lines of their container end .... Outside of SAS, the parser as it is now gives 2 rows with failed missing and the NOTE of the requests that were running where the lines of their container end for the first of those two files, and for the second each request its own values, the one without a status with failed missing. Outside of SAS as well, one line made one, two, five and thirty seconds older at each of the 31 positions of two requests that overlap gave no answered request with failed = 1 and no value of the other request, and 24,000 made-up logs whose requests were interleaved at random - with one model, and with a model per request - gave no row with a value of another request, no answered request with failed = 1 and no missing value without a NOTE. The parser as it ran on 2026-10-11 had 430 such faults on 2,000 of the logs with one model. Limits a reading of the parser found after the third run, with logs that were made up for them. None is a line of a collected log. Versions 2.6 and 2.7 of the step were changed for them; the numbers that follow each are of the Python of the parser outside of SAS, on the generators of that reading, in files with and without the lines of the collection script: A line that is two or more seconds older, between the first lines of two requests of one model. With the five first lines of a request A, the five of a request B, the rest of A and the rest of B, and one of A's first lines - or B's request line - 2, 5 or 30 seconds older than the request line in front of it, row B holds the transaction id, the token counts, the run time, the response and the status 200 of A, and the only NOTE counts row A. Of 62 such logs for each of the three, 5 gave that row where all lines carry one second, and 1, 2 and 5 where two seconds lie between the lines; with a line one second older none did. The sentence above about the 31 positions holds for two requests that are split behind their third transaction line, as the test of the repository splits them. The same row is written, without a NOTE and without a time that goes back, where a file begins in the middle of the first lines of a request while a second request of that model starts. With the lines of the collection script a line that is older is a late line of its part and starts no part, whatever its time; the tests of the repository read such files with a line 2, 5 and 30 seconds older inside a part. Without them this limit stands as written. A part that ends on a running request, in front of a part that starts later than that request did. The end of a part is seen where a line is more than a second older than the request line of a request that is running or waiting, and not where the time goes back against the line in front of it. A request that started at :00 and wrote its last line at :22, followed by the part of another container that starts at :10, is failed = 1 without a NOTE. And where two requests were running when a part ends, the earlier one is ended at the request line of a later request of its model and is failed = 1, although the lines of its container end on it. So failed can be 1 for a request that was cut off. Both cases need a second container that started seconds earlier, or requests that ran at the same time, which no collected log has shown. With the lines of the collection script the part ends at the line, the request is cut off with failed missing and counted in the NOTE. Measured with the Python of version 2.7 outside of SAS, five seeds a generator: the second generator of that reading (24,000 files) gave no cut-off request with failed = 1 and no row with a value of another request, and the numbers of the two NOTEs are the rows they count in every file that has a row for each request line; 29 files have one row fewer, the request line in a response that nothing behind it decides. Its first generator (the same seeds, 18,000 files) gave no row with a value of another request and no answered request with failed = 1; 13 files have one row fewer. A third generator, of a second reading (2,000 files), gave every request its row, no value of another request, no cut-off request with failed = 1 unless its part holds an ERROR line of it, and NOTE numbers that are the rows in every file. Version 2.6 gave 13 of the 42,000 files of the first two a row with a value of another request and one a cut-off request with failed = 1. Without them this limit stands, for failed in four ways. Every failed that is not what the part of its request says was put to its kind file by file, in the generated files of all three generators read without the lines - the 12,000 files of the four modes of the second generator that end a part while a request runs and the 18,000 of the first, five seeds each, and 2,000 of the third: 3,400 of the 32,000 files have such a value, 27 more have a row fewer than request lines and were left out, and no value was left over. No code decides them: for each kind a test of the repository holds two files that are the same byte for byte and need different rows (test_log_parser.py), and test_log_parser_generated.py sorts the values of its own files in every run and fails on a value of no kind. (1) failed = 1 for a request the lines of its container end on (3,954 rows): a request without a Response: line and without an error that is followed by another request is the same bytes whether its container was collected while it ran and the lines of a later collection or of the next container follow (failed missing), or the request ended without a line and its container went on (failed = 1). The parser reads the second wherever the time of the lines does not go back by more than a second against a request that is running or waiting, and writes no NOTE for it. Of the 2,060 such rows of the second generator, 1,453 have a request line of their own part behind them and 607 the lines of the next part; in 425 of those the next part begins more than a second before the last line in front of it and later than the request, which is no end of a part for the parser, because a file whose containers are mixed holds such lines with the container going on behind them. (2) failed = 1 for a request that was answered (47 rows), and (3) failed = 0 for a request the lines end on (none in these files, one row in 1,200 files of a sixth seed): a Response: line names no request - the Response Data: line behind it does -, and the lines end between the two. The line is read as the line of the one transaction that is running where that one has the line that follows its score code, and is given to none otherwise. (4) failed = 1 with the text of an error for a request that wrote none (235 rows, all of the third generator, the only one whose requests fail): the ERROR line of the score code names no request, like its other lines. Of the 12,000 files of the four modes of the second generator that end a part while a request runs (with and without lines a second late, a next part that starts seconds before the last line of the part, and two collections of two containers appended; the same five seeds), 319 give a row a value of another request - 62 of the 2,400 of one seed, for which version 2.6 gave 90. They are of three classes, and for each a test of the repository holds two files that are the same byte for byte and need different rows: lines of the score code behind a request whose transaction no later line names - the lines of the next container, or of that request, which was still running (313 files); such a line inside the response of the request that is running - or a response that quotes it (9 files, 4 of them also in the first class); and first lines that broke off in front of requests that ended - or a request that went on while each request since waited for the next one (1 file). What the parser makes of a part could depend on the parts in front of it. Of 600 made-up files of three parts, without a cut and without a late line, 10 gave a request the values of another request of its model. It needs three or four requests whose first lines interleave. The cause: the time of the newest request that could not be told apart from another one was kept after the last such request had been counted, so in a part that began while nothing ran a line read as older by more than a second, a part began that was none, and the request that was waiting took the next transaction. Since version 2.6 that time counts only while such a request is counted, and the 600 files - and 600 more with lines a second late - give no such row, with and without the lines of the collection script.
documents.s: Requests that run at the same time

documents.t: On 2026-10-11 Log-Parser-Code.sas as it was that day - the program with the 24 further columns, version 2.2 of the step - ran on the test system as a SAS Job Execution job, on a redacted collection of all model containers with 1040 requests to seven models, and wrote to a table of its own in CASUSER: No ERROR, no WARNING and no NOTE about requests that ran at the same time. 1040 rows and 36 columns in their order, 24 of them VARCHAR and 12 numbers, promoted and saved. The program took 4.8 seconds, the job 21. 437 embedding, 355 decision and 248 LLM rows. 787 rows with status 200 and 253 failed rows - 170 of a decision model, 83 of an LLM. They are exactly the requests without a Response: line: 251 with HTTP 401 of the score code and 2 with a KeyError. 290 embedding rows in query mode and 147 in document mode; 185 decisions with an answer. 238 LLM rows with a collection - 193 of one and 45 of another -, each with a question hash that is the input_hash of an embedding row in query mode. 867 requests of python-requests and 173 of a browser; 1040 distinct transaction ids and request ids. options in every row, 426 of them with API_KEY:REDACTED; max_tokens in 235 rows. The nine link columns empty in every row. The first twelve columns against the parser as it was before the further columns (version 2.1 of the step), which was run on the same file into a second table: 1035 rows were equal, and 5 differed in max_tokens only - missing before, and now 4000 (three times), 64 and 120, read from max_completion_tokens and max_length. The step in a flow. The code SAS Studio generated for a flow of the step (version 2.2) held the program of the step character for character and one %let line for each of the 36 column controls. Run as a job it wrote the same 1040 rows with the same 36 columns, types and labels, without an ERROR or a WARNING, and its log held _FLW_ACTION_TABLE_|CASUSER|<table>|1. The step had been put on the server with PUT /dataFlows/steps/{id} and had kept its id. The three appends and the refused one are under Appending. The parser was changed after these runs: how a line is given to a request (Requests that run at the same time), which retrieval of a prompt counts, further secrets in options, a request whose content can not be read, and what the append checks before it swaps. That parser - version 2.3 of the step - ran on the test system on 2026-10-12, on the same collection: No ERROR, no WARNING and no NOTE of the parser. 1040 rows and 36 columns in their order, 24 of them VARCHAR and 12 numbers, promoted and saved, with the label Extracted LLM Log Data. The program took 5.5 seconds, the job 21. The same counts as on 2026-10-11: 437 embedding, 355 decision and 248 LLM rows; 787 rows with status 200 and 253 failed rows; 238 rows with a question hash, 44 of them distinct, each the input_hash of an embedding row in query mode. Against the parser of 2026-10-11, which was run on the same file into a second table and joined by the transaction id: 1040 rows and 1040 distinct transaction ids each. Of the 26 columns that were compared - 11 numbers, and 15 texts by their digest - 25 were equal in every row. rag_query_hash differed in 41 rows and was filled in both: those prompts hold two or three retrievals with different questions, and the hash is now the one of the last. The step in a flow (version 2.3, as the code SAS Studio generated for a flow): the same 1040 rows in the same order and the same 36 columns with their names, order, types and labels, the 27 columns the parser fills equal in 1040 of 1040 rows, no ERROR or WARNING, and _FLW_ACTION_TABLE_|CASUSER|<table>|1 in its log. The step had been put on the server with PUT /dataFlows/steps/{id} and had kept its id. In Public. In one chain of that day the parser wrote its table to Public, under a name of its own, with the same 1040 rows and 36 columns; the table and its file were dropped again. The files made by hand are under Requests that run at the same time, the appends under Appending, and the lines of a run that is refused under Reading the Job Log. The parser was changed again after that run - version 2.4 of the step: where a part of the file ends and what a line that is one second older does, the one line of a run that is refused, the condition code of a run without a table, the function every message goes through, and the wording of one NOTE. That parser ran on the test system later that day, in the third run: 1040 rows and 36 columns for the same log, without a message, and joined by transaction_id no row differed from a parse with the parser of the second run in any of the 26 compared columns. Version 2.5 of the step differs from 2.4 in the text of its About tab and in one comment, and the code file in how it takes its settings (Settings that stay yours); neither is run in SAS. Version 2.6 reads the line the collection script of this release writes in front of every container, decides a request line in a response at the end of the file, and keeps the time of the newest request that could not be told apart only while such a request is counted (Requests that run at the same time); its code file ran on 2026-10-13 (The Pass of 2026-10-13). Outside of SAS, its Python gives for the collected log of 1040 requests the same 1040 rows, the same values in all 36 columns and the same messages as the Python of version 2.5. Version 2.7 ends a part at every line of the collection script whatever its time of collection, takes off the backslash the script puts in front of a line of a container that starts like its own, reads what stands in front of the first line of the script by the time of its lines, counts every request whose failed is missing in one of the two NOTEs, counts the request lines it read as lines of a response, and gives fewer rows a value of another request. Its code file ran in SAS in The Second Pass of 2026-10-13, on a collected file that holds no case for the two NOTEs and for the rules about a value of another request; those are not run in SAS. Outside of SAS, its Python gives for three collected logs - the 1040 requests, and the file of 2026-10-13 with and without the lines of the script, 1024 requests each - the same rows, the same values in all 36 columns and the same messages as the Python of version 2.6. Version 2.8 has the three states of _log_append_table and appends a request once; it ran on 2026-10-13 in SAS Job Execution jobs. Version 2.9 writes a request once in every state of the setting, lets a row that was cut off give way to the whole one and writes nothing where it has nothing to add; it ran on 2026-10-14 (Appending, The Pass of 2026-10-14). Version 2.10 takes an action CAS refused for no answer and then writes nothing (Reading the Job Log); its code file ran once, late on 2026-10-14, in an append with every action of CAS answered (The Pass of 2026-10-14), and a refusal has not run in SAS. Version 2.11 takes a PROC CAS step that halts for an action CAS did not run. Its code file ran early on 2026-10-15, in the ninth pass, in the three states of _log_append_table, and the step ran with Append new rows to existing table ticked and unticked; every action of CAS answered (The Pass of 2026-10-14), and a halt has not run in SAS. Version 2.12 and the code file use a connected session of their own name where the session SESSREF names is not connected; that came after the pass and has not run in SAS.
documents.s: The parser of this release on SAS Viya

documents.t: The collection script of this guide, Log-Parser-Code.sas and the LLM - Log Parser step were run on the test system (SAS Viya 2026.09) on 2026-10-11, the parser as SAS Job Execution jobs that wrote to a table in CASUSER. All of it was run with the parser as it was before the 24 further columns - version 2.1 of the step, a table of twelve columns, and an append that added rows to the existing table with table.append: Collection and redaction. The script, with only llm_log_path and llm_logging_interval changed, read the pods its selector picked - all of them model pods - and wrote 5,773 lines with 174 requests. An unredacted copy of the same logs held one provider key and seven Cookie headers; the written file held API_KEY:REDACTED once and Cookie: REDACTED seven times, neither the key nor one of the cookie values, and the same number of lines. Every kind of model that had requests. The 174 requests gave 174 rows with the twelve columns: 57 of three LLMs with prompts, response, token counts and run time; 50 of a decision model with the questions and the answers as JSON, the state, token counts and run time; 67 of an embedding model with its tokens in prompt_length and its run time, and no prompt, response or output_length. No cell held API_KEY or a Cookie header. An empty log and a log without requests. A file of 0 bytes and a file with start-up lines only each ended with the note, in replace and in append mode. The table kept its 174 rows and its saved file was not written. Append. Two newer collections with 21 and 7 requests took the table from 174 to 195 to 202 rows, and no earlier row was lost. Before the second one the table was dropped from memory while its .sashdat stayed: the parser loaded the saved table first, appended, promoted and saved it again. The three files held different requests; with the program of that day a log that was parsed twice was in the table twice. The warning for unread requests. A log collected with kubectl logs --timestamps (858 lines, 26 of them with Request: POST) gave the warning with that count and the note, and the table was left as it is. A request that is still open. A request that was still running when its container's part of the file ended gave one row with its prompts and without token counts, run time and response. The lines of another container's finished request followed it in the file, and their numbers were not added to it. Failed requests. Two requests to a decision model that failed in the container - a traceback in the log, no score lines, no Response: Status Code line - gave one row each with the questions and the state, without numbers and response. The custom step. Run as the code SAS Studio generated for a flow, in a session with a CAS session and the libref, the step wrote the same 174 rows as the program in replace mode and the same 195 after appending the second collection. The custom step in a session without a CAS session. With no cas and no libname statement in front of the generated code, the macro variable _CASNAME_ did not exist; in a job of the same context that held no other code, cas _all_ list; listed no session and the option SESSREF named CASAUTO. The step ran cas llmLogMySess; - NOTE: The session LLMLOGMYSESS connected successfully to Cloud Analytic Services ..., NOTE: The SAS option SESSREF was updated with the value LLMLOGMYSESS. -, wrote the table and ended the session: NOTE: Deletion of the session LLMLOGMYSESS was successful., the NOTE about the option SESSREF= quoted above, and NOTE: Request to TERMINATE completed for session LLMLOGMYSESS. Promoted and saved, the table was read from a new CAS session, global, with the 174 rows. Saved and not promoted, no table was in memory and the .sashdat held the 174 rows. Neither promoted nor saved, nothing was left. SYSCC was 0 and the jobs ended as completed. The custom step without the libref. Behind cas mysess; alone the step ran in that session, started none of its own and wrote the promoted and saved table to CASUSER, with the same 174 rows. The log of that job held the line _FLW_ACTION_TABLE_|CASUSER|<table>|0; with the libref it was |1. The step twice in one SAS session. The code SAS Studio generated for two flows of the step, one behind the other in one SAS Job Execution job whose session had no CAS session: the first run started LLMLOGMYSESS and ended it. Between the runs _CASNAME_ existed, the option SESSREF named LLMLOGMYSESS and cas _all_ list; listed nothing. The second run started no session: ERROR: There is no server connection to execute the action 'session.sessionId'., ERROR: Unhandled Python exception., ERROR: The log could not be parsed, the table CASUSER.<table> was left as it is., SYSCC 1012, no table, and a job that ended as failed. This is what the session check was changed for: the step now asks SESSFOUND, and the same job was run again with that check (below). The step put on the server in place. PUT /dataFlows/steps/{id} with the step file plus its id was answered 200 and the id was kept; the stored program and the texts of the About tab equalled the file. The copy from SAS Content, as it is printed in this guide - see Without a Shared Mount: the copy with the size and the digest of the upload, and the 174 rows from Log-Parser-Code.sas behind it. A log file that is missing, in replace mode: the ERROR described under Reading the Job Log, no table, no <table>_NEW and no saved file. No table of that name existed before the run, so that an existing table is left as it is was not seen there. The runs from The custom step in a session without a CAS session on were made later on 2026-10-11, with the step and with Log-Parser-Code.sas as they were at that time of the day: their session check went by the macro variable _CASNAME_. Every run of Log-Parser-Code.sas in the list above was made before that line was changed as well; the program holds the same check behind its own cas mysess;.

After the check was changed, the step was put on the server again - POST /dataFlows/steps, then PUT /dataFlows/steps/{id}, answered 200 with the id kept, the stored program and ui equal to the file - and run the same day in seven more SAS Job Execution jobs of the SAS Studio compute context, as the code SAS Studio generated for flows of the step, with the 174 requests of the first collection. It was the step as it was at that point of the release: version 2.1, with the twelve columns. SESSFOUND on that system. No log of the seven jobs held an ERROR or a WARNING at a line that calls the function. It returned 0 in a session without a CAS session, where the option SESSREF named CASAUTO; 0 for a session that had been ended (LLMLOGMYSESS, MYSESS); and 1 for a connected MYSESS. Twice and three times in one SAS session without a CAS session. In a job with two flows of the step one behind the other, both runs started and ended LLMLOGMYSESS, with two session ids. Between the runs the option SESSREF named LLMLOGMYSESS, SESSFOUND returned 0, _CASNAME_ existed and cas _all_ list; wrote no line. The second run wrote, promoted and saved its table, and none of the lines of the failed second run described above occurred. In a job with three runs the third did the same and replaced the global table of the second. A CAS session of the user, used and left alone. Behind cas mysess;, the libref and a session table of the user, the step ran in MYSESS: outside the echoed source no line of the log named LLMLOGMYSESS, and no Deletion of the session and no Request to TERMINATE line was written before the job read the table back. After the step the session had the same id, SESSFOUND returned 1 for it, cas mysess list; named MYSESS as ACTIVE and the session table of the user was still there. The same held after the step had run twice behind that session. A session that was ended before the step. Behind cas mysess; cas mysess terminate; the option SESSREF named MYSESS and SESSFOUND returned 0: the step started LLMLOGMYSESS, wrote and saved its table and ended LLMLOGMYSESS. A CAS session without the libref. The step used MYSESS, wrote the promoted and saved table and left the session active. Log-Parser-Code.sas with the same check, three of its %let lines changed: the program ran in the mysess it starts itself, no line outside the source named LLMLOGMYSESS, and it wrote the 174 rows. All seven jobs ended as completed with SYSCC 0 and without a line of the type error or warning from source line 1 on. Each of the seven tables, read from a new CAS session, was global and had the 174 rows and the twelve columns, the rows equal to those of the earlier runs. _FLW_ACTION_TABLE_. The line ended in |0 in every run in which the step ran in a session of its own or without the libref - four of the jobs - although the table existed, and in |1 in the two jobs with the libref. An observation, not caused by the check. After the step, or Log-Parser-Code.sas, had run in a CAS session of the user, the action session.sessionId returned that session under the name py-session-1 where it had returned MYSESS before, with the same id. SAS went on listing the session as MYSESS, ACTIVE, and SESSFOUND returned 1 for mysess. The Python part of the program is the one of the runs before the check changed; whether the step of those runs did the same was not looked at. The step and the program of this release hold that check line unchanged. What this release changes beside it is not part of these runs: for version 2.2 of the step, with the 24 further columns, see The parser of this release on SAS Viya.

The redaction of the Authorization and X-CSRF-TOKEN headers: none occurred in the logs, so only the API_KEY and the Cookie expression were exercised. The shared mount of the example paths and the hourly crontab entry. The models that had no request in the collected day. The rows come from three LLMs - one of them, with a single row, is called with a provider key -, one embedding model and one decision model. No embedding model that is called with a provider key had a request, and a second decision model has failed requests only. The error branches: an append whose saved .sashdat can not be loaded, a replace that can not build the <table>_NEW table, and a log file that is missing while the output table exists. Append without promoting, a saved table whose name differs from the table name in upper and lower case, and a target caslib other than CASUSER - nothing was written to Public. The step clicked in the SAS Studio UI, and how SAS Studio shows its About tab: the step was run as the code SAS Studio generates for a flow, in SAS Job Execution jobs. Whether an interactive SAS Studio session of the test system starts without a CAS session was not looked at either. The step's own session in append mode, a CAS session of the user in append mode, and a run without the libref where the name of the libref is not the name of a caslib. The condition code SAS Job Execution keeps for a job: the job API returned none for the seven jobs of the session check, their SYSCC of 0 was written by the jobs themselves. A log with bytes that are not valid UTF-8, and two requests that overlap in one container. Both are covered by the tests of the repository, which run the parser's Python outside of SAS. Of the parser with the 36 columns: the output port of the step on the flow canvas of SAS Studio and its About tab as SAS Studio shows it - the stored step, its 36 column controls and the generated code were looked at -, the default table names - the runs of 2026-10-11 wrote to CASUSER, and on 2026-10-12 one chain wrote to Public under names of its own -, a collected log with requests that ran at the same time, and the LLM Usage Report opened on a table of this release: the twelve columns it reads of LLM_LOGS were compared with the report package and are all there. The package joins LLM_LOGS with LLM_FACT_SHEET; whether the new column model_id of LLM_LOGS touches that join was not looked at. What the three programs do since the chain ran a second time on 2026-10-12: version 2.4 of the LLM - Log Parser step, version 2.2 of the LLM - Get All Prompts step and Link-Logs-To-Models.sas as they are now. The Chain on SAS Viya lists what was changed after each run.

SAS-Viya-Integrations/Logging-Monitoring/Get-All-Prompts.sas reads what the Prompt Builder keeps in SAS Model Manager and writes it into five CAS tables. Every row of every table carries modelID and projectID, the SAS Model Manager ids of the model and of its project - the model being the prompt template, the decision template or the RAG setup itself, where its trackers and its manifested score code are stored. The LLM - Get All Prompts custom step runs the same program. The program ran on the test system on 2026-10-11 as it was that day - version 2.0 of the step - and on 2026-10-12 with what that run had led to - version 2.1 of the step: the refusal of a table name that no libref can address, the runs taken from a ledger, the further columns and roles of the catalog, the setup without a collection and the session check of the code file. See The Pull on SAS Viya. What was changed after the second run - version 2.2 of the step: the condition code of a run that wrote an ERROR line, the function its messages go through, the counter of an optimizationId that a tracker holds twice - ran there later that day (the third run). Version 2.3 of the step - the counter that passes over the id of another entry - and the settings the code file takes only where they are not set are not run in SAS. The Python of the program runs in the test suite of the repository against a made-up SAS Model Manager, and the SAS code around it is held by the tests as text.

The projects with the tag Prompt-Engineering - projects of decision templates carry that tag as well. Of every model: Prompt-Experiment-Tracker.json, Prompt-Optimization-Tracker.json and the manifested score code (the .py file with the role score). The projects with the tag RAG-Engineering. A setup saved by the Prompt Builder is read from its rag-setup.json. A model registered by the step RAG - Register Setup (named RAG Retrieval - <setup>) has no such file: it is read from the pipeline.yaml the step stores with it, from its properties collection, pipelineVersion, configuration and ingestionRunId, and from its training table, which the step sets to <CAS server>/<caslib>/<prefix>_LEDGER. Any other model of such a project is left out with a NOTE. The projects that hold the definitions of the models that answer a request. The Prompt Builder finds them by id (its options llmProjectID and embeddingProjectID) and the decision models by the project name Decision Model Project; the program finds all three by name - LLM Model Project, Embedding Model Project, Decision Model Project, the names mdb setup gives them - so that it needs no id. Nothing is written to SAS Model Manager, and every listing is read to its last page.

The program takes each of these settings where its macro variable is not set when it starts (Settings that stay yours). In the custom step the output table gives the CAS library and the table of the experiments, and the others are fields of the step. Macro variable Default Meaning _gap_tag Prompt-Engineering Tag of the projects with prompt templates and decision templates _gap_rag_tag RAG-Engineering Tag of the projects with RAG setups; empty reads none (in the step an empty field takes the default) _gap_llm_project LLM Model Project Project of the LLM definitions: a name, a project id or tag:<tag>, several separated by |; empty leaves the LLMs out of the catalog _gap_embedding_project Embedding Model Project The same for the embedding models _gap_decision_project Decision Model Project The same for the decision models _gap_out_caslib Public CAS library of all five tables _gap_out_experiments PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS Table names, one per output _gap_out_optimizations PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS _gap_out_rag_setups RAG_SETUPS _gap_out_rag_runs RAG_RUNS _gap_out_catalog MODEL_CATALOG Two outputs can not have the same name, and an output needs a name: the program says so and reads nothing. The five table names are SAS names of 32 characters at most - letters, digits and underscores, no digit in front. CAS takes a longer name, but no CAS libref can address such a table: the program ends with one ERROR line before it reads SAS Model Manager. The program needs PROC PYTHON with the package requests. Get-All-Prompts.sas runs in the CAS session the option SESSREF names when that session is connected, and otherwise in a connected session mySess, to which it sets the option; only where neither is connected does it start one (cas mySess;), and it ends only a session it started. The step does the same with a session called gapMySess.

Each table is dropped, loaded, promoted and saved, as PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS was. A table without rows is written as well, with all its columns: the DATA step that builds it declares the columns and reads nothing. A long text column is as wide as its longest value, at most 32,767 bytes; a longer text is cut between two characters. Table One row per Key PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS experiment run and model that answered, of a prompt template or decision template; one row without a run for a model that has none modelID, runID, model PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS entry of a Prompt-Optimization-Tracker.json: an optimization or a comparison of target models modelID, optimizationId RAG_SETUPS RAG setup, saved by the Prompt Builder or registered by the step RAG - Register Setup modelID RAG_RUNS ingestion run of a setup: the rows of its run table when that is in memory, otherwise the runs its ledger still names modelID, run_id MODEL_CATALOG model and pattern modelID, role, runID, optimization_id, target_model PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS. The 49 columns the table had, unchanged in name, order and type: unique_id (the row number, no key), name, description, createdBy, modifiedBy, function, runID, model, systemPrompt, userPrompt (the templates; for a decision run the questions and the state template), response, run_time, prompt_length, output_length, cost, cheapest_prompt, best_prompt, fastest_prompt, fewest_tokens_prompt, judge_rank, judge_best, judge_cost, judge_model, judge_confidence, judge_mode, judge_panel, judge_agreement, judge_chairman_model, variables_count, integrated_llm_call, output_variables_count, creationTime, modifiedTime, temperature, top_p, top_k, max_tokens, thinking_budget, max_completion_tokens, seed, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, dimensions, api_key_required, reasoning_effort, input_type, normalize, projectLink, modelLink. Behind them: modelID, projectID, projectName, kind (prompt or decision), expected (the expected answers of a decision run, JSON), options (as stored; the value of an option that is a secret by its name, by the names the log parser goes by, is replaced by REDACTED), variables (JSON), resolved_system_prompt, resolved_user_prompt (the prompts as they were sent), resolved_system_hash, resolved_user_hash, judge_reasoning (at most 2,000 bytes). runID is a number. PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS. modelID, projectID, projectName, name, optimizationId, startedAt, finishedAt (SAS datetimes, UTC), status, targetModel, optimizer, metric, judgeModel, datasetSource, datasetRef, sampleCount, trainSize, validationSize, metricBefore, metricAfter, targetCalls, targetPromptTokens, targetOutputTokens, targetRunTime, judgeCalls, judgePromptTokens, judgeOutputTokens, judgeRunTime, error, type (comparison for a comparison of target models, else empty), skippedReason, jobId, computeContext. The prompts, the few-shot examples and the evaluations of an optimization stay in the tracker. RAG_SETUPS. modelID, projectID, projectName, name, description, creationTime, modifiedTime, source (builder or step), collection, backend, embedding_model, embedding_dims, chunker, input_token_limit, overlap_tokens, tables_prefix, tables_caslib, source_path, pipeline_version, artifacts_folder, job_definition_uri (both only for a setup of the Builder), ingestion_run_id, configuration (both only for a model of the step), runs_table (<tables_prefix>_RUNS), createdBy, modifiedBy. A setup that was saved in the Builder and registered with the step is two models and two rows with the same collection. RAG_RUNS. The rows of every setup's run table <tables_caslib>.<tables_prefix>_RUNS, stacked (run_source = run table). Both ingestion paths publish that table: the step RAG - Load Vector Store, and since release 2.3.0 the ingestion job of a setup of the Prompt Builder (Ingest-Documents.sas), which names it by its ledger table without the ending _LEDGER - the table prefix of the setup. Only a table that is in memory is read, and no table of a setup is loaded or changed. Columns: modelID, projectID, then the columns rag_core writes - as text run_id, rag_project, collection, backend, started_at, finished_at, status, pipeline_version, config_id, embed_model, chunker, enrich_model, error_text; as numbers embed_dims, input_token_limit, overlap_tokens, docs_new, docs_changed, docs_unchanged, docs_deleted, docs_skipped, docs_excluded, docs_failed, docs_ingested, chunks_written, chunks_retired, collection_chunks, embed_calls, embed_tokens, embed_seconds, enrich_calls, enrich_input_tokens, enrich_output_tokens, enrich_seconds, enrich_failed - then source_caslib, source_table and run_source: 40 columns. A column a run table of an earlier release lacks is empty, a count that was published as text is a number here, and started_at and finished_at are the text the run table holds (UTC; on the test system YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS+00:00). Only the runs of the setup's own collection are taken. A run table two setups share gives its rows once per setup. A setup that the job ingested before has no run table until its job definition holds the program that publishes it - Manifest setup writes the program of the release into the job definition - and the job ran once with the run history switched on. That run publishes every run the vector store holds for the collection (the newest 500), so after the next pull, and a link with _lnk_redo_all = 1, the document embeddings of its earlier ingestions can be given to their runs, as far as the store recorded those runs. The publication by the job was measured on 2026-10-12 with a setup of its own, and the pull and the link on its run table - see the third run. Outside of SAS, the file the job writes for the table gives the same rows of RAG_RUNS as the table the step stages - by a reading of the two macros that stack the tables, which no test runs. For a setup whose run table is not in memory - its job definition holds the program from before, or its run history is switched off - the pull writes the runs that the ledger <tables_prefix>_LEDGER still names, if that table is in memory (run_source = ledger): one row per run id, started_at the second the id of the run holds (run-<seconds since 1970>-<digits>), finished_at the latest updated_at of its rows, collection and embed_model those of the setup, source_table the ledger, and every count missing. Every run writes its id into the row of every document of the folder, so a ledger names the newest run only. The ledger is read only where the run table is not in memory, so a run that both name is one row. A setup with neither table in memory is left out with a NOTE. The rows taken from a ledger ran on the test system on 2026-10-12, see The Pull on SAS Viya. MODEL_CATALOG. modelID, projectID, projectName, name, role, runID (text), target_model, system_template, user_template, resolved_system_prompt, resolved_user_prompt, collection, template_source, resolved_system_hash, resolved_user_hash, and behind these fifteen the six that were added after the run of 2026-10-11: run_time, prompt_length, output_length (numbers), window_start, window_end (text, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ in UTC) and optimization_id (text). The link program reads every column but projectName, prompt_length and output_length. role Rows What the row holds prompt, decision one per template (runID empty) The templates with their {{variables}}; for a decision template the questions and the state template. template_source says where they are from: score code (what the manifested score code sends, with the model it calls in target_model), best run (the newest run marked as the best prompt) or newest run. A model without a run and without such score code has no row prompt, decision one per experiment run and model (runID set) The templates of the run, the prompts as they were sent, their hashes, the model they were sent to, and what the tracker holds of that call: run_time in seconds, prompt_length and output_length in tokens. The run time is what tells the request of this run from another request with the same prompts rag one per RAG setup that names a collection collection, the embedding model in target_model, and in template_source who wrote the model: builder or step. A setup without a collection - its properties or its setup file could not be read - keeps its row of RAG_SETUPS and has none here, as no request could be linked to it judge one per run that was judged and model that judged it modelID, projectID and name are the prompt's, runID the run, target_model the judge - the judge, each member of a panel, the chairman. resolved_system_prompt and resolved_user_prompt are the prompts of the run as they were sent, which the Prompt Builder shows a judge in the user prompt of its call. No run time and no window: the tracker holds none for the call of a judge optimization one per entry of the optimization tracker and model it called runID is empty and optimization_id the id of the entry; target_model is a target model or the judge of the optimization. window_start and window_end are the start and the end of the job, the start rounded down and the end up to the second, empty where the tracker has none. resolved_system_prompt is the system prompt the optimization started from, as it is stored, and the two templates are the optimized prompt where the tracker holds one. An optimizationId that a tracker holds on more than one entry is counted, so that no two rows of the catalog have one key: the rows of the second entry carry it as <id>#2, of the third as <id>#3, and a WARNING names the model. PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS holds such entries as the tracker has them, so its key (modelID, optimizationId) is not unique for that model. Measured on 2026-10-12 in the third run with a copy of a tracker that held its entry twice under the id 1: the catalog rows 1 and 1#2, a key that was unique, and two rows with the id 1 in PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS. Since version 2.3 of the step a counter that would make the id of another entry is passed over - the ids 1, 1 and 1#2 give 1, 1#3 and 1#2 -, an id longer than the 16 bytes of the column makes room for its counter, and an entry without an id carries the counter alone (#2); that is not run in SAS llm, embedding, decision_model one per model definition name is the name of the container, which is the model a log row names

The Prompt Builder stores the templates and the variables of a run and sends the prompts with the values filled in. The program fills them in the same way: the variables one after the other in the order they are stored, {{name}} with blanks or line ends inside the braces, the value as it is - not trimmed, whatever the type of the variable - and a {{name}} of no variable left as typed. A decision run sends its questions as they are stored and gets the variables filled into its state only. The hash is the one of the log table, taken of the whole text before it is cut to the length of its column. The templates of a manifested model are read from its score code, which is parsed and never run. A manifested model strips every value before it puts it into the prompt, the Prompt Builder does not. Measured outside of SAS on files saved from the test system: the templates were read from nine manifested score codes, one of them a decision template manifested with 2.2.0 whose score code does not compile and is read statement by statement; the questions and the state template read from the score code of one decision template fit 41 of the 105 requests to its decision model in the collected log of 1040 requests, and the questions of its tracker equalled the questions of those requests character by character. Not compared: a prompt as an experiment run sent it with a logged request.
documents.s: The Prompts as They Were Sent

documents.t: A model whose file can not be read (not JSON, a failed request), and a project or model that can not be listed, is a WARNING with its name; the model keeps its row without runs and the pull goes on. When the projects themselves can not be listed, the program ends with an ERROR and leaves the output tables as they are. A definition project that is not found is a WARNING; an empty setting asks for nothing. The run ends with one NOTE per output table: <caslib>.<table> was written with <n> rows and <m> columns. A run table whose name is no SAS name of at most 32 characters, or whose caslib holds a quote, &, % or ;, is left out with a WARNING. An output table name of more than 32 characters, or one that is no SAS name: ERROR: The table name <name> of the output <output> has <n> characters. A SAS libref addresses a CAS table by a name of 32 characters at most, nothing was read or written., or ... is no SAS name: letters, digits and underscores, and no digit in front. Nothing was read or written. Nothing is read and no table is touched. A RAG setup without a collection: WARNING: The properties of the model <name> (<id>) could not be read: <reason>. The setup has no collection without them and is left out of the model catalog, where no request could be linked to it. Its row of the RAG setups stays., or WARNING: The RAG setup <name> (<id>) names no collection and is left out of the model catalog, ... A setup whose runs are taken from its ledger: NOTE: The run table <caslib>.<prefix>_RUNS is not in memory. <n> run(s) were taken from the ledger <caslib>.<prefix>_LEDGER - the runs its rows still name, each from the start its id holds to the latest of its rows. A setup whose CAS library is not available in the session is left out, and so is a setup where CAS refused the question for its run table, the question for its ledger where the run table is not in memory, or - for a CAS library other than CASUSER - the listing of the CAS libraries, and a setup whose PROC CAS step halted before it set what it found: NOTE: The CAS library <caslib> of the run table <table> is not available in this session, or CAS did not say whether it, the table or its ledger table is there, so its runs are not in <RAG_RUNS>. The setup has no rows in RAG_RUNS. Measured in the eighth pass, late on 2026-10-14, with a CAS session that had ended: up to version 2.5 a halted step wrote NOTE: The run table <caslib>.<table> is not in memory, its runs are not in <RAG_RUNS>., also for a run table of 5 rows in memory (The Pass of 2026-10-14). The halt as version 2.6 handles it ran in the ninth pass, on 2026-10-15: the program and the step wrote the NOTE above for each run table whose step halted, and their five tables. A refusal as version 2.6 handles it is not run in SAS. An optimizationId that a tracker holds on more than one entry: WARNING: The file Prompt-Optimization-Tracker.json of the model <name> (<id>) holds the optimizationId <ids> on more than one entry. In the model catalog the rows of a later such entry carry the id with a counter, as in 1#2 - for an entry without an id the counter alone -, so that no two rows of the catalog have the same key. The table of the optimizations holds the entries as the tracker has them. Where entries without an optimizationId repeat, the message says ... holds <n> entries without an optimizationId. in that place, or both joined by and. The WARNING of version 2.2 of the step was seen on 2026-10-12 in the third run; its wording as it is here, of version 2.3, is not run in SAS. In the step, an output table that is no CAS table: ERROR: The selected output library does not point to a CASlib, nothing was read or written. - one line, where the step ended with an ABORT statement up to version 2.1. Not run in SAS. A run that wrote an ERROR line and left an output table unwritten sets the condition code of the SAS session (SYSCC) to 1012 as its last statement in front of the macro variables it deletes: a table name that is refused, projects that could not be listed or another reason for which SAS Model Manager could not be read, a table that was not written, and in the step an output library that is no CAS library. A WARNING - a model that could not be read, a setup that is left out - leaves the condition code as it was. Measured on 2026-10-12 in the third run: the refusal of a table name of 34 characters ended with SYSCC 1012 and a failed job. And the step in the code SAS Studio generates for a flow, with its output table in WORK: ERROR: The selected output library does not point to a CASlib, nothing was read or written., no ABORT line, no request to SAS Model Manager, SYSCC 1012 and a failed job. The first DATA step behind the step is the flow's own %_flw_action_end; it wrote NOTE: Due to ERROR(s) above, SAS set option OBS=0, enabling syntax check mode. and did not run, so the log held _FLW_ACTION_START_ and neither _FLW_ACTION_TABLE_ nor _FLW_ACTION_END_ for the node, and obs was 0 behind the flow code. A refusal behaves like any SAS error: later DATA steps of the session do not run until SYSCC is reset. What SAS Studio shows for such a node was not looked at. A table name that is refused still gives two ERROR lines: its own, and the line that says that the experiments could not be read, which is the line that ends such a run. Every message the Python writes is made one text before it is handed to SAS, by the function the parser and the link program carry: in a name from SAS Model Manager a quote shows as a backtick, % as pct, & as +, a semicolon as a comma, a comment mark is split by a blank, a tab or a line break is a blank, and parentheses that do not pair up show as brackets - then the ones around the id of the model as well. Up to version 2.1 of the step the function let comment marks, tabs and a parenthesis without its partner through. Measured on 2026-10-12 in the third run with models named /* open (x) setup, /* open setup and a name with quotes, a semicolon, a percent sign and %put: the WARNINGs arrived whole - / * open (x) setup (<id>), with the parentheses that pair up left as they are, and `q` `d` , 50pct pct put x, setup (<id>) -, the closing NOTEs followed, SYSCC was 0 and RAG_SETUPS held the names unchanged. SAS Model Manager refused a model name with a parenthesis without its partner (HTTP 400), so that such a parenthesis shows as a bracket was not measured. The requests are made one after the other: one per project and one or more per model.
