documents.t: Measured on the test system on 2026-10-11 with Get-All-Prompts.sas as it was that day (version 2.0 of the step), in SAS Job Execution jobs that wrote to tables of their own in CASUSER. Where a point goes on with On 2026-10-12, the program was changed after the run, and the changed program - version 2.1 of the step - ran on the test system that day. Where it ends in Since then, the program was changed once more - version 2.2 of the step -, and that change ran in the third run later that day. What it read. 41 projects with the tag Prompt-Engineering and 92 models in them, 10 projects with the tag RAG-Engineering and 17 RAG setups, in 17 to 20 seconds per run - the Python step 16.6 of the 19.5 seconds of the first. The five tables. PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS with 318 rows and 61 columns, PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS with 27 and 32, RAG_SETUPS with 17 and 26, RAG_RUNS with 105 and 39 and MODEL_CATALOG with 365 and 15, each promoted and saved. The keys were unique: 318 of 318 rows of the experiments and 365 of 365 of the catalog. The JSON libname with its map, the loop over the CAS libraries and the look at each written table through the libref ran as they are written. On 2026-10-12: PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS with 318 rows and 61 columns, PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS with 27 and 32, RAG_SETUPS with 17 and 26, RAG_RUNS with 107 and 40 and MODEL_CATALOG with 421 and 21, in 18.6 seconds (the job 34). All four keys were unique: 318 of 318, 27 of 27, 107 of 107, and 421 of 421 rows of the catalog - 392 without optimization_id in the key. The catalog held 285 prompt, 47 decision, 24 judge, 35 optimization, 14 rag, 8 llm, 3 embedding and 5 decision_model rows, and run_time, prompt_length and output_length were numbers in CAS. Three runs with one content. The program alone, the program behind the parser in one SAS session, and the step (version 2.0) as the code SAS Studio generated for a flow wrote the same five tables - compared by the ids, counts, lengths and hashes of every row, not by the texts. On 2026-10-12: the step (version 2.1) as the code SAS Studio generated for a flow wrote the five tables of the program of that day, with the same columns in name, order, type, length and label and the same ids, counts, lengths and hashes in every row, and the same three WARNINGs, in 16.1 seconds. A decision template, a prompt template and a RAG setup of the test system, looked at row by row. The decision template had 41 rows of 21 runs with two decision models and kind = decision, and in the catalog its template (score code) and 41 run rows with both hashes. The prompt template had 32 rows of 14 runs with four LLMs and one optimization, and in the catalog its template and 32 run rows. The setup had source = builder with its collection, vector database, embedding model and table prefix, and in the catalog one rag row marked builder. The catalog held 8 llm, 3 embedding and 5 decision_model rows. On 2026-10-12, in the catalog with its further columns and roles: the prompt template with 32 run rows, each with a run_time; 13 judge rows for its runs 2 to 14, with the judge in target_model and without a run time; and one optimization row with the model the optimization called, the id 1, the window 2026-10-11T17:34:10Z to 2026-10-11T17:35:11Z and the system prompt it started from, 817 characters. The decision template had its template row and 41 run rows. The columns the LLM Usage Report reads - 38 of PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS, read from the report package - were all in the table under their names. The report was not opened on it. A table name of 34 characters. For an output with such a name the last line of the run was ERROR: The table <caslib>.<name> was not written. - for a table that had been written, promoted and saved with its 27 rows and 32 columns. The closing check looks at the table through a CAS libref, and the exist function returned 0 for the name of 34 characters and 1 for one of 32. On 2026-10-12: a name of more than 32 characters, or one that is no SAS name, ends the program before anything is read. With a name of 34 characters for the optimizations the run wrote ERROR: The table name <name> of the output optimizations has 34 characters. A SAS libref addresses a CAS table by a name of 32 characters at most, nothing was read or written. and then ERROR: The experiments could not be read from SAS Model Manager, the output tables in <caslib> were left as they are., in 3.6 seconds, and no table of that job existed afterwards. SYSCC was 0 and the job ended as completed. Since then a run that wrote an ERROR line and left an output table unwritten sets SYSCC to 1012, see Messages and Limits of the Pull. A model whose properties the service does not return. GET /modelRepository/models/<id> of one model registered by the step was answered with HTTP 500, by the program and outside of it. The program wrote one WARNING and kept the setup, with an empty collection and embedding model, in RAG_SETUPS and in the catalog. On 2026-10-12: such a setup keeps its row of RAG_SETUPS and is left out of the catalog, and the WARNING says so. Each of the six runs that read SAS Model Manager that day wrote three such WARNINGs - for that model, which the service still answered with HTTP 500 (... The setup has no collection without them and is left out of the model catalog, ... Its row of the RAG setups stays.), and for two setups that name no collection (... names no collection and is left out of the model catalog, ...). RAG_SETUPS had its 17 rows, and the catalog 14 rag rows where there had been 17, none of them without a collection. The run table of the Builder's setup does not exist. The pull wrote NOTE: The run table Public.<prefix>_RUNS is not in memory, .... The caslib held the ledger of the setup (<prefix>_LEDGER, 7 rows, and its .sashdat) and no run table, in memory or as a file. The 105 rows of RAG_RUNS came from four run tables of setups that the step path had ingested; three of those tables are shared by two or three models the step registered and are in RAG_RUNS once per model. 15 of the 105 rows hold a finished_at about two hours before their started_at. On 2026-10-12: for a setup without a run table in memory the pull writes the runs its ledger still names. For that setup it wrote NOTE: The run table Public.<prefix>_RUNS is not in memory. 1 run(s) were taken from the ledger Public.<prefix>_LEDGER - the runs its rows still name, each from the start its id holds to the latest of its rows. The row had the run id of the ledger, started_at 2026-10-11 17:49:41, finished_at 2026-10-11 17:49:47, the collection and the embedding model of the setup, run_source ledger, and no counts and no status. A second setup gave one row from its ledger as well: 2 of the 107 rows of RAG_RUNS were from ledgers and 105 from the four run tables. The ledger was unchanged - 7 rows, the same modified time, the same file -, and the steps that read it wrote no note about a variable that is not initialized or a value that was converted. Since then the ingestion job publishes the run table of its setup, see RAG_RUNS above; in the third run the pull read four runs of a setup from the table its job had published. Behind the parser in one SAS session the cas mySess; of the program wrote WARNING: A session with the name MYSESS already exists. - SAS Job Execution keeps such a warning in the record of a job: another job of that day with the same warning ended as completed and carried the error code 5710 with that message -, and the program ended the session the parser had started and its librefs were bound to. On 2026-10-12: both code files ask SESSFOUND before they start a session, and Get-All-Prompts.sas ends only a session it started. Alone in a fresh SAS session the program started MYSESS and ended it. In one job with the parser, the pull, the parser, the pull and the link twice, no line said already exists, the session and the librefs public and casuser were there after every program, and both pulls wrote their five tables with the row counts above. Behind a CAS session of the user no program started one of its own. Not measured: an output without rows - every output had rows -, a pull that takes longer than two minutes (51 projects and 109 models took 17 to 20 seconds), the default table names - on 2026-10-12 one pull wrote its five tables to Public under names of its own, with the same rows and columns -, the step run from its page in SAS Studio, and of the runs taken from a ledger a ledger without the columns run_id and updated_at and a CAS library that is not available. What the program does since the third run - version 2.3 of the step, and the settings it takes only where they are not set - is not run in SAS.

SAS-Viya-Integrations/Logging-Monitoring/Link-Logs-To-Models.sas fills the nine link columns of the log table. It reads the log table, MODEL_CATALOG and, when it is there, RAG_RUNS, links the rows without a match_method and, where it linked a row, puts the table back, promoted and saved. A run that links no row leaves the table as it is. The program ran on the test system on 2026-10-11 and on 2026-10-12, each time as it was that day, see The Chain on SAS Viya. The first run linked the 1040 rows of the collected log, and its summary broke the SAS log. The program was changed - its messages, the rule for an experiment run, the window of a retrieval query, the calls of optimizations and judges, what it does to a table it links no row of -, and the second run measured the rules as this section has them. What was changed after the second run - the condition code of a run that wrote an ERROR line and no table, and what the program does with a log table that it loaded from its saved file and linked no row of - ran in the third run later that day. The link program has no custom step. The parser and the link program must not run on one table at the same time. Since the third run the program takes its settings only where they are not set (Settings that stay yours), which is not run in SAS.
documents.s: Linking the Log to the Models

documents.t: Macro variable Default Meaning _lnk_log_caslib, _lnk_log_table Public, LLM_LOGS The log table. Its link columns are filled in place _lnk_catalog_caslib, _lnk_catalog_table Public, MODEL_CATALOG The catalog of Get-All-Prompts.sas _lnk_runs_caslib, _lnk_runs_table Public, RAG_RUNS The ingestion runs. Without the table no embedding row is linked to an ingestion run; the program says so in a NOTE _lnk_redo_all 0 0 links the rows without a match_method and leaves every other row as it is. 1 links all rows again _lnk_min_literal 20 The characters of fixed text (whitespace not counted) a template needs to take part, an experiment run in its prompts, and a call of an optimization or of a judge in the texts the catalog holds of it _lnk_utc_offset 0 The hours the clock of the containers is ahead of UTC. The ingestion runs and the windows of the optimizations are recorded in UTC _lnk_query_window 300 The seconds within which the prompt that carries a retrieval follows the embedding of its query. A query embedding without such a prompt is not linked _lnk_promote_table, _lnk_save_table 1, 1 They decide for a table that is not promoted and for one that has no saved file. A table that is promoted is promoted again and a table that has a saved file is saved again, whatever the two say - as the parser does it when it appends A table that was saved but is not in memory (after a restart of the CAS server) is loaded from its .sashdat file first; this holds for all three tables. A log table that was loaded and of which the run then links no row is promoted as _lnk_promote_table says, and its saved file is left as it is (see What the Program Does to the Table); the catalog and the runs table that were loaded stay tables of the session of the program. The program needs PROC PYTHON with the pandas and swat packages and the caslib CASUSER, as the parser does. A setting that has to be a number and is none gives a WARNING, and its default is taken. The program runs in the CAS session the option SESSREF names when that session is connected, and otherwise in a connected session lnkMySess, to which it sets the option; only where neither is connected does it start one (cas lnkMySess;), and it ends only that one.

No request, header or log line names the caller. Every link is therefore made by content, and match_method says which rule decided. The model that answered (model_id): the catalog row with the role llm, embedding or decision_model whose name is the name of the container (model). When two models of that role have the name, model_id stays empty and a NOTE names the two. experiment run (LLM and decision rows): the system and the user prompt of the row are the prompts of an experiment run as the Builder sent them (for a decision: the questions and the state), the run was sent to the model of the row, the request was not sent by the score code or a SAS session (user_agent is not python-requests or SAS) - the Builder page sends its runs from a browser -, and the runtime of the row is the run_time the catalog holds for that run and model, compared with three decimals. The prompts are compared by the hashes the catalog holds of them, so a prompt that is longer than a column of the catalog is still found. A run is given to one row: the earliest request gets it, and a run that a row of an earlier link holds is taken. A request with the prompts of a run whose run time is the one of no run is another request with the same prompts: the rules below say who sent it, and it gets no experiment_run_id. Where the catalog holds no run_time for the runs with these prompts - a catalog written before the column existed -, the row gets the newest of them, match_candidates is their number, and a NOTE counts such rows. questions and state, questions (decision rows): the questions of the row are the questions of a decision template. Questions are compared as JSON, so the order of the keys and the whitespace do not matter; a text that is no JSON is compared as text. When the state of the row fits a state template that has fixed text, the method is questions and state, otherwise questions. template (LLM rows): the system prompt and the user prompt of the row fit the templates of a prompt. Every {{variable}} stands for any text, also for none and for several lines; the fixed text has to be there in its order, from the first character to the last, whitespace squeezed. The templates of earlier experiment runs of a prompt count as its templates. optimization, then judge (LLM rows): the request is a call the Prompt Builder made for a prompt and not with it - a call of a prompt optimization, or the call a judge gets to rank the answers of a run. A catalog row of that role links a request when three things hold: the request holds every text of the row (resolved_system_prompt, resolved_user_prompt) in its system or in its user prompt, at least one of them as a part of the prompt and not as the whole of it; it went to the model in target_model; and, where the row has window_start and window_end, it was sent inside that window (whole seconds, _lnk_utc_offset applies). The texts need _lnk_min_literal characters together. caller_model_id is the prompt the call was made for and caller_kind what the catalog says that caller is. A judge call gets the experiment_run_id of the run that was judged when exactly one run remains; two judged runs with the same prompts leave it empty. An optimization is asked first: a call of a judge that was made while an optimization of the same prompt was running, to a model that optimization called and with the system prompt it started from, is an optimization row. The RAG setup of a prompt (LLM rows, column rag_model_id, does not change match_method): the prompt carries the results of a retrieval, and the setup is the one the catalog has for its collection. So a call of a prompt that is fed by a retrieval is linked to its prompt and to the setup. Of several retrievals in one prompt the last one counts, as for the parser. retrieval query (embedding rows in query mode): the hash of the embedded text is the hash of the query of a retrieval that an LLM row of the table carries, and that LLM row follows the embedding within _lnk_query_window seconds. The nearest such row decides: the embedding row gets the setup of the collection it names. The same question is embedded many times and for more than one collection, so a prompt that came before the embedding, or long after it, says nothing about this request. Two prompts of two collections in the same second are ambiguous. A setup of which the catalog names another embedding model than the model of the row is not taken. ingestion run (embedding rows in document mode whose project input is rag, as the RAG runtime sends it, or empty): the request lies between started_at and finished_at of exactly one run of RAG_RUNS whose embed_model is the model of the row. A run without a start or an end, or whose end lies before its start, takes no part, and a NOTE counts such runs. Between several callers that fit, the one with the most fixed text wins and match_candidates is their number. A caller of which the catalog only names other target models is taken when no other caller fits. Two callers with the same amount of fixed text, two collections for one query or two overlapping ingestion runs give match_method = ambiguous and empty caller columns. A row that fits nothing gets none and match_candidates = 0; its model_id is filled all the same. Where two models hold one collection - a setup that was saved in the Prompt Builder and registered with the step RAG - Register Setup - the model the Builder saved is taken, for rag_model_id, for a retrieval query and for an ingestion run, when the other model is its registration: the catalog marks it step, the two name no different embedding models, and it is named RAG Retrieval - <name of the setup> or holds an ingestion run of RAG_RUNS that the setup holds as well. Another model with the same collection name, two setups of the Builder with one collection, or two models of the step stay open: rag_model_id is empty and the embedding rows are ambiguous, unless the retrieval names an ingestion run that RAG_RUNS holds for one of them only. A row whose content can not be compared - questions that are nested deeper than Python reads JSON - gets none, a catalog row that can not be read takes no part, and a WARNING names both. The rows around them are linked. Measured on 2026-10-12: a decision row whose questions were 30000 opening brackets gave WARNING: 1 row(s) could not be compared with the catalog - RecursionError - and got match_method none., and every other row was linked as before. With 2000 opening brackets the Python of that system (3.12.12) raised no such error: the row got none without the WARNING, as questions that fit no template do. The limits of the rules optimization and judge. Both link by containment: the texts of the catalog row have to stand in the prompts of the request, with _lnk_min_literal characters together as the only limit of size, without a word boundary, and for a judge row without a window of time. A request that is no call of the Prompt Builder is therefore linked when it holds those texts and no rule above fits it. Outside of SAS, on made-up rows: a request to the target model inside the window of an optimization that asks about the prompt (Is this a good system prompt? <the system prompt> Tell me.) is an optimization row, and so is a variant of the prompt - the system prompt and one more sentence - that is sent inside the window; a request to the judge model that quotes both prompts of a judged run is a judge row of that run, months later as well; and Claim: hail is found inside Claim: hailstorm. On the collected log the 49 optimization and 13 judge rows of 2026-10-12 were the calls of the Prompt Builder and none more: checked outside of SAS, the whole text of the catalog row stood in the system prompt of all 49, inside the window, and both prompts of the judged run in the user prompt of all 13, and no other caller and no other run held them. Such a row carries a rag_model_id when the prompt it quotes held the results of a retrieval, although the call made no retrieval itself: on that log 62 of the 193 LLM rows with the setup of one collection are such calls, and the summary line and the second statement of the example under How the Tables Join count them among the prompts of the setup. The window of a retrieval query on the collected log. Of the 290 query embeddings of the log of 1040 requests, 124 were followed by the prompt with their question within one second, 13 more within 33 seconds and one after 178 seconds. 83 were followed only after 6.8 to 23.8 minutes, 18 only had such prompts before them, and 51 had none. The 83 and the one of 178 seconds are 84 query embeddings of one collection that were sent before the first prompt of that collection - retrievals that were tested before a prompt used them. The default of 300 seconds links the 138, the one of 178 seconds among them; with _lnk_query_window = 1800 it is 221. Both numbers are what the program linked on the test system on 2026-10-12.

No caller id is logged. A request carries its inputs and nothing about who built them. A direct call of a model (a script, a health check, the test of a deployment) has no caller in SAS Model Manager at all. Two templates with the same text. A copy of a prompt, or two decision templates with the same questions and no state that tells them apart, fit the same requests: ambiguous. A template that is one variable. {{input}} fits everything, so it says nothing. A template with less than 20 characters of fixed text takes no part; the program counts such callers in a NOTE. The Builder's test calls against a template that was changed afterwards. The catalog holds the saved template and the templates of the runs that were kept. A test call that was not kept as a run and was made with a text that is no longer the template fits nothing. The health check of an optimization, and a call whose instructions the optimizer rewrote. The calls of a prompt optimization and of a judge are linked through a text of the prompt they hold. The health check an optimization sends first (You are a health check.) holds none, and neither does a call of an optimizer that has replaced the instructions by a proposal of its own. A further request with the prompts of an experiment run - the run sent again from the Builder page without being kept - is linked to the prompt by its template or its questions, and to no run. A retrieval that never reached an LLM prompt (the test of a retrieval, a flow that only retrieves), or whose prompt does not follow within _lnk_query_window seconds: its query embedding has no LLM row to be linked through. Embedding calls outside of an ingestion run, a run without finished_at, a setup with neither a run table nor a ledger in memory when RAG_RUNS was written, and the earlier ingestions of a setup whose run table is not in memory - a setup of the Prompt Builder whose job definition holds the program from before release 2.3.0, or whose run history is switched off: its ledger names the newest run only. The LLM calls of an enrichment during an ingestion: their prompt is in no catalog. A published model that sends the prompts of an experiment run again is linked to the prompt, not to the run. A template longer than 32,767 bytes is cut in the catalog and fits no request. Rows of an earlier parser have no kind, no hashes and no collection. The kind is taken from the role of the model that answered, where the catalog holds a model of that name; a row whose model the catalog does not hold is counted in a NOTE of its own, <n> rows of no known kind. Measured on 2026-10-13 on a copy of a table of release 2.2 after the append of a collected log: of its 3,630 earlier rows none got a caller, 3,434 got no model_id - their model names are not in the catalog - and all 3,630 carried the match_method none afterwards, so a later link leaves them out unless _lnk_redo_all is 1.

documents.t: From To Meaning LLM_LOGS.model_id MODEL_CATALOG.modelID (roles llm, embedding, decision_model) The model that answered LLM_LOGS.caller_model_id PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS.modelID The prompt or decision template (caller_kind = prompt or decision) LLM_LOGS.caller_model_id, experiment_run_id, model PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS.modelID, runID, model The row of the experiment run (match_method = experiment run). experiment_run_id is text and runID a number, and a run id counts inside one model only. A judge call (match_method = judge) carries the id of the run it judged, and its model is the judge LLM_LOGS.caller_model_id PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS.modelID The optimizations of that prompt. A call of an optimization (match_method = optimization) carries no id of the optimization: it is the one with startedAt <= timestamp <= finishedAt LLM_LOGS.caller_model_id RAG_SETUPS.modelID The setup of an embedding row (caller_kind = rag) LLM_LOGS.rag_model_id RAG_SETUPS.modelID The setup whose retrieval an LLM prompt carried RAG_SETUPS.modelID RAG_RUNS.modelID The ingestion runs of a setup LLM_LOGS.model_id, caller_model_id, rag_model_id MODEL_CATALOG.modelID The name and the project of any of the three MODEL_CATALOG has one row per model and pattern, so a model is there several times: join to it through a distinct list of modelID. MODEL_CATALOG.target_model, PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS.model and RAG_SETUPS.embedding_model are names of containers and equal LLM_LOGS.model. experiment_run_id is the place of the run in the tracker of the prompt, not a lasting id: when a run is deleted in the Prompt Builder, the runs behind it are numbered again, so after a new pull a row that was linked earlier can name another run. The link program counts such rows in a WARNING - rows whose run id the catalog no longer has, and rows whose run has another run time than the request - and %let _lnk_redo_all = 1; links all rows again. An example - what each prompt, decision template and RAG setup asked of the models, and the calls of the Builder's experiment runs beside their rows of PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS. The three statements ran on the test system on 2026-10-11 and on 2026-10-12 on the tables of the chain, with only the table names changed, without an ERROR or a WARNING and in 0.3 seconds; input(l.experiment_run_id, best32.) read the VARCHAR column: libname public cas caslib='Public'; proc sql; /* Requests, failures, tokens and seconds per caller and answering model */ create table work.usage_by_caller as select l.caller_kind, l.caller_name, l.caller_model_id, l.model, count(*) as requests, sum(l.failed) as failed_requests, sum(l.prompt_length) as input_tokens, sum(l.output_length) as output_tokens, sum(l.runtime) as seconds from public.llm_logs as l where l.caller_model_id is not missing group by l.caller_kind, l.caller_name, l.caller_model_id, l.model; /* The prompts that were fed by a retrieval, per RAG setup */ create table work.prompts_by_rag_setup as select s.name as rag_setup, s.collection, l.caller_name as prompt, count(*) as requests from public.llm_logs as l inner join public.rag_setups as s on s.modelID = l.rag_model_id group by s.name, s.collection, l.caller_name; /* The logged request of an experiment run beside what the tracker kept of it */ create table work.experiment_run_requests as select e.name, e.runID, e.model, e.best_prompt, e.run_time as tracked_seconds, l.timestamp, l.runtime as logged_seconds, l.status_code from public.llm_logs as l inner join public.prompt_experiments as e on e.modelID = l.caller_model_id and e.runID = input(l.experiment_run_id, best32.) and e.model = l.model where l.match_method = 'experiment run'; quit;

The log table has no key, and its prompts and every column a site added must not be rewritten. The program therefore numbers the rows in a copy in the caslib CASUSER, reads what it compares into Python (the prompts only of the rows it links), uploads the nine link columns with the row number, merges them back by that number into <table>_NEW beside the log table, checks that this table has as many rows as the log table, restores the order of the columns, gives the new table the label of the log table, and replaces the log table the way the parser does: dropped, renamed, promoted, saved. While it runs it needs room for two more copies of the table. A table that grew while it was linked - the parser appended to it - is left as it is, with an ERROR line; run the two one after the other. A run that links no row - every row has a match_method - builds no new table: the log table, its promotion and its saved file stay as they are, and the SAS log has NOTE: 0 of <n> rows of <caslib>.<table> were linked, as every row has a match_method. The table was left as it is. With _lnk_redo_all = 1 all rows are linked again. A log table that was not in memory, and that the program loaded from its saved file, is put in place by such a run as it was loaded: it is promoted where _lnk_promote_table is 1, the saved file is not written again, and one line says so - NOTE: The table <caslib>.<table> was not in memory. It was loaded from its saved file and promoted as it was loaded, the saved file was left as it is. With _lnk_promote_table = 0 the line is NOTE: ... It was loaded from its saved file and not promoted, as _lnk_promote_table is not 1, so it is a table of this CAS session and gone when the session ends. The saved file was left as it is., and where the promotion does not take, WARNING: ... could not be promoted, so it is a table of this CAS session and gone when the session ends. ... Where CAS refuses to say whether the promotion took, or the step that asks halts, the line is WARNING: ... It was loaded from its saved file, and CAS did not say whether it was promoted then: where it was not, it is a table of this CAS session and gone when the session ends. The saved file was left as it is. (not run in SAS). Before, the loaded table was a table of the session of the program and ended with it. Measured on 2026-10-12 in the third run, with the table dropped from memory and its saved file left: with _lnk_promote_table 1 the first NOTE, and the next job found the table in memory, promoted, with its 1040 rows and 36 columns and the saved file as it was; with 0 the second NOTE, and the next job found no table and the file as it was. The WARNING was not provoked. Every message of the program is made one text before it is handed to SAS, where a line for the log is a statement on its way: in a message a quote shows as a backtick, % as pct, & as + and a semicolon as a comma, a comment mark is split by a blank, a line break or a tab is a blank, parentheses that do not pair up show as brackets, and a message of more than 900 characters ends in three dots. Measured on 2026-10-12 with a catalog in which two models carried one name with a quote, a semicolon and %put ERROR: x;: the NOTE about the two models showed the quote as a backtick and the % as pct, and no ERROR followed. The parser and the pull carry the same function since version 2.4 and 2.2 of their steps; with it their messages arrived as text in the third run. A log table without the link columns was written by an earlier parser and is refused with one ERROR line that names the parser. Without the catalog there is one ERROR line that names Get-All-Prompts.sas. In both cases the table is left as it is. Where CAS refuses to say whether a table the program reads is in memory, or to list the saved files of its CAS library - for a table of the link that is not in memory, or for the saved file of the log table where _lnk_save_table is not 1 -, or where the PROC CAS step that asks halts, the run links nothing and writes nothing: ERROR: CAS did not say whether a table the program reads is in memory or did not list the saved files of its CAS library, so it is not known whether that table is there or whether the log table has a saved file. Nothing was linked and the tables were left as they are. Up to this release such a listing was taken for a library without the file, and the question whether a table is in memory was read without asking whether CAS had refused it. A new table that CAS does not say is there takes the place of nothing; where CAS refused the question the line is ERROR: CAS refused to say whether the new table <caslib>.<table>_NEW is there, so it did not take the place of the table <caslib>.<table>, which was left as it is., and a step that puts the table in place and halts ends the run with SYSCC 1012. The Python of the program takes the answers of table.fetch, table.columnInfo, simple.numRows and table.tableInfo only with the severity 0: a warning of one of the first three ends the link with ERROR: The rows could not be linked, ..., and a label that could not be read gives NOTE: The label of the table <caslib>.<table> could not be read, so the linked table has none. Not run in SAS. A run that wrote an ERROR line and no table - a log table or a catalog that was not found, a question or a listing of saved files that CAS refused or did not answer, a table the program refused, rows that could not be linked, a new table that could not be put in place - sets the condition code of the SAS session (SYSCC) to 1012 as its last statement; a WARNING, a NOTE and a run with nothing to link leave the condition code as it was. In the second run, before the statement existed, the refusal of a table of twelve columns ended with SYSCC 0 and a completed job. In the third run the same refusal and the run without a catalog ended with SYSCC 1012 and a failed job, and a second run with nothing to link and a run with a _lnk_query_window that is no number - a WARNING - as completed with SYSCC 0. As for the parser, the first DATA step behind a refused run does not run until SYSCC is reset (Reading the Job Log). The SAS log ends with one NOTE per kind of row, for the whole table, and with a fourth one where the table holds rows whose kind is not known - rows of an earlier parser whose model is not in the catalog: NOTE: 3434 rows of no known kind: 0 linked to a model, caller by ambiguous 0, none 3434. (2026-10-13). The three lines of a table without such rows: NOTE: 248 llm rows: 248 linked to a model, caller by experiment run 32, template 144, optimization 49, judge 13, ambiguous 0, none 10, and 238 linked to a RAG setup. NOTE: 355 decision rows: 355 linked to a model, caller by experiment run 41, questions and state 310, questions 0, ambiguous 0, none 4. NOTE: 437 embedding rows: 437 linked to a model, caller by retrieval query 138, ingestion run 3, ambiguous 72, none 224. The program wrote these three lines on the test system on 2026-10-12 - each with Python-Subprocess - behind NOTE: , as every line the Python hands to the SAS log - for the 1040 rows its parser had made of the collected log, the catalog of 421 rows and the 107 ingestion runs its pull had written that day. The matching of the 1040 rows took 0.09 seconds. The Chain on SAS Viya has the numbers of both runs, and what changed between the two.
documents.s: What the Program Does to the Table

documents.t: The three programs ran one after the other on the test system three times, each time as they were then: on 2026-10-11, on 2026-10-12 with the changes the first run had led to, and later that day with the changes the second run had led to. This section has the first run, then for each defect of the first run what the changed program did in the second, then the second run as a whole with what was changed after it, and then the third run, which measured those changes. What was changed after the third run is the part that is not run in SAS. On 2026-10-11 the chain was 23 SAS Job Execution jobs of the SAS Studio compute context, all of them on tables of their own in CASUSER, on a redacted collection of 1040 requests. The CAS server of that system runs without workers, and its PROC PYTHON is Python 3.12 with pandas 2.3.3, swat 1.18.1 and requests 2.34.2. The job logs hold the build stamp of the system (V.04.00M0P09082026), not the name of its release. What the parse did is under The parser of this release on SAS Viya and Appending, what the pull did under The Pull on SAS Viya. The link and the joins: What held The link. NOTE: 1040 of 1040 rows of <caslib>.<table> were linked against 365 catalog rows in 0.09 seconds. Every row had a model_id. The table kept its 36 columns in their order with their types and labels - only the lengths of the eight text link columns changed -, its rows in their order and the other 27 columns unchanged in every row. It was promoted and saved, and _LNK_STAGE, _LNK_LINKS and <table>_NEW were gone. The program took 4.9 seconds. Per kind and method, counted in the table: LLM rows - experiment run 32, template 144, none 72; decision rows - experiment run 50, questions and state 301, none 4; embedding rows - retrieval query 239, ingestion run 3, ambiguous 72, none 123. The callers were right. For all 769 linked rows the caller was compared with the content of the row afterwards, outside of SAS: the questions or the system prompt of the row are those of the caller's template or of a version kept in its runs, the state or the user prompt fits its user template, and no other caller of the catalog fits. 310 decision rows went to one decision template - 168 of them failed requests, linked like the others -, 131 LLM rows to one prompt template, and all 193 LLM rows with the collection of one RAG setup carried that setup in rag_model_id, whatever their match_method. A second run linked nothing: NOTE: 0 of 1040 rows ... were linked against 365 catalog rows in 0.06 seconds, 1040 rows that have a match_method were left as they are. All nine link columns were unchanged in every row. With _lnk_redo_all = 1 the program linked the 1040 rows again and wrote the same links. The refusals. A table of twelve columns as the log table: one ERROR message that names the missing columns and the parser, and the table unchanged. A catalog that does not exist: ERROR: The catalog table <caslib>.<table> was not found. Run Get-All-Prompts.sas first, ..., and the log table unchanged. Both jobs ended as completed. More rows than one read. A table of 3120 rows - the 1040 three times - takes two reads of 2000 rows, with prompts of up to 22559 characters: 3120 of 3120 rows ... in 0.17 seconds, the rows in the same order before and after, and every row with the links its request had in the table of 1040 rows. Tables that are saved and not in memory. The log table, the catalog and the runs table were loaded from their .sashdat files. The log table was promoted again, the two others stayed tables of the session. That run linked 0 rows, and the program of that day built, promoted and saved the table on every run - which is what promoted it. A run that links no row leaves the table as it is since (below), so a table that was loaded and not linked is now promoted by statements of their own, see What the Program Does to the Table. They ran in the third run. The joins. The three statements of How the Tables Join ran. Counted: 527 rows join to PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS by caller_model_id, which are the rows with caller_kind prompt or decision; 242 to RAG_SETUPS by caller_model_id, the rows with caller_kind rag; 238 by rag_model_id; all 1040 to the answering rows of the catalog by model_id; and 82 to the row of their experiment run. In one SAS session - parse, pull, link, link again - the chain gave the same links as the separate jobs, in 47 seconds. What the programs do in CAS, on this server: the DATA step of the append ran in CAS in several threads; the rows that were numbered with single='yes' and merged back by that number came out in their order, for 1040 and for 3120 rows; and the order of the columns was restored. A CAS server with workers was not tried. What did not hold on 2026-10-11, and what the changed program did on 2026-10-12. Each point names the change that was made after the first run, and then what the second run measured of it. The summary broke the SAS log. The three summary lines held semicolons. A line is handed to the SAS log as a statement, so the statement ended at the first semicolon and the rest ran as SAS code: four ERROR 180-322: Statement is not valid or it is used out of proper order. in each of the seven runs that reached the summary, PROC PYTHON stopped, and the job ended as failed although the table had been written, promoted and saved correctly. The NOTE lines ended behind linked to a model; the counts per method stood in the echoed source lines of the log only. The change: every message takes one way on which it is made one text, the summary is worded without a semicolon, and a macro variable is only ever given a whole number. On 2026-10-12: no log of the 35 jobs held ERROR 180-322, the job of the link ended as completed with SYSCC 0, and the three summary lines arrived in full. An experiment run was given to more than one request. The 82 rows with an experiment_run_id belonged to 70 runs and models: twelve were a second row. Three requests of the first run of a prompt carried the id of its second run, which had sent the same prompts - their logged run times are the ones the tracker holds for the first run -, and nine decision requests that had been sent again carried the id of a run whose tracked run time is not theirs. The third statement of the example therefore showed two requests for that second run and none for the first. The change: a row gets the run whose run_time is its runtime, and a run is given to one row. On 2026-10-12: 73 rows with an experiment_run_id - 32 LLM and 41 decision rows - for 73 runs and models, none of them on two rows. Joined to PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS, the logged run time equalled the run time of the tracker to three decimals in all 73. The three requests of the first run carried the first run, and the nine decision requests that had been sent again were questions and state without a run id. With a copy of the catalog without run_time the program linked 82 rows again, twelve runs and models on two rows, and wrote NOTE: 82 row(s) were linked to an experiment run without a run time to compare, as the catalog holds none for the runs with their prompts. ... A query embedding was linked through any prompt with its question. 18 query embeddings were linked to a setup whose last prompt with their question had been sent 20 minutes to two hours before them, and 84 embeddings of another setup were made before the first prompt of their collection was sent, up to 20 minutes before it. The rule had no time window. The change: the prompt has to follow within _lnk_query_window seconds. On 2026-10-12: 138 of the 290 query embeddings were linked - 100 to one setup and 38 to the other - where 239 had been. The 18 were none, with match_candidates 0. Of the 84, 83 were none; one, sent 178 seconds before a run of the Prompt Builder with the same text, is still linked (see the second run). With _lnk_query_window = 1800 and _lnk_redo_all = 1 221 were linked, 183 and 38, and with _lnk_query_window = soon the program wrote WARNING: The setting _lnk_query_window is soon, which is no number. 300 is taken in its place. and linked the 138. The calls of a prompt optimization and of a judge stayed none: 49 and 13 of the 72 LLM rows without a caller. The change: they are linked to their prompt with the methods optimization and judge. On 2026-10-12: 49 and 13, all to that prompt, the judge calls with the ids of the runs 2 to 14 of the prompt, one each. 10 LLM rows stayed none: the health check of the optimization, three browser requests with a system prompt that no kept run holds, and six test calls. A second run rewrote the table. With 0 rows linked the program still built <table>_NEW, dropped, renamed, promoted and saved: the table had a new modified time and its .sashdat was written again, with the same content. The change: such a run leaves the table as it is. On 2026-10-12: one message, NOTE: 0 of 1040 rows of <caslib>.<table> were linked, as every row has a match_method. The table was left as it is. With _lnk_redo_all = 1 all rows are linked again. The modified time of the table and the size and the time of its .sashdat were the same before and after, and so were the nine link columns of every row. The label of the table was lost by the link, as it was by the append. The change: the new table gets the label of the log table. On 2026-10-12: the table had the label Extracted LLM Log Data after the link, as before it. Two copies that had no label before the link had none after it, and the link was not run on a table with a label of a site's own - that such a label stays was seen for the append only. A second start of mysess. In the chain of one session the second run of the link wrote WARNING: A session with the name MYSESS already exists., as the pull behind the parser did. The change: the program asks SESSFOUND and starts lnkMySess only when no session is connected. On 2026-10-12: alone in a fresh SAS session the program started LNKMYSESS and ended it. In one job - parser, pull, parser, pull, link, link - no line said already exists, the job ended as completed without an error, one session with one id was connected after every program and at the end, and the links equalled those of the separate job in 1040 of 1040 rows. Behind a CAS session of the user - parser, pull, link, link - no program started a session of its own, and that session was the only one at the end. No ingestion link for the setup of the Builder. Its run table does not exist (see The Pull on SAS Viya). Of the 147 document embeddings 3 were ingestion run - they lie inside the one run of a setup that holds its run table alone -, 72 were ambiguous, lying inside runs of run tables that two or three models registered by the step share, and 72 were none. An embedding row carries no collection, so the log does not say which setup those 72 belong to; 60 of them lie in four bursts of that afternoon. The change: the pull writes the runs a ledger still names, which is the newest run of a setup only. On 2026-10-12: RAG_RUNS held one run of that setup, of six seconds, and the log holds no document embedding in those seconds, so no link changed: 3 ingestion run, 72 ambiguous and 72 none as before. Since then the ingestion job of a setup publishes its run table with every run the vector store holds for the collection (see RAG_RUNS under The Tables). That was measured in the third run with a setup of its own, whose four document embeddings were linked to its runs. Whether the store of the setup of this point holds the runs of that afternoon is not known: its ingestion was not run again.

The chain of that day - version 2.3 of the LLM - Log Parser step, version 2.1 of the LLM - Get All Prompts step and the link program as it was then - ran as 35 jobs. 31 ended as completed and 4 as failed: the refused append and the run with an engine other than CAS, as they should, one job the compute service started no session for, and one with an error of the test harness; the last two were run again. One of the chains wrote to Public, all others to CASUSER, and every table and file was dropped at the end. The parse is under The parser of this release on SAS Viya, Appending and Requests that run at the same time, the pull under The Pull on SAS Viya, and what each change after the first run did is in the list above. The link as a whole: What held The link. NOTE: 1040 of 1040 rows of <caslib>.<table> were linked against 421 catalog rows in 0.09 seconds., the three summary lines quoted under What the Program Does to the Table, and three more NOTEs: 4 prompt(s) or decision template(s) of the catalog have a template with less than 20 characters of fixed text. ..., 8 catalog row(s) of an optimization or a judge name no model, hold less than 20 characters of text or have a window that can not be read. ... and 15 ingestion run(s) have no start or no end and take no part. - the 15 are runs whose finished_at lies about two hours before their started_at. No ERROR and no WARNING, and the job ended as completed with SYSCC 0. The table kept its 36 columns - only the lengths of the eight text link columns changed -, its rows in their order and the 27 columns of the parser unchanged in 1040 of 1040 rows. The program took 5.6 seconds, the job 23. Per kind and method, counted in the table: LLM rows - experiment run 32, template 144, optimization 49, judge 13, none 10; decision rows - experiment run 41, questions and state 310, none 4; embedding rows - retrieval query 138, ingestion run 3, ambiguous 72, none 224. Against the run of 2026-10-11, by transaction id: 9 decision rows went from experiment run to questions and state, 101 embedding rows from retrieval query to none, 13 LLM rows from none to judge and 49 to optimization; no row had another model_id or rag_model_id. The links were checked afterwards, outside of SAS. All 730 linked rows were compared with the texts, run times, windows and runs of the catalog by rules written for the check, and none was wrong; a run of the link function outside of SAS on a parse of the same file gave the same nine link columns in 1040 of 1040 rows. All 238 rows without a caller were classed, and by the rules none of them should have been linked. One link is doubtful: a query embedding of 17:02:37, one of a batch of 40 of which the 39 others are none, is linked to a setup through a run of the Prompt Builder that was sent 178 seconds later with the same text. The setup is probably the right one, but what links the row is not a prompt of that request. The refusal of a table of twelve columns: one ERROR message of about 430 characters, over two log lines, and the table unchanged. The two table options. With _lnk_promote_table = 0, _lnk_save_table = 0 and _lnk_redo_all = 1 a table that was promoted and saved was still promoted afterwards and its .sashdat was written again. A table of a CAS session of the user, without a file, stayed a table of that session without a file, with its 1040 rows linked, and the session was still connected. Names that SAS would read as code. With a catalog in which two models carried one name with a quote, a semicolon and %put ERROR: x;, the NOTE about two models of one name showed the quote as a backtick and % as pct, no ERROR was written, the job ended as completed, and model_id was empty in the 6 rows that those two models could have answered. Run ids that no longer fit. With two linked rows set to the run id 99 and a run without redo: the NOTE of a run that links nothing and WARNING: 2 row(s) that were linked to an experiment run earlier no longer name that run: for 2 the catalog has no run with their id, for 0 the run with their id has another run time than the request. ..., and the table untouched. In Public. One chain wrote its six tables to Public under names of its own: the rows and columns of the parse and of the pull as in CASUSER, the same three summary lines of the link, all six tables promoted and saved, and dropped again afterwards. The joins. The three statements of How the Tables Join ran without an ERROR or a WARNING, in 0.3 seconds. Counted: 589 rows join to PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS by caller_model_id, the rows with caller_kind prompt or decision; 141 to RAG_SETUPS by caller_model_id and 238 by rag_model_id; all 1040 to the answering rows of the catalog by model_id; 73 to the row of their experiment run, one request for each run and model; the 13 judge rows to the run they judged; and the 49 optimization rows to the one optimization whose startedAt and finishedAt hold their time. ERROR and WARNING lines. From the first source line on, the logs of the 33 jobs that count held 41 such lines, all of them lines this page names: the three WARNINGs of the pull in each of its six runs that read and its two ERROR lines for the name of 34 characters, the lines of the refused append and of the engine other than CAS, one WARNING of the link each for a window that is no number, for the run ids that no longer fit and for questions of 30000 brackets, and its ERROR message for the table of twelve columns. Twelve runs of the link wrote none, and no log held 180-322 or already exists. What did not hold in the second run, and what the programs do since. The second half of each point is a change made after the run; the third run measured it later that day. A run that was refused left its job completed. The pull's refusal of a table name of 34 characters, with two ERROR lines, and the link's refusal of the table of twelve columns ended with SYSCC 0, and SAS Job Execution reported both jobs as completed, so a schedule saw no failure. The refused append ended with SYSCC 1012 and a failed job, as its DATA step had set it. Since then each of the three programs and both steps sets SYSCC to 1012 as its last statement in front of the macro variables it deletes, for every run that wrote an ERROR line and no table - the value and the place Ingest-Documents.sas has for a failed run. Reading the Job Log, Messages and Limits of the Pull and What the Program Does to the Table name the runs of each program. In the third run eight refusals ended their jobs as failed, and in the code of a flow the end action of the flow behind a refused step did not run. An engine other than CAS gave four ERROR lines, the fourth about a log that was never read (see Reading the Job Log). Since then such a run ends with its one line and reads no log. A response that holds a request line gave a second row where one line of text followed the request line: see Requests that run at the same time. This page named only the case with a Request Headers: line. Since then it names both, and a request whose response quotes lines of an earlier or a later time has status_code and failed missing, where it had failed = 1. The second row is still written: the lines do not tell these two cases from a request. Files whose times were not in file order gave failed = 1 for requests that had been answered, without a NOTE, and in one file a request the numbers and the response of another (same section). Since then the next part of a file begins where the time goes back by more than one second, a line that is older by one second ends no request, and a request the lines of its container end on has failed missing and is counted in a NOTE. Questions of 2000 opening brackets gave no WARNING. A decision row with such questions got none without a message - the Python of that system (3.12.12) raised no RecursionError at that depth -, and with 30000 brackets the WARNING of The Rules, in Their Order came. The row is none either way, and the program was not changed for it. Still no ingestion link for the setup of the Builder, see the last point of the list above. Changed after the second run for what a reading of the programs found - none of it a line of a job log of that run. The third run ran each of them but Load-Fact-Sheets.sas: The function of the pull that makes a message one text let comment marks, tabs and a parenthesis without its partner through, and three messages of the parser were handed to SAS as they were. The LLM Usage Report is a ready-made SAS Visual Analytics report. It is part of the transfer package of the content folder and sits in SAS Content > SAS Agentic AI Accelerator > Logging and Monitoring - see Install or upgrade with the transfer package. It is the recommended template for monitoring LLM usage and prompt experimentation in your environment — import it and use it as-is, or as the starting point for your own dashboards. Up to release 2.2 the report was a package of its own, LLM Usage Report.json; that package carried a share and an authorization rule that named two users, and the one package carries neither.

The report builds on seven CAS tables, all expected in the Public caslib by default. Load them (promoted and saved) before or after importing so the report has data to bind to: Table Produced by LLM_LOGS Parsing the collected container logs — Log-Parser-Code.sas or the LLM - Log Parser SAS Studio custom step, then Link-Logs-To-Models.sas LLM_FACT_SHEET / EMBEDDING_FACT_SHEET / DECISION_FACT_SHEET mdb load-facts (or Load-Fact-Sheets.sas) — see Model Definition Builder PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS / RAG_SETUPS / RAG_RUNS Get-All-Prompts.sas or the LLM - Get All Prompts SAS Studio custom step - see The Experiments of Every Kind Every metric is a calculated item of the report; the joins and aggregations are data sources of the report too, so no table is written for it: Model Calls (all kinds) - LLM_LOGS left-joined to the three fact sheets on the model. Cost per call is the input tokens times the token price (plus the output tokens times the output price), or the run time times the price per second for a model priced by the second. Behind the Overview, Decision Models and RAG pages. LLM Calls - LLM_LOGS left-joined to LLM_FACT_SHEET; every object on it counts the calls of LLMs only (kind is llm, or missing in rows of a release before 2.3.0). Behind the LLM pages. Templates (experiments and calls) and RAG Setups (ingestion and calls) - the templates of PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS and the setups of RAG_SETUPS, each left-joined to its calls in LLM_LOGS (by the caller the link program found, and by the setup whose collection a prompt carried), the setups also to their ingestion runs in RAG_RUNS. A template or setup without calls is listed as Never called. The pages: Page What it shows Overview What LLMs, decision models and RAG are; calls, estimated cost, failed calls and response time; calls per month and cost per 1,000 calls by kind of model Prompting Overview, LLM Usage Overview, LLM Usage Details, LLM Details Prompt experiments and LLM calls as before; LLM Usage Details also lists every prompt template with its experiment runs and calls Decision Models Calls, confidence, answers below 0.7, failed calls, time and cost; calls by template and model; answers by confidence band; the experiments of each template and model with the accuracy of their first answer against the expected one; every decision template with its calls; the calls RAG Grounded LLM calls, collections, chunks and questions embedded, tokens embedded, cost; per setup the ingestion summary (runs, last run, documents, chunks, embedding tokens, failed documents) and its calls; the grounded calls RAG_RUNS holds the runs of a setup only where its run table was in memory when Get-All-Prompts.sas ran; load the saved <prefix>_RUNS tables first, or a setup shows No ingestion run recorded. The first-answer accuracy compares the answer to the first question of a decision template with the first expected answer. The report reads the twelve columns LLM_LOGS had before release 2.3.0 by their names, and the link columns of release 2.3.0. A table that a parser of an earlier release wrote, and that was not appended to with the parser of release 2.3.0, lacks them: run the parser of this release and the link program once.

mdb builders-import imports the content folder, and the report with it: mdb builders-import # the tables of the report stay bound to Public mdb builders-import --report-caslib MyLib # ... or are pointed at the tables of the same name in MyLib See First install and upgrade for what the command does, and Importing without mdb for SAS Environment Manager and the sas-viya CLI. After the import the report is under SAS Content > SAS Agentic AI Accelerator > Logging and Monitoring > LLM Usage Report. The three fact sheets are loaded by mdb load-facts, or by the job Data/Load-Accelerator-Tables of the content folder (The tables of the reports).

The report binds each of its seven tables to server=cas-shared-default;library=Public. If your tables live in a different CAS library, repoint them one of two ways: mdb builders-import --report-caslib <library> points every table of the report at the table of the same name in that library, through the import mapping of the transfer service. The file is not edited. The release table of the Prompt Builder report follows --caslib / SAS_CAS_LIBRARY. The option has not run against SAS Viya. SAS Environment Manager / SAS Visual Analytics — import the package as-is, then open LLM Usage Report in SAS Visual Analytics and, in the Data pane, use Edit → Change data source on each of the seven tables to point to the same table in your library. note The package of earlier releases carried the report under the identifier /reports/reports/1f08db8d-d6c6-4ed1-9684-e7d11c4ec50c — the URI shown as the example SAS_LLM_MODEL_CARD_REPORT_URI and the Prompt Builder Model card report URI. Which identifier the report has on your site after an import of this release — the one of the package, or another where your site had a report of that name — has not been measured. Read it from the report in the folder Logging and Monitoring of the content folder after the import, and use that URI where the report doubles as the model-card custom chart for your registered models and manifested prompts.

The accelerator can resolve every external secret it needs — LLM provider API keys and RAG vector-store passwords — from a SAS Viya credential domain instead of governed tables or report-assigned data. Credentials are then centrally administered, per-user or per-group, and never stored in a CAS table or report definition. The Prompt Builder additionally uses this to show each user only the models they actually hold a key for.

One credential domain (for example agentic-ai-keys) serves the whole deployment — its name is the single value configured in the app Options. A credential in the domain belongs to a user or group and carries a map of named secrets: Entry name Holds OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AzureOpenAI, … LLM provider API keys — named after the KeyName each model definition's API_KEY option references (key_name in definition.yaml), because the Prompt Builder, its RAG Builder part included, looks a model's key up under exactly that name PGVECTOR_RAG_USER, PGVECTOR_RAG_PW RAG vector-store credentials — the prefix names the vector DB backend SINGLESTORE_RAG_USER, SINGLESTORE_RAG_PW, … further vector-store backends; one domain serves several stores side by side Who resolves what: A group credential (for example for LLMConsumers) equips every member at once — and nobody else. The credential has to go to a group the people who open the Prompt Builder are members of. A credential for a group they are not in is written without an error and mdb credentials-report shows the group holding it, and those users still find the models of the provider disabled in the Prompt Builder, with this note: No <provider> key available in the <domain> credential domain - ask your administrator for access. The examples on this page use LLMConsumers for those people: it is the group for everybody who needs access to the LLM repository, and mdb setup writes the commands that create it into sas-viya-cli-commands.txt (see Setup SAS Model Manager). A site that equips another group names that group instead — what counts is the membership, not the name. A user credential belongs to one person and overrides the group credential entirely — a personal set of keys. A user with neither, or with a map that lacks a specific entry, sees the affected models greyed out in the Prompt Builder with a note naming the missing entry and the domain — access to keys is an identity decision, not an application setting. Connection configuration — vector-store host, port, database name — is not a secret and stays in the RAG setup, never in the credential.
documents.s: The model: one domain, named entries, per-identity credentials

documents.t: Multi-entry credentials are authored with the shipped scripts create-credential-domain.ps1 (Windows) / create-credential-domain.sh (Linux/macOS), which authenticate through your sas-viya CLI session: Sign in once: ./sas-viya auth login. Keep your secrets where they already live: the accelerator's git-ignored .env file. The script reads it directly — no second secrets file to author or clean up. Provider key variables map onto their provider entry names, and every <BACKEND>_RAG_USER / <BACKEND>_RAG_PW pair is carried over verbatim (uppercased); everything else in the .env is ignored: .env variable Domain entry OPENAI_API_KEY OpenAI ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Anthropic GEMINI_API_KEY Google OPENROUTER_API_KEY OpenRouter AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY AzureOpenAI MISTRAL_API_KEY Mistral VOYAGE_API_KEY VoyageAI HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY HuggingFace AWS_BEDROCK_API_KEY AWSBedrock PGVECTOR_RAG_USER, PGVECTOR_RAG_PW, SINGLESTORE_RAG_USER, … same names Run the script per identity you want to equip: ./create-credential-domain.ps1 -IdentityType group -IdentityId LLMConsumers ./create-credential-domain.sh -t user -i myuser By default the repository's own .env is used. Point at a different file to manage multiple environments from separate .env files: ./create-credential-domain.ps1 -IdentityType user -IdentityId myuser -EnvFile C:\envs\prod.env ./create-credential-domain.sh -t user -i myuser -e /envs/prod.env For full control (custom entry names, no mapping), pass a raw NAME=VALUE file instead with -KeysFile my-keys.env / -k my-keys.env — its entries are stored verbatim. The domain is created if needed and the identity's credential is fully replaced with the recognized entries (the source file must list every entry the identity should keep, not only new ones). Creating the domain and any group credential requires SAS administrator rights; a user can (re)run the script for their own user credential in an existing domain. Secret values are never printed.
documents.s: Creating and updating: the CLI workflow

documents.t: The scripts above equip one identity per run, which is right for a demo and wrong for a rollout. mdb does a whole deployment from a manifest, and reports what it did: mdb credentials-init # write a starter manifest mdb credentials-add group LLMConsumers # add an identity to it mdb credentials-apply --dry-run # see the plan mdb credentials-apply # do it mdb credentials-report # who holds one mdb credentials-remove group FormerTeam # mark a credential for removal credentials-init reads your .env and writes a manifest listing the entries it actually carries — names only, never a value — so you can see what is available to hand out before deciding who gets it. All five commands default to credentials.yaml in the working directory, and --manifest (-m) puts it anywhere you keep deployment records; credentials-init still reads --file / -f, the earlier name of the option. The manifest is the one place a rollout is managed from: identities are added to it, narrowed in it and marked for removal in it, and credentials-apply carries out what it says. The manifest says who gets keys and where those keys come from. It never contains a key, so unlike the .env it is meant to be committed and reviewed in a diff — who may call which provider is a decision worth having a history of. A fuller example is credentials.example.yaml: domain: agentic-ai-keys source: ../../.env # relative to the manifest identities: - {type: group, id: LLMConsumers} - {type: group, id: RAGEngineers, only: [PGVECTOR_RAG_USER, PGVECTOR_RAG_PW]} - {type: user, id: sas-be-sa} - {type: group, id: FraudAnalytics, source: ../../envs/production.env} - {type: group, id: FormerTeam, state: absent} LLMConsumers stands for the people who open the Prompt Builder. Name the group your users are members of: a credential for another group is written, reported as held, and leaves them with the note No … key available in the … credential domain (see Who resolves what). After a run that plans or writes a group credential, credentials-apply prints one line to that effect, and credentials-report prints it where a group holds a credential: A group credential reaches only the members of that group, and a user's own credential replaces it for that user. Its last line names the report of the same manifest - mdb credentials-report --manifest <file> - or, for a run with --identity, of the same identities and domain. A path with a blank is printed in quotes. Paths inside a manifest resolve against the manifest's own directory, not your working directory, so a manifest and the .env files it names can be kept together and moved together. credentials-init writes the source path relative when the two are near each other and absolute when they are not — a ../../../../../.. chain is correct and unreadable, and breaks the moment either end moves. only narrows an identity to some of the entries, named the way the domain spells them (OpenAI, PGVECTOR_RAG_PW) rather than the way the .env does (OPENAI_API_KEY); a name the source does not carry is refused rather than quietly dropped. A single identity needs no manifest at all: mdb credentials-apply --identity-type group --identity LLMConsumers --dry-run mdb credentials-report --identity <user id> --identity-type user --domain, --identity-type, --env-file and --keys-file belong to that mode. With a manifest the run goes to the domain the manifest names and takes the type and the key file of each identity from it. A --domain that names another domain is refused before the sign-in, because an apply also removes what the manifest marks absent; so is any --identity-type, --env-file or --keys-file. Two entries for one identity are refused by credentials-apply and credentials-report as they are by credentials-add, and so is an identity named twice with --identity. An empty value of any option (what a variable of the shell that is not set gives) ends the command with exit code 2 before anything is read or written, as does a --manifest that names a folder. An identity id and a credential domain hold printable ASCII alone (U+0020 to U+007E), with no blank at either end. Any other character - a line break, a control character, a blank such as U+00A0, an invisible one such as U+200B or U+034F, a letter outside ASCII such as ö - is refused with exit code 2 before anything is written or asked of SAS Viya, in a manifest, as an argument and as --domain; a manifest that lists such an id is refused by every credentials command that reads it. Every line names an id and a domain as they are and unquoted, and such a character can show as another one or as none. A value of the manifest is taken only as YAML reads it. id, domain and source must be text, only a list of texts and verbatim true or false. YAML reads an unquoted 0123 as the number 83 and yes as true, so such a value is refused with exit code 2 before anything is written or asked of SAS Viya: <file>: identity <n>: 'id' must be a text, and YAML read a number there - put it in quotes ('0123', 'yes') to have it read as it is written. Write such a value in quotes (id: '0123'). mdb credentials-init, mdb credentials-add and mdb credentials-remove quote every value they write where YAML would read it otherwise, so --domain 2024 is written domain: '2024'. An id that is missing, empty or ~ is refused as no id; a domain that is missing, empty or ~ is agentic-ai-keys. An empty name in only names an entry no source carries, so the identity is not equipped. This was tested, not run against SAS Viya.

mdb credentials-add <type> <id> adds a group or a user to the manifest, so the file need not be edited by hand. The type is group or user: mdb credentials-add group LLMConsumers mdb credentials-add group RAGEngineers --only PGVECTOR_RAG_USER,PGVECTOR_RAG_PW mdb credentials-add group FraudAnalytics --source envs/production.env mdb credentials-add user sas-be-sa --manifest deployment/credentials.yaml The command edits the manifest and makes no call to SAS Viya; the credential is written by the next mdb credentials-apply, and the command prints that as its next step (mdb credentials-apply --manifest <file> --dry-run). Option Meaning --only The entries this identity gets, named the way the domain spells them. Repeat the option or separate the names with commas. --source This identity's own key file. The path is the one you type in the shell, relative to the working directory; it is written into the manifest relative to the manifest. --manifest, -m The manifest to edit. Default: credentials.yaml in the working directory. --env-file The .env a new manifest points at. Default: .env in the working directory. Not read when the manifest exists. --domain The credential domain a new manifest targets. Default: agentic-ai-keys. Not read when the manifest exists. What it does with the file: Only that identity changes. Comments, blank lines, the order and the other identities stay byte for byte as they are - but for the two comment lines credentials-init writes above its placeholder, which leave with the placeholder. A new identity is written in block style (- type: group / id: …) after the last one; an identity that is written {type: group, id: …} keeps that style when it is updated. The placeholder is replaced. A manifest from credentials-init names the identity CHANGE-ME-to-a-real-group; the first identity that is added takes its place. The comment about the placeholder above it leaves with it. No manifest yet: it is written the way credentials-init writes it, from the .env, with the identity in place of the placeholder. Without a .env nothing is written. The identity is already listed: no second entry is written, and the command says so and ends with exit code 0. With --only or --source the entry that is there is updated and the change is printed. An identity is the same one when type and id are equal, the id letter for letter. A name the source does not carry is refused. An --only name that is not among the entries of the source, or a --source file that is not there, ends the command with exit code 2 and the message credentials-apply gives for it, and nothing is written. The edit is made in the text of the file, because the YAML library mdb uses would drop every comment on a rewrite. Before the file is written, the result is read back and has to be the manifest that was there plus the one change. These layouts are refused with a message, and the file is left alone: an identities list that is not written one - line per identity, for example identities: [{…}, {…}], identities: [] or identities: null; an identity that is listed more than once; an only: list that is to be rewritten and holds a comment between its entries, because nothing says which entry of the new list such a comment belongs to; any other layout whose result does not read back as the manifest plus the one change, for example an only: that is an alias or an identity that takes a key through a merge (<<: *o). It ends with the manifest is laid out in a way this edit cannot be made in safely - nothing was written; edit the file by hand. A file YAML cannot read is refused with the line and the column where the reader stopped, and nothing of its text is shown: a key file handed as the manifest would otherwise be printed with a value.

A credential is removed through the manifest as well. An identity may carry state: absent: identities: - type: group id: FormerTeam state: absent mdb credentials-remove <type> <id> writes that line — on the identity that is listed, or as a new entry when the manifest does not list it — under the same rule as credentials-add: nothing else in the file changes. It does not contact SAS Viya. The credential is deleted by the next mdb credentials-apply: mdb credentials-remove group FormerTeam mdb credentials-apply --dry-run # the plan shows the action "remove" mdb credentials-apply # deletes the credential mdb credentials-report # shows it as absent credentials-apply plans the action remove for such an identity. A dry run shows it and removes nothing. A credential that is already gone is not an error: the run says that there was none to remove. An identity with state: absent needs no source and no entries, so a credential can be removed after its key file is gone. A run that only removes does not create or update the domain. credentials-report shows such an identity as absent (as the manifest says) once its credential is gone, and as STILL THERE (manifest: absent) while it exists. A credential that cannot be read is shown as unreadable with the answer of the service, and the lines below the table count it neither way: the line of the identities the manifest names ends ... hold a credential; <n> could not be read., and the line of those it marks absent ... hold none; <n> could not be read. state: present is the default and may be written. Any other value is refused when the manifest is read, with exit code 2, before anything is written or removed. mdb credentials-add on an identity that is marked absent sets it back to present and says so. The state line is taken out again, or rewritten to state: present where it is the first line of a block entry or where a comment stands on it. The comment stays as it is. Nothing is removed because a line is missing from the manifest. The service cannot list who holds a credential, so mdb cannot know what a deleted line once said. Leave the entry in the file with state: absent until the report shows the credential as absent. A refused read, removal or write of a credential names the answer of the service. A write shows the reason only for a 404 - for a group that does not exist, errorCode 12310, measured on 2026-10-14 - and not where the answer holds a value the write carried. The values are compared as the line prints the answer, every run of blanks, tabs and line breaks as one blank, and with the whole answer, also past the 300 characters a line shows of an answer that is no JSON. A request that gets no answer - a connection reset, a timeout - ends with one line, ... failed: no answer (<kind of exception>), that names nothing of the request. No traceback of mdb shows the locals of a frame. The id of an identity is percent-encoded as one segment of the address, so an id with #, ? or / names that identity and no other; . and .. alone are refused. Measured on 2026-10-14 in a second pass: an identity ZZ#X marked absent was asked for as .../groups/ZZ%23X, and SAS Viya answered 404 (errorCode 12302), its answer for a credential that is not there. ? and / were not tried. credentials-add and credentials-remove were run on files. The removal by state: absent, the plan and the report that show it were measured on 2026-10-14 in a credential domain and a group made for the pass, with the commands as they were before the fix-up of that day: the apply created the domain and the credential of the group with its three entries; after credentials-remove the next apply deleted it - HTTP 204 - without writing the domain, and the report said absent (as the manifest says); an apply once more said that there was none to remove and ended with exit code 0; and a credential the manifest marked absent while it was there was STILL THERE (manifest: absent). The lookup the Prompt Builder makes found the group credential with lookupInGroup=true and answered 404 without it. Of what the fix-up of that day changed, a second pass that day measured three things: a write for a group that does not exist printed the reason of the service - storing the credential for group '<group>' failed: HTTP 404 The credential could not be created because the group identity "<group>" does not exist. (errorCode 12310) - and ended with exit code 1; the report printed the line about a group credential once; and a --domain other than the one of the manifest ended credentials-apply with exit code 2 before any request. The comment on the state: line, the refusal of an identity listed twice and the count of a credential that could not be read ran against a stand-in for the credentials service in the test suite of mdb, not against a SAS Viya server, as did everything changed after that pass. A dry run cannot show you a diff Reading a credential returns its metadata — who wrote it, and when — and never its contents, not even the entry names.
