So a dry run tells you an identity will be created, replaced or removed, but not what it holds today. That is a privacy property rather than a gap: no identity can ever see another's keys. For the same reason there is no way to list who holds a credential. Both commands report on the identities you name, which is why passing the same manifest you applied gives you the after-picture of that rollout — and why a credential is removed by marking its identity state: absent, never by deleting its line.

A credential that is managed with a manifest is deleted through the manifest: mdb credentials-remove, then mdb credentials-apply (see Removing a credential). The standard tools delete as well — one credential, or the whole domain, which mdb never deletes — and they show the domain. Authoring the multi-entry map is the job of the scripts and of mdb credentials-apply: ./sas-viya credentials domains list ./sas-viya credentials domains show-info --domain-id "agentic-ai-keys" # show-info never returns secret values ./sas-viya credentials users delete --domain-id "agentic-ai-keys" --identity-id thatuser ./sas-viya credentials groups delete --domain-id "agentic-ai-keys" --identity-id LLMConsumers ./sas-viya credentials domains delete --domain-id "agentic-ai-keys" A credential that is deleted with these tools while a manifest still lists its identity as present is written again by the next mdb credentials-apply: the apply writes every identity the manifest does not mark state: absent. In SAS Environment Manager (as an administrator), Security → Domains lists the domain and its credentials per identity, and supports deleting them.
documents.s: Inspecting and deleting: CLI and Environment Manager

documents.t: The Prompt Builder Options pane gets a Credential domain setting, defaulting to agentic-ai-keys — the same default the admin scripts use, so a deployment that runs a script needs no configuration at all. The Builder fetches the signed-in user's secrets map once at load time and disables models whose provider entry is missing (a note names the entry and domain). The domain is the only key source; enter none to skip the lookup in deployments that use exclusively key-less models - self-hosted ones, and definitions whose container holds the key (--auth env), which are never disabled for a missing entry. The setting is one option for every kind the Prompt Builder offers: prompt templates, decision templates and RAG setups read the same domain. none works for the two template kinds only. A RAG setup has no key-less mode — the vector store's user, password and location come from the domain — so with none the RAG setup card is shown disabled with that reason, and nothing RAG is requested. The prompt-optimization job accepts the same domain name (keyDomain, same default) and resolves keys server-side under the identity its compute session runs as. That is only the launching user when the compute context runs its servers as the requesting user — see the service-account caveat below. RAG ingestion and retrieval read the <BACKEND>_RAG_USER / <BACKEND>_RAG_PW entries the same way — the backend prefix (PGVECTOR_, SINGLESTORE_, …) lets one domain hold credentials for several vector stores at once. Ingestion (SAS Studio / Job Execution) runs under the calling user, so access to the vector store follows the same identity rules end to end. The SAS code of an LLM call that the custom steps LLM - Create LLM Call (1.7) and LLM - Get Options (1.6) and the program Create-LLM-Call.sas write keeps the entry name in %let API_KEY=OpenAI; and reads the key of that entry when it runs, from the domain named in its line %let API_KEY_DOMAIN=agentic-ai-keys; and under the identity of its SAS session; the call sends the key in the place of the name. That line is written as it stands: the steps and the program do not read the Credential domain option of the Prompt Builder (credentialDomain). A site whose keys are in another domain edits that one line of the generated code. The key is not written to the log, and the macro variable options - what LLM-Call-Result-Table.sas puts into the result table - keeps the name. The request goes through the temporary file llmIn, which then holds the key: the code clears that fileref right behind the call, also behind a call that failed, and SAS deletes the file. Code of LLM - Create LLM Call 1.6, LLM - Get Options 1.5 and the program before this release left the file in the WORK folder until the SAS session ended - generate it again, or add filename llmIn clear; behind its PROC HTTP step. The code finds an entry whose name has letters, digits, ., _ and - only: it writes the name with COMPRESS (an entry named Azure OpenAI is looked up as AzureOpenAI and not found) and into a Perl expression that a / ends. The Model Definition Builder refuses any other name in key_name and in the API_KEY default of an options.json. Where the domain holds no such entry for that identity, the code writes WARNING: No key was read for the entry ... and sends an empty API_KEY. Code these programs wrote before sent the entry name as the key, and the provider refused it (401) - generate it again. See the README of SAS-Viya-Integrations/SAS-Code-LLM-Calls.
documents.s: How the applications use the domain

documents.t: Resolving a credential requires a SAS Viya session: the browser (the signed-in user) and compute-session runtimes (SAS Studio steps, Job Execution jobs) have one. A SAS Container Runtime (SCR) container does not, and neither do the MAS and CAS scoring runtimes that published decisions and Intelligent Decisioning tests execute in. For those destinations the secrets are supplied as environment variables at deployment time, using the same names as the .env and the domain (for a vector store: <BACKEND>_RAG_USER / <BACKEND>_RAG_PW, e.g. PGVECTOR_RAG_USER; connection config: the RAGSTORE_* variables; the embedding call: the RAGEMBED_* variables), exactly like the LLM containers receive their configuration today. The manifested retrieval code takes the user and the password of the vector store from the options input of the call first, then from the environment variables, and asks the credential domain only for what is still missing after both, so the same artifact runs on every destination. Where the two variables are set, they are used and the domain is not asked. The LLM containers themselves are unaffected either way: they receive the API key per call via the options payload, resolved by the caller - except a definition built with mdb add --auth env, whose container reads the key from an environment variable filled from a Kubernetes Secret. Its options.json has no API_KEY, so no caller asks the domain for it and no identity needs an entry for it - once the callers built before the switch are rebuilt. RAG ingestion looks the entry of an embedding model or an enrichment LLM up in two static maps of rag_core/providers.py, and a model that is still in them is still asked for (needs the 'OpenAI' entry in the credential domain). After a definition is switched, regenerate the maps from the fact sheets and replace them in the module: cd SAS-Viya-Integrations/RAG python -m rag_core.providers --from ../../Embedding-Definitions/embedding_fact_sheet.csv python -m rag_core.providers --llm-from ../../LLM-Definitions/llm_fact_sheet.csv A model whose options.json has no API_KEY is left out of the map and needs no entry. Without the two variables of the vector store the retrieval model does not fail the decision: it answers retrieval failed: RuntimeError: no vector-store credentials resolved: … in retrieval_status and returns no chunk. That is what it answered on 2026-10-11 in a test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning and in the publishing validation on a SAS Micro Analytic Service destination, where neither runtime had them. With the user and the password passed per call instead, in the options input of the model, the retrieval model returned chunks in both places the same day. The two variables as environment variables were measured for SAS Micro Analytic Service, also on 2026-10-11: PGVECTOR_RAG_USER and PGVECTOR_RAG_PW were put into a Kubernetes secret and set on the containers of the deployment from it, kubectl -n <namespace> set env deployment/sas-microanalytic-score --containers=* --from=secret/<name> the pod restarted, and a call with {} as the options of the retrieval model returned retrieval_status ok and three hits. Not measured: the same variables for the test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning, which runs in CAS, and for a SAS Container Runtime container. The retrieval model in a decision lists every variable the model reads and where each destination takes them. Service-account compute contexts. A compute context can be configured to run its servers under a shared service account instead of the requesting user (the stock SAS Job Execution compute context often is). A job running there resolves the domain as that service account — not as the person who clicked Optimize — so a personal credential is never found. Whether a context does this is its attribute runServerAs, which the answer of GET /compute/contexts/<id> holds as attributes.runServerAs. A context without the attribute runs as the requesting user. On SAS Viya 2026.09 the stock SAS Job Execution compute context has runServerAs set to a service account and SAS Studio compute context has none (read with the REST call on 2026-10-20). The remedy is a compute context that runs as the requesting user: point the app's compute-context Option at it, and keys follow the per-user/group rules above. The Prompt Builder has two such options, one per job: Optimization: compute context (computeContext) for the prompt-optimization job and RAG: ingestion compute context (ragComputeContext) for the RAG ingestion and the retrieval test. Granting the credential to the service account's identity or one of its groups with the admin script is no remedy for these two jobs. It makes the keys available to every job that runs under that account, and the jobs still fail: the optimization job writes its result to the prompt in SAS Model Manager, and the service account may not change the prompt of a user - on 2026-10-20 the job, run under it, made all its model calls and was then refused the write with HTTP 403. From release 2.3.0 the optimization job compares the user its session runs as with the user who started it and ends before its first model call when the two differ; its message names the account the session runs as and the option to change. The RAG ingestion cannot reuse the CAS session it needs in such a context (see Deploying the Builder UIs).
documents.s: Where the domain applies — and where it cannot

documents.t: The Model Definition Builder (mdb) generates complete LLM model definitions from a single manifest file per model, replacing the manual 10-step copy-and-edit process described in LLM Definitions. You pick a provider and a model, answer a few questions, and every asset the framework needs is generated consistently: the score script, inputVar.json/outputVar.json, modelConfiguration.json, options.json, requirements.json, the documentation files and the fact-sheet row. Generated definitions work with the established registration flow — continue with Register & Publish LLMs exactly as before.

cd Model-Definition-Builder/cli python -m venv .venv .venv/Scripts/activate # Windows; on Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate pip install -e ".[viya]" # keep the quotes; the [viya] extra adds sasctl for the Viya commands Requires Python 3.11 or newer. Without the [viya] extra mdb still adds, generates, validates and tests definitions; setup, register, publish, ship, load-facts, options-*, credentials-apply and credentials-report need it; credentials-init, credentials-add and credentials-remove edit a file and need neither the extra nor a sign-in. For air-gapped environments, download the dependency wheels on a connected machine and install with pip install --no-index --find-links <wheel-dir> sas-mdb.

New to mdb? The Model Definition Builder user guide is a step-by-step walkthrough of creating, checking, iterating on and registering a model (including embeddings and self-hosted Ollama/vLLM servers). This section is the reference summary. Run mdb add from anywhere inside the repository for the interactive wizard, or use the non-interactive form in scripts and pipelines: # Interactive: pick provider and model from a live (or bundled) catalog mdb add # Non-interactive examples mdb add openrouter deepseek/deepseek-v3.1 --yes mdb add anthropic claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 --id claude_sonnet_4_5 --yes mdb add azure-foundry --resource myres --deployment my-gpt41 --id gpt_41_az --yes mdb add hf-selfhosted --repo Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --id qwen_25_05b --params-billions 0.5 --yes Supported providers: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry (any host flavor; GA v1 or legacy api-version endpoint, key auth), Mistral, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock (Converse API - Bedrock API key by default, --auth-variant sigv4 for boto3/IAM shops), Google Gemini, Voyage AI, self-hosted Hugging Face models (transformers for LLMs, sentence-transformers for embeddings) and self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, vLLM). Before anything is written, the wizard shows the catalog-derived values — option defaults, metadata (description, context length, dates) and token pricing — for you to confirm or adjust: these steer scoring behavior and cost monitoring, so they should be accepted consciously. Adjusting also lets you rename or drop options (max_tokens=max_completion_tokens renames, -top_p drops) — useful when a model's provider contract differs from the classic parameter names; where the catalog's supported_parameters reveal the right token-limit name, the wizard picks it automatically. --accept-defaults skips the review (and --yes implies it); unknown token pricing is always asked about (or warned about in non-interactive runs). Embedding definitions work exactly like LLM definitions: the wizard picks the kind from the model you select (or the runtime you choose for self-hosted models), the folder lands in Embedding-Definitions/, the row goes to embedding_fact_sheet.csv, and registration continues with mdb register, exactly like an LLM. The generated embedding scorers return all three declared outputs (embedding, run_time, tokens) and embed the full vector — two long-standing bugs in several hand-written definitions that the templates fix centrally. The bundled open-source embedding models run on CPU: all_minilm_l6_v2, the BGE family, embedding_gemma_300m and the RTEB-leaderboard IBM Granite models granite_embedding_small_r2 (47M, 384-dim) and granite_embedding_r2 (149M, 768-dim), all Apache-2.0/MIT ModernBERT or MiniLM bi-encoders.

mdb add ollama and mdb add vllm create definitions that call a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible server, for either chat (--kind llm) or embeddings (--kind embedding). Unlike the hf-selfhosted path — which downloads weights into the SCR image — these keep the weights on the inference server and the container only carries the thin api-wrapper requirements. The server base URL is environment-neutral, resolving per call as option → OLLAMA_BASE_URL / VLLM_BASE_URL container environment variable → a localhost default, and an optional bearer token is read from OLLAMA_API_KEY / VLLM_API_KEY (leave blank for an open server). So one published image can point at a dev, test or production inference server without a rebuild. # chat model served by a local Ollama, addressed by its Ollama tag mdb add ollama llama3.1:8b --id llama31_8b_ollama --kind llm --yes # embedding model served by vLLM, with the server URL baked as the default mdb add vllm intfloat/e5-mistral-7b-instruct --id e5_mistral_vllm --kind embedding \ --base-url http://vllm-svc.ml.svc:8000/v1 --yes AWS Bedrock regions work like Azure resources: the region resolves per call as option → AWS_BEDROCK_REGION container environment variable → baked default, so one image can serve multiple regions.

Azure definitions are environment-neutral by default: the resource host you enter during mdb add is used for smoke tests, but is not baked into the definition unless you confirm it (or pass --commit-resource). A deployed container resolves its target as AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE container environment variable → the baked default — where a container sends its requests is a property of the deployment, never a scoring option, so nothing a caller passes can redirect it (an optional AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT replaces the built URL for a gateway in front of Azure). mdb deploy renders the Azure Deployment YAML, with that env block, for every Azure definition. Set AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE in each deployment's YAML to serve dev, test and production (or different customer subscriptions) from the same published image — and set it in your .env so the wizard and smoke tests use your environment automatically. mdb validate reminds you when a definition carries a baked resource. Host flavors and API styles. Azure hands out the same OpenAI-compatible data plane under three host suffixes, and mdb accepts any of them verbatim (a bare name still expands to the classic *.openai.azure.com): Host Resource type <res>.openai.azure.com classic Azure OpenAI resource <res>.cognitiveservices.azure.com Azure AI Services / Foundry resource <res>.services.ai.azure.com Azure AI Foundry endpoint (sometimes region-qualified) By default mdb calls the GA v1 endpoint (/openai/v1/chat/completions, deployment name in the body — Microsoft's recommended surface). If your resource or org policy still requires the legacy deployment-scoped route — recognizable by URLs like …/openai/deployments/<name>/chat/completions?api-version=2025-01-01-preview — answer the wizard's API version question (or set the AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION container environment variable) and the calls switch to that route. The reverse works too: a definition that bakes a version is forced back onto the GA route by setting AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION to an empty value in the container — a v1-only resource answers the legacy route with a bare 401 and no body, which is the symptom to look for. Embedding deployments work the same way: mdb add azure-foundry --kind embedding --deployment <name> builds on the emb_azure_openai_v1 template (/openai/v1/embeddings or the legacy route, api-key header, dimensions supported). Not just OpenAI models. The whole Foundry Models catalog is served through this same OpenAI-compatible surface — a DeepSeek, Llama, Mistral, Phi or Grok deployment on a Foundry resource works exactly like a GPT one (mdb addresses the deployment name, not the vendor); Microsoft's older separate Model Inference API (/models/chat/completions) is deprecated in favor of it. The boundaries are API-surface ones: the deployment must serve chat completions — embedding, audio/image/realtime, and Responses-API-only models (/openai/v1/responses, a different request/response shape, e.g. computer-use previews) are outside the chat-completions score contract — and some non-OpenAI models reject specific OpenAI options (e.g. temperature on certain reasoning models), which you control per definition anyway. API keys are read from environment variables or the .env file at the repository root (for example ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY). The wizard tells you which variable it used; keys are never written into any generated file.

By default a hosted model takes its key per call, in the API_KEY scoring option: options.json names a credential-domain entry (provider.auth.mode: api_key with key_name), and the caller - the Prompt Builder, the optimization job, a decision - resolves it. A call that carries no API_KEY option, or a blank one, fails before any request with No API key: pass the provider key in the API_KEY option of the call. (partials/_option_api_key.py.j2). The SCR container answers such a call with HTTP 422 and the source line of the raise as its errorMessage, not the text of the exception, so every message of this kind is written out on that one line: the caller reads raise RuntimeError("No API key: pass the provider key in the API_KEY option of the call.") behind 422 Unprocessable Entity:. Up to this release such a call failed with a KeyError and the errorMessage held only the marker line of the traceback (~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^); the containers of 2026-10-20 answered so. The new score code has not been published to a container yet. The name of the entry (key_name, and the API_KEY default of an options.json) has letters, digits, ., _ and - only: the SAS code of an LLM call writes it into %let API_KEY=...; with COMPRESS, so Azure OpenAI would be looked up as AzureOpenAI, and into a Perl expression that a / ends - mdb refuses any other name with a line that names the characters, at generate, validate, import and register. A definition with provider.auth.mode: none and a score template that sends the key of the API_KEY option is refused the same way: its options.json would have no API_KEY, and every call would fail with the line above - set api_key with key_name, or env. A score code kept by hand (generation.overrides, such as the self-hosted Llama and Phi folders) is not refused, and mdb import of a folder of such a template whose options.json has no API_KEY is refused naming options.json. With --auth env the SCR container holds the key instead, in an environment variable filled from a Kubernetes Secret: mdb add openai gpt-6-luna --auth env --yes mdb add anthropic claude-sonnet-5-5 --auth env --key-env TEAM_ANTHROPIC_KEY --yes mdb add openrouter typesafe/jev-1.13 --auth env --yes # a decision model # definition.yaml provider: auth: mode: env env_var: OPENAI_API_KEY # optional - the adapter's default when absent The variable. --key-env NAME (auth.env_var, upper-case letters, digits and _) names it; without it the provider's own name is used - the names of .env.example: OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY (google), MISTRAL_API_KEY, VOYAGE_API_KEY, AWS_BEDROCK_API_KEY (bedrock), AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY (every azure adapter) and TYPESAFE_API_KEY. An adapter without a default needs --key-env. key_name is not used in this mode, and a manifest that sets it is refused. What is generated. options.json has no API_KEY entry. The score code reads the key from the variable (partials/_env_api_key.py.j2, shared by every template that sends a key) - only its name is written into the file. A caller that passes a non-empty API_KEY option still wins, so a credential-domain caller keeps working; a blank one counts as not set. With neither, the call fails before any request with No API key: set the <VAR> environment variable on this container (or pass an API_KEY option). The README and model card say where the key comes from, and the description the fact sheet, modelConfiguration.json and the model card show ends with The key comes from the container environment variable <VAR>. That sentence is not written into definition.yaml: every mdb generate and mdb sync derives it from auth, so it follows when you switch a definition to env by hand, name another variable or go back to api_key. A manifest in this mode that declares an option named API_KEY is refused - its default would take the place of the container's key in every call. mdb import of a folder generated in this mode (also mdb pull --import) reads the variable from the score code and keeps the mode. In env mode the env partial takes the place of the API_KEY option partial; nothing else of the score code changes. Where it applies. Templates that send a provider key: OpenAI-compatible chat and embeddings (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Mistral), Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock (bearer key), Azure AI Foundry, Voyage and System One decision models. A template that takes no key - self-hosted weights, Ollama/vLLM (their own token variable), Bedrock SigV4, azure-foundry-env (already environment-keyed) - refuses --auth env with one line. No credential-domain entry. A model whose options.json has no API_KEY is offered in the Prompt Builder without a key - run, judged, used in a council, optimized and manifested - and is never shown disabled for a missing entry; mdb credentials-* need no entry for it either. Remove an API_KEY option from a flow or a manifested model that was built while the definition still took one: a non-empty option wins over the container's key. The same holds for SAS code generated by Create-LLM-Call.sas or the custom step LLM - Create LLM Call (and LLM - Get Options) from the options.json of before: it sets %let API_KEY=<entry name>; - the name of the credential-domain entry, such as OpenAI, not a key - and sends a key in its options. Code of LLM - Create LLM Call 1.6 and 1.7, LLM - Get Options 1.5 and 1.6 and the program of this release reads the key of that entry from the credential domain and sends it, in the place of the container's key; code of earlier versions sends API_KEY:&API_KEY., the entry name, so the provider answers 401. Generate that code again from the new options.json, or delete the %let API_KEY=...; line and the API_KEY:&API_KEY. part of its options string. RAG ingestion looks a model's entry up in the static maps of rag_core/providers.py: regenerate them after the switch (python -m rag_core.providers --from ../../Embedding-Definitions/embedding_fact_sheet.csv and --llm-from ../../LLM-Definitions/llm_fact_sheet.csv, see Managing Credentials), or ingestion still asks the domain for the entry. Who can call it. The Ingress mdb deploy renders has no authentication: anyone who can reach host/llm/<model> calls the provider with the organisation's key, without any credential-domain check - the same holds for azure-foundry-env. Restrict who can reach the path - an allowlist of source addresses on the Ingress (with ingress-nginx the annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/whitelist-source-range), a NetworkPolicy, or no Ingress at all where only callers inside the cluster use the model - and set a spending limit for the key at the provider. On the workstation. mdb test lets the score code read the variable from the environment or .env, as the container does, and stops with one line when it is not set; mdb validate --live, ship and radar read the definition's variable first, then the adapter's. Deploying. mdb deploy adds the variable to the Deployment from a Secret (secretKeyRef, the Secret key named like the variable; --key-secret, default llm-api-keys) and prints the kubectl create secret generic line for every variable it rendered - names only, each value filled in by your shell (see Deployment YAML).
documents.s: The provider key from the container's environment (--auth env)

documents.t: By default mdb reads and writes definitions in the accelerator clone's LLM-Definitions/ and Embedding-Definitions/ folders. If you would rather commit your definitions to your own git repository (instead of carrying them in a fork of the accelerator), point MDB_DEFINITIONS at your repo in its .env: # .env in your own repository MDB_REPO=/path/to/sas-agentic-ai-accelerator # supplies the definition-core templates MDB_DEFINITIONS=/path/to/your-repo # mdb keeps its layout under this root mdb loads the .env from your current working directory (and its parents), so running it from inside your repo picks these up automatically. Under that root, mdb creates the familiar layout as needed — LLM-Definitions/, Embedding-Definitions/, and the mdb retire archive _archive/ (add that one to your .gitignore) — and every command (add, apply, generate, validate, register, list, retire, …) operates there, including the fact sheets (llm_fact_sheet.csv / embedding_fact_sheet.csv) inside the definition folders. The accelerator clone is still required for the templates, which is what MDB_REPO points at. After adding a model, work through the pipeline in order — each step catches a different class of problem before the next one can be blamed for it: mdb validate <model_id> --live # coherence rules + one real provider call through the adapter mdb test <model_id> # run the GENERATED scoreModel() locally - exactly what SCR will execute mdb register <model_id> # register in SAS Model Manager mdb publish <model_id> # publish to the SCR destination (or mdb ship for register + publish) mdb validate --live proves the provider, endpoint and key work; mdb test additionally proves the generated score code works — options parsing, request body, response extraction — so a template or option problem surfaces on your machine, not in a published container.
documents.s: Keeping your definitions in your own repository

documents.t: mdb now owns the full Viya lifecycle for managed definitions (install the extra: pip install -e "Model-Definition-Builder/cli[viya]"): mdb setup # create the LLM Repository + LLM/Embedding # projects if missing (idempotent; register # runs this automatically for its kind) mdb register <model_id> # create in SAS Model Manager (skips if it exists) mdb register <model_id> --update # replace a registered model IN PLACE: new minor # version + content replacement + refreshed attributes mdb publish <model_id> --wait # publish to SCR and poll until the image build finishes mdb ship <model_id> # validate --live -> register --update -> publish --wait mdb unregister <model_id> # delete a registered model from Model Manager mdb endpoints --json # SCR endpoint manifest for CI and testing mdb options-save # save this deployment's Prompt Builder options to a file mdb options-restore # write them back after importing a report package mdb builders-import # import the content folder - the one transfer package: # release table, host, data-source binding and the # options of the Prompt Builder report in one run mdb content-deploy # bring a SAS Content folder to the state of the checkout mdb package-export # maintainers: export the content folder to the one package mdb package-check # compare the package with the checkout mdb decision-node-migrate # give the site's Call LLM node the id of the package and # move every decision that uses it (dry run; --apply) On a fresh environment, mdb setup creates the LLM Repository and the LLM/Embedding Model Projects (idempotent — existing objects are left untouched), and mdb register performs the same check automatically for the kind it registers, so you do not have to run setup explicitly. mdb setup also writes the authorization-group rules (sas-viya-cli-commands.txt) and one seed file, llm-prompt-builder.json — the repository ID, the LLM project ID, the embedding project ID, the SCR endpoint and the deployment type, each under the name of the Prompt Builder option it is the value for. It is the single entry point for bootstrapping the environment. Once the Prompt Builder is configured, mdb options-save supersedes the seed file: it starts from the same discovered values and overlays what the live report actually holds, so what you keep is your deployment as configured rather than as bootstrapped — see Preserving builder options across a report import. --update removes the old delete-and-re-register workaround: after mdb generate, one command refreshes the registered model while keeping its ID, history (a new model version is created) and project placement. Both kinds use one implementation — embedding models register into the Embedding Model Project with the same content roles and fact-sheet enrichment. Each registered model also stores its definition.yaml as model content, so the source of truth travels with the model.
documents.s: Register, update and publish from the CLI

documents.t: The content folder /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator ships as one transfer package, SAS-Viya-Integrations/SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json. What it holds is listed in SAS-Viya-Integrations/package-manifest.yaml: one entry per object with its path below the content root, its kind - folder, file, custom step, job definition, report, decision - and the repository file it is a copy of. The content folder has the layout and what never ships. Four commands act on that list, and a fifth prepares a site for the decision it holds: mdb builders-import [<file>...] [--options <file>] [--content-root <path> [--create]] [--no-reports] [--no-decisions] [--compute-context <name>] [--report-caslib <lib>] [--dry-run] # bring the package to a site mdb content-deploy [--content-root <path>] [--create] [--only <path> [--to <path, id or URI> [--force]]] [--compute-context <name>] [--dry-run] # bring a content folder to the state of the checkout mdb package-export [--content-root <path>] [--out <file> [--keep-user-ids]] [--allow-differences] # export the content folder to the one package mdb package-check [<file>...] [--release [--base <commit>]] [--fix] [--allow-missing] # compare the package with the checkout mdb decision-node-migrate [--node-name <name>] [--target-id <id>] [--from-id <id>] [--apply [--delete-old]] # move the Call LLM node to the id of the package The commands ran on SAS Viya 2026.09 in eleven passes, twice on 2026-10-12, three times on 2026-10-13, three times on 2026-10-14, twice on 2026-10-15 and once on 2026-10-16, each as they were then, in test content roots below the folder of a user; each paragraph below says what was measured. What the first pass found changed them, and the second pass measured the import in place, the write of a file in place, the settings of a site, --to and the two forms of the gate. The third pass measured what was built after the second: release.json written last, --create, --force, the If-Match of the compared read and a write that is refused, the commit check of --release, the user ids an export replaces, the deletes an export sends, and the paths a package may hold. The fourth pass, the second of 2026-10-13, measured what was built after the third: the refusal of a part that names release.json, the content root of a folder that goes somewhere else, the rule for a reference of the name of an entry, the line for a folder that is created, the whole answer of a refused write, the command a failed import names, a custom step registered without the user of its .step file, userName among the fields an export replaces, and the commit id in full. What that pass and two reviews of the same code found was changed once more, and the fifth pass, the third of 2026-10-13, measured of it: a port in SAS_VIYA_URL, a reference of another kind in the list at the end of a run, the hint of a FAILED line for a reference alone, run as printed, the line of a refused write on one line, and the command the export printed for a test folder, which brought the 70 entries of an export into a second test root in place; on the workstation, without a request, the refusal of a part that names release.json in front of the sign-in; and at a stand-in on the workstation, not at SAS Logon, one sign-in for an answer that says Bad credentials and the one line for other 401 answers. What the fifth pass and the reviews beside it found was changed again, and the sixth pass, on 2026-10-14, measured it: a value printed as it is, the hints of a FAILED line in a run of a part and for the folder Data, each run as printed, the words of the list at the end of a run, the refusal of an empty --only or --content-root and of an address that cannot be used, without a request, and --create in the command the export prints for a test folder, which created a second test root that was not there and the 70 entries in it. What that pass and the reviews beside it found was changed once more, and the seventh pass, later on 2026-10-14, measured of it: the refusal of an empty --manifest, of --content-root / and of the address forms refused since then, without a request, and a deploy of the whole content folder into a new test root, whose export the command it printed brought into a second new root in place. What that pass and the reviews beside it found was changed once more, and the eighth pass, late on 2026-10-14, measured of it the lines of mdb package-export for a test folder, and again a deploy of the whole content folder into a new test root and the import in place of its export into a second one. The ninth pass, on 2026-10-15, measured of what was changed after the eighth the HEAD of a sign-in with a token, which the test system answered with 302, and again the deploy, the export and the import in place. The tenth pass, late on 2026-10-15, measured once more the deploy, the export and the import in place, with the commands as they were then. The eleventh pass, on 2026-10-16, measured them once more, and the credentials commands for a group and a user: credentials-init, credentials-add, credentials-apply after its dry run, credentials-report, credentials-remove, and credentials-apply and credentials-report again, after which no credential was left. The rest of those changes has not run against SAS Viya: the refusal of every empty value and of the options a manifest makes useless, and the one line of each outcome of the sign-in; nor has what was changed after the eighth pass but the HEAD of a token: the HEAD of a CLI login, and the refusal of an identity id or a credential domain outside printable ASCII, which ends before a request; nor the traceback of an exception that no command caught, which is printed without control characters since a change made after the ninth pass, with the text of each exception on the one line that names it since a later one, and the refusal of an empty port in SAS_VIYA_URL. Not run either: the quotes of a value, the answers of the token address that end a command since the sixth pass, the line for another status of the token address, which went to a stand-in on the workstation, the two commands for two packages of which one is refused its reports, and the gate for an id that is no commit. What was measured, and what has not run has the list. mdb builders-import is the command of a site: First install and upgrade describes it. It brings the package in two ways: the reports, with the files that are children of a report and the folders they sit in, through the SAS Viya transfer service, and every file, custom step and job definition in place, by the requests mdb content-deploy sends, with the package as the source of the content - What an upgrade does to what a site has. Three things it says rather than does: A package from before 2.3.0 that somebody names. Such a file still holds the report RAG Builder and the job definition RAG-Builder-UI, the standalone RAG UI that is now part of the Prompt Builder. The command names it as predating 2.3.0, because importing it brings that UI back and mdb does not configure its report. A report named RAG Builder that is still on the site. It is retired, keeps serving the old UI with its own options, and is neither written to nor deleted; the message says how to remove it. See the retired RAG Builder report. A run that did not do everything. The exit code is 1 and the run ends with the command to repeat for its case, with the files and flags it was given, on a line of its own that can be selected and pasted into PowerShell or bash: paths are spelled with forward slashes, and an argument a shell would read something into is quoted. The line is built from every option of the run but --dry-run. Where the reports were refused for the content root and no package's reports went to the transfer service, it carries --no-reports and says that it was added; where the reports of one package went through and those of another were refused, it is two commands: the run without that package, and that package with --no-reports; only the line with the package the release table came from loads the table again. Where the package imported and only the options could not be written, that command is mdb options-restore --file <the kept file>, which writes the options and imports nothing. mdb content-deploy makes a content folder hold what the checkout holds, without a package. It creates the folders, uploads the files, registers the custom steps and updates a step that exists in place (PUT /dataFlows/steps/{id}), so that the step keeps its id and saved flows keep working, and creates the job definitions or updates them in place - the program as code, the page as the property form, the parameters. It writes two files itself: Data/ACCELERATOR_RELEASES.csv, the release table as mdb load-releases --csv writes it, and release.json. It does not deploy the two reports, which are authored in SAS Visual Analytics and reach a site with the package. One line per entry says equal, updated, created, or FAILED with the reason. --dry-run writes nothing and says what a run would do. Where the folder the content goes into is created, the first line says so - created folder <path> (the folder the content goes into ...), in a dry run too; it is no entry and is not counted with them. Everything is written in place. A file that is missing is uploaded; one whose bytes differ gets its content replaced (PUT /files/files/{id}/content under the ETag of the content that was compared, so that a file somebody changed after the comparison is refused and left as it is) and stays the file it was - same id, same place. A custom step and a job definition are updated under the id they have. Nothing is deleted. What sits in a folder of the list and is not listed is named at the end and left alone. The run stops at the first write that is refused or gets no answer. That entry is FAILED, every entry behind it is not attempted, and the line Stopped at the first write that failed: ... says what was written before it and that nothing was removed. Where the update of a file is refused, the file is left as it is. An entry that fails before anything was sent - two objects of its name in the folder, a reference of its name to an object of its kind elsewhere - alone, or beside the object itself -, an object that cannot be read - is reported and the run goes on: each object and each reference of the name is named on the line, and none is written. A reference of that name to an object of another kind fails nothing and is listed at the end as <path> (reference to a <kind> - not the <kind of the entry> that is listed under this name). The kinds are spelled as the other lines spell them: file, folder, report, registered step, job definition; an object of no kind of the manifest is called by the content type the Folders service gives it, or by its address. A folder that FAILED this way takes what is in it with it - nothing is written into it, in a dry run as in a run -, and a folder that cannot be created stops the run like a failed write. Either way the exit code is 1, and a second run leaves what is equal by then as it is. The line of a refused request shows message, remediation and errorCode of the answer whole, on one line. The line of a FAILED entry names the command that updates one object - mdb content-deploy --only "<path in the manifest>" --to <its URI>, --to <id>, or for a folder --to <the SAS Content path of that folder> - with the path the manifest lists, also in a run of a part. For a folder with a job definition that reads the content root it sits in (Data) the line says that the path has to end with that folder; for release.json it names no command, because release.json is written only by a run of the whole manifest. release.json is written last, only by a run that covers every entry of the manifest, and only when every entry in front of it was written: behind a stop or a failure its line says not attempted and why, and the folder keeps the release.json of an earlier run, or has none. A run of a part that names it - --only release.json - is refused with one line before the command signs in. A folder that is not there is created only where the manifest's own content root is the target; for another --content-root, and for the folder form of --to, --create creates it with every folder above it, and without it nothing is written: there is no folder P, and nothing was created: pass --create to create it .... A repository file is uploaded with LF line ends whatever the checkout holds, so that the same file has the same hash from every checkout. A custom step is compared in its program, its form and its ports; a change of its description alone is not deployed. Site settings. A parameter the manifest marks siteSetting is a value of your site: _contextName and contentRoot, and of Start Here and the loader the CAS library and server, the credential domain, the names of the repository and the projects, the compute contexts to look for and the release table. A new job definition gets the default, and so does one that has no such parameter; a value a job definition on the site holds stays, and the deploy does not count it as a difference. --compute-context <name> writes a compute context into every job definition that has _contextName; contentRoot is always written with the content root the content goes to - for a folder that goes somewhere else see One part, somewhere else; one object named with --to keeps the one it has. The other parameters of a job definition - the address of the guides, _action, _output_type - are written as the manifest has them. --only RAG deploys the RAG runtime alone; with --to a part goes somewhere else, see One part, somewhere else. An empty --only - what --only "$PART" gives where the variable is not set - or one that is nothing but slashes ends the command with exit code 2; so does an empty --content-root, here and in builders-import, package-export, options-save and options-restore. Measured on SAS Viya 2026.09 on 2026-10-12, with the command as it was then, in a test content root: The dry run listed the 72 entries of the manifest - 61 objects and their eleven folders - as 70 created, 2 not deployed, the two reports, and wrote nothing: the folder did not exist afterwards. The run created the 70. Read back from the folder, every repository file had the bytes of the repository with LF line ends, every custom step and job definition equalled its source in each compared part, the release table CSV was byte for byte the file mdb load-releases --csv writes (626,101 bytes, 707 rows), and release.json held the release, the commit and 72 entries, with the hash of a downloaded file equal to its entry. A second run said 70 equal, 2 not deployed; a listing before and after it differed in no id and no modified time. An update in place. A file, a custom step and a job definition were changed by hand: the dry run named the three as updated and wrote nothing, the run updated them, and the step and the job definition had the ids they had before. The file had a new id - the command of that day deleted a file that differed and uploaded it again, which is what the write in place replaced. What is not in the manifest - a file, a folder with a file in it, a registered step and a job definition that were put into the folder - kept its ids and modified times through every run. Four of the five were listed under Not in the manifest and left alone: of a folder that is not listed, the folder is named and not what it holds. Against the content folder of the test system the dry run said 16 equal, 34 updated, 20 created, 2 not deployed and wrote nothing. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-12, with the command as it was then, in a new test content root: the same counts for the dry run, the run and a second run; a file changed by hand updated ... (content replaced in place; id <its id> kept) by one PUT /files/files/{id}/content with If-Match, answered 200, without a DELETE, the id and the creation time of the file kept and its bytes those of the checkout, the file and its content answering with the same ETag; a custom step and a job definition changed by hand updated under their ids; a _contextName set by hand on Start Here left alone and the next run all equal; --compute-context and --content-root written. Measured in the third pass, on 2026-10-13, with the command as it was then, in two new test content roots: --create. For a content root that was not there the command ended with there is no folder <root>, and nothing was created: pass --create to create it (with every folder above it that is missing), exit code 1 and GET requests only. With --create: 72 entries: 70 created, 2 not deployed., exit code 0, release.json the last line of an object and the last write, and the new root in contentRoot of the two job definitions that have it. The folder of the root was created without a line for it, in the dry run and in the run; the line is new since then. A reference at a path of the manifest. With a file deleted and a folder member of type reference of its name in its place, the dry run and the run said FAILED for the entry (a reference of that name is in the folder ...) and not attempted for release.json (not written: 1 entry in front of it FAILED ...): 72 entries: 68 equal, 2 not deployed, 1 not attempted, 1 FAILED., exit code 1, GET requests only, and release.json with the time stamp, the bytes and the ETag it had. The same path was also listed under Not in the manifest and left alone, which it no longer is. With the reference removed the file was created and release.json equal. The ETag of the compared read. A file changed by hand was updated ... (content replaced in place; id <its id> kept); the If-Match of the PUT was the ETag of the GET .../content in front of it, and the answer was 200. A write that SAS Viya refuses. A file that another writer changed between the read and the write of the command - staged by the harness of the pass - was refused with HTTP 412: FAILED ... (the file was left as it is ...), 30 entries not attempted, the usage report not deployed ... (not looked up after the stop), release.json not attempted and unchanged, 39 equal, 2 not deployed, 30 not attempted, 1 FAILED, Stopped at the first write that failed, exit code 1. The content of the other writer stayed, and the next run updated the file in place. The line of that day ended in the middle of the JSON the service answered ("remediation":"Get the latest re))); it shows the answer whole since then. release.json holds the release, the commit of the checkout the folder was deployed from with the date of that commit, and every entry of the manifest with its kind and - for a file, a custom step and a job definition - a SHA-256 hash of its content. The page Start Here reads it. mdb package-export is for maintainers. It exports the content folder with its dependencies and keeps what the list names: every other object of the export is dropped with its entries in the package - a generated artifact, a report somebody parked in the folder, a dependency from outside it -, and so is every authorization rule and share. Of the files a report brings along, those stay that are children of the report and that its manifest entry lists under files: with their SHA-256 - the four pictures of the LLM Usage Report; a picture the report shows from a folder of its own is left out, and the report is then a difference. In every copy of the Prompt Builder report it resets the option defaults to the neutral values - no project ids, RAG and optimization off, Verify TLS certificates in manifested models on -, it removes the per-user states of the reports (each is a full copy of the report with a user id) and rewrites the exporting host to your-sas-viya-host, also inside the compressed report content. What would be written is compared with the checkout first; the command writes nothing and ends with exit code 1 - the file from before stays byte for byte - when a difference is left, when the package still names a host, or when an object sits on a path that never ships. An export of another folder than the content root needs --out, and --allow-differences, with --out only, writes the export of a test folder that holds no report; in such a folder mdb content-deploy writes that folder into the contentRoot of the job definitions and brings no report, so that contentRoot and the reports that are not there stay differences however often it runs, and the line of the differences says so; the last line of such an export says to keep that file out of the repository and names the command that brings it into a test folder - mdb builders-import <file> --content-root "<folder>" --no-releases --no-reports --no-decisions --create --no-files: the files, custom steps and job definitions into a test folder, which it creates where it is not there, and no report, no decision, no release table and no commands file. The export replaces the user ids in createdBy, modifiedBy and userName - of the package, the summaries, the bodies (userName stands in the body of a folder) and the report wrappers - with sas-agentic-ai-accelerator and prints whose ids it replaced; --keep-user-ids, with --out only, leaves them and says so. contentSourceLocation, the path of the exported folder, and the contentRoot of the job definitions stay, and the summary line names both; mdb reads contentSourceLocation to refuse a package of a nested folder. For the content root of the release it names no one; the export of a folder below /Users/<user id> carries that id in these paths and in the contentRoot of its job definitions, so the release file is written from the content root of the release only, also when --out names it. The export deletes its package and the record of its export job on the server; if a delete is refused or gets no answer, the file is still written and checked, a line names what is left and how to delete it, and the command ends with exit code 3. What the transfer service does with neutral user fields on an import of the reports has not been measured. (In Git Bash on Windows prefix a command that names a content folder with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, or run it from PowerShell: the shell otherwise rewrites the /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator/... argument into a Windows path before mdb sees it.) Measured on 2026-10-12 on the test content root: without the two reports in the folder the export ended with exit code 1 and wrote no file; with --allow-differences it wrote 71 objects and left nine out - the five objects of the folder the manifest does not list and the four folders above the content root, each as (not below the content root) -, and no rule came with the export of that folder. The file held nothing outside the manifest, no host, no rule and no share, and the user id of the exporter 215 times. With copies of the two reports of the test system in the folder the export went through without --allow-differences: nine option defaults reset, the host replaced in four places, 77 objects, four of them the pictures of the usage report. In the second pass of 2026-10-12 the export of a test root without the reports ended the same way, and with --allow-differences wrote 71 objects and named the user id of the exporter in 298 places; it deleted its package (HTTP 204) and left the record of the export job, which it deletes since. In the third pass, on 2026-10-13, the export of a test root with --allow-differences ended with exit code 0, the DELETE of its package and of the record of its export job were each answered 204, and the counts of both on the server were what they were before it. All 143 createdBy and 143 modifiedBy of the file were sas-agentic-ai-accelerator. The 12 userName of the folder bodies still held the id of the exporter: the export printed left as the export wrote them (--keep-user-ids) without that option and no Replaced the user id(s) line, and mdb package-check failed the file in both forms with names the user id(s) .... userName is one of the fields the export replaces since then: in the second and in the third pass of 2026-10-13 the export of a test root printed Replaced the user id(s) <id> in createdBy / modifiedBy / userName with 'sas-agentic-ai-accelerator' (298 place(s)), and its file held that text in all 143 createdBy, 143 modifiedBy and 12 userName. In the third pass the command the export printed for a test folder - without --create then - created the 70 entries of that file in a second test root, in place and without a request to the transfer service. Not measured: an export of the content folder itself, whether it brings rules, a delete that is refused, and exit code 3. mdb package-check is the same comparison on the file in the repository, and a step of the workflow verify-model-definitions.yml. Every entry of the manifest has to be in the package, once, and equal its source - a file its repository file, line ends aside; a generated file what mdb generates now, release.json by its kind, its release, its commit and its entries; a custom step the .step file in templates, ui and flowMetadata; a job definition its program, its form and its parameters. Nothing else may be in the package, there may be no authorization rule and no share, and a report must name no host, carry no per-user state and pass the checks of its entry: for the Prompt Builder report every option the UI reads with its neutral default, for both reports the CAS tables they bind, and the files that are its children by name and hash. One line per difference. --fix rewrites hosts, states, option defaults and the user ids in createdBy, modifiedBy and userName in the file; a difference in content is fixed in the folder, with mdb content-deploy, and by exporting again. Not compared, by decision: a description and the fields the service derives for display, ids, links, users and time stamps, and a line end. Measured on 2026-10-12 on packages exported from the test content root: for the export without the reports the command printed the two lines that say so and ended with exit code 1; for the export with copies of the two reports, every entry of the manifest is in the package and equals the checkout, exit code 0; and for an export after a file, a custom step and a job definition were changed by hand it named six differences - the ui of the step, the file with its two sizes, code and parameters of the job definition, and the two reports. The package that passed held the four pictures of the usage report, which the command of that day did not look at. In the second pass of 2026-10-12 the lenient form printed the parameters of the two job definitions of an export without reports as drift: lines and the two reports as errors (exit code 1), --release printed the four without drift: (exit code 1), and a file changed by hand in the root was drift: ... (76 vs 1020 bytes) in the lenient form and an error with --release. In the third pass, on 2026-10-13, both forms were run on the export of a test root and on copies of it in which only the commit and the date of release.json were changed: the commit of the checkout and an ancestor with its own date gave no line; a commit of another line of history gave not in the history of this checkout (the clone holds it on another line of history) and 40 digits of no commit which this clone does not hold, each a drift: line in the lenient form and an error with --release; a text that is no commit id and a date that is not the commit's were errors in both forms. Every one of these runs ended with exit code 1: the file named the user id in userName (above) and held no report.
documents.s: The content folder: deploy, export, check

documents.t: The content folder holds one decision, Decisions/Call LLM Node. It holds nothing but the Call LLM node and is not meant to be published: it is how the package brings that custom node type to a site under one id, f9efcbb7-f57b-4a62-b56d-1a89595e2039 - The Call LLM node and its id says why. Its manifest entry is of the kind decision and lists the node types it uses with their ids (nodeTypes:), and for the Call LLM node the program that writes its code and its terms (content:, the Update program); like a report, the decision has no source in the repository. mdb package-export keeps the decision and the node type the export carries as its dependency, when the id is one the entry lists, and drops the authorization rule on the node type. mdb package-check fails a package whose decision uses a node type its entry does not list, whose node type is missing or has another id or name, or no code, or code and terms other than those of the program its entry names - the import would give every site that code -, or whose step names no node type (a node type that was deleted where the package was exported). mdb content-deploy does not deploy the decision. Its line says not deployed ... (on the site) or (not on the site - it comes with the package), as for a report. mdb builders-import imports the decisions and the node types they use through the transfer service, in an import job of their own after the reports. It asks the site first. A node type of that id on the site is overwritten in place: local edits of its code and its terms are replaced, and the line says so. One that is not there is created under the id. Where a Call LLM node is there under another id, the command uploads nothing of the decisions, names mdb decision-node-migrate and ends with exit code 1 - unless --no-decisions leaves the decisions out. With another --content-root the decisions are refused like the reports, and the command it names to run again adds --no-decisions. Decisions that are not imported get no folder in place either. A site without SAS Intelligent Decisioning gets a line and no failure. The tasks of the job are read, and a decision or node type without a completed task counts as not imported.
documents.s: The decision that carries the Call LLM node

documents.t: mdb decision-node-migrate is the migration that The Call LLM node and its id describes - what it does to a site, and why a node that a decision uses is never deleted. What the command takes and says: Without --apply it only reads: it finds the node type by its name (--node-name, default Call LLM), refuses where another node type has the id (--target-id, default the shipped one), and lists every decision version that calls the node type, locked versions included - each version of each decision is read, which takes about two minutes for 250 decisions. Every run also lists each node type like the one of the id with the versions that call it. A copy has its code - line ends aside - or the (before f9efcbb7) name a run gives the old node type; a run with --apply that leaves decisions on a copy ends with exit code 1. A node type whose name alone starts with the name of the node, in any case, and whose code is another - a node renamed by hand from an older release, or another node such as Call LLM Streaming - is a warning only. Where the node type of the id is there, --from-id <id> moves the decisions of one of them to it and creates and renames nothing; it warns where that node type is no copy. Versions whose node lost its address - a node type deleted earlier - are a warning of the dry run and of the run: they cannot run, and no mapping moves them. --delete-old, with --apply, deletes the old node type at the end, and only when a fresh look finds no version that calls it. A --from-id node type that is no copy is kept: its decisions are moved, the line says why it is not deleted, and you delete it in SAS Intelligent Decisioning once you are sure. SAS Intelligent Decisioning does not say how many node types there are. The command reads up to 1000, and warns that the list may be incomplete when all 1000 come back. So does mdb builders-import. A site without SAS Intelligent Decisioning gets one line and exit code 0. A refusal or a failure ends with exit code 1; an id that is no UUID, and a --from-id that is the --target-id, end with exit code 2 before the sign-in. A run that stopped is run again: what was done is found done. Measured on SAS Viya 2026.09 on 2026-10-20 with a throwaway node type and a decision with a locked version 1.0 and a current 2.0: the dry run listed both versions and changed nothing; --apply renamed, created and moved, and both versions then called the new node type and ran with its code; a second run found nothing to do; --delete-old deleted the old node type, and both versions still ran. Measured on 2026-10-21 as a dry run on the test system, where the node type of the id is there: it read 245 decisions, found no node type like it, named the two versions whose node type had been deleted, and sent GET requests only. Measured on 2026-10-21 on the test system with two throwaway node types, each called by a decision with a locked version 1.0 and a current 2.0: one with the code of the Call LLM node under another name, and one named like it with other code. The dry run listed the first as a copy and the second as a name alone, each with its decision and both versions. --from-id --apply --delete-old moved both versions of each decision to the node type of the id. It deleted the copy and kept the other node type, with the line that says so.
documents.s: Moving the Call LLM node to its id

documents.t: mdb content-deploy --only <path of the manifest> --to <target> deploys one part of the manifest to another place than its own in the content root. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-12 with the command as it was then: a step of a test folder changed by hand was updated ... (ui; id <its id> kept) in the dry run (GET only) and in the run (one PUT), --to <its id> then said equal, a --to that names nothing ended with Nothing was updated. and exit code 1, and --only RAG --to <folder> created the 41 entries directly in that folder. Measured in the third pass, on 2026-10-13: --to <id of a step of another name> ended with --to <id> names the registered step '<its name>' in <its folder>, not '<the name of the entry>': nothing was written - pass --force ..., Nothing was updated. and exit code 1, with GET requests only - GET /folders/ancestors was answered 200 and named the folder; with --force the step was updated with its id kept, and the line named the step and its folder; --to <path> of a step of the entry's name said equal ... - the registered step '<name>' in <folder>; --only RAG --to <a folder that is not there> ended with there is no folder ...: pass --create, exit code 1 and no write, and with --create - for a folder of another name - 41 entries: 41 created. --only Data --to <root>/Data --create wrote the content root of the manifest into the job definition of that folder. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-13 with the command as it is since then (below): --only Data --to <root>/Data --create wrote <root> there, --to <root>/zz_loader/Data --create wrote <root>/zz_loader, and --to <root>/zz_tables ended with exit code 2 without a sign-in. Measured in the third pass of 2026-10-13: two custom steps that had been registered in a folder of their own from the files of the build before were updated ... (templates, ui; id <its id> kept ...) with --only "Custom Steps/<step>" --to <path>, one PUT each, and a dry run behind it said equal. A custom step, a file or a job definition a site has somewhere else. A site whose flows use a step it registered in a folder of its own has that step under an id the flows reference, and neither mdb builders-import nor a deploy of the content folder touches it. --to takes the SAS Content path, the id or the URI of that object and updates it in place from the checkout: mdb content-deploy --only "Logging and Monitoring/LLM - Log Parser.step" --to "/SAS Agentic AI Accelerator/Custom Steps/LLM - Log Parser.step" --dry-run mdb content-deploy --only "Logging and Monitoring/LLM - Log Parser.step" --to "/SAS Agentic AI Accelerator/Custom Steps/LLM - Log Parser.step" The object keeps its id and its name. It is updated and never created, no folder is made, and the content root is not looked at; where the target is not there the command says Nothing was updated. and ends with exit code 1. A report is refused. With an id or a URI the object is read for its name and its folder is asked for (GET /folders/ancestors), and the line ends with - the registered step '<name>' in <folder>. An object whose name is not the entry's is refused unless --force: --to X names the registered step 'Y' in /F, not 'E': nothing was written - pass --force to update it all the same. A path that names the object and a reference of its name is refused: name the object by its id. --only release.json --to is refused: release.json is the record of a whole folder. A folder of the manifest, into a folder of another name. mdb content-deploy --only RAG --to "<your RAG content root>" deploys the entries below RAG directly into that folder - rag_core/, steps/, jobs/, models/ -, for a site whose option RAG: content root is not /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator/RAG. That folder is created only with --create. deploy-rag-content.ps1 -ContentRoot / .sh -r run this command, and -Create / -c pass --create on. A folder with a job definition that reads the content root - Data, with Load-Accelerator-Tables - goes to that folder of a content root: --only Data --to "<root>/Data" writes <root> into contentRoot, and a target that does not end with /Data ends the command with exit code 2 before it signs in.

The package is exported from a system, so between two exports it holds the content of an earlier commit: a changelog entry, a fact sheet row or a fix to a program makes it differ from the checkout until a maintainer exports again. The gate therefore has two forms: mdb package-check, which the workflow runs on a branch and for a pull request. A difference in content against the checkout - a file, a custom step, a job definition, the release table, release.json - is printed as drift: <file>: <what differs> and does not fail. What a package must never be fails: an object the manifest does not list or that is in the package twice, an authorization rule, a share, a host in a report or in what an object says about itself (its summary, description or links), a connector other than the parentFolder of a file, step, job definition or folder, a substitution, a user id in createdBy, modifiedBy or userName (--fix rewrites it), a per-user state, a report default that is not neutral, a release.json whose commit is no commit id in full (40 hexadecimal digits, 64 in a SHA-256 repository; an abbreviation is none, and neither is an id with a blank or a line break around it) or is the id of a tag, a tree or the content of a file in the clone, an entry of the manifest that is missing, a path that never ships - a folder whose name holds generated among them -, a property or a field nothing in the checkout gives it. A host inside a form, a program or a file is content and a drift: line; the workflow therefore runs --release as well on a branch whose change replaces the package file. --allow-missing is honoured only while a package file of an earlier release is still in SAS-Viya-Integrations/. mdb package-check --release, which the release procedure runs after the export and the workflow runs for a version tag. Every difference is an error, also a release, a commit or a hash in release.json that is not the one of the checkout; --allow-missing has no effect with it, so a release cannot be tagged without the package. The commit of release.json passes only where it is HEAD or an ancestor of it. A commit the clone holds on another line of history (is not in the history of this checkout (the clone holds it on another line of history)), one it does not hold (which this clone does not hold - a commit of a branch that was squash-merged or deleted after the deploy ...) and an answer git cannot give are drift in the lenient form and errors here; a text that is no commit id in full, and a date that is not the commit's, fail both forms. --base <commit> asks the same of the history of that commit, which the workflow gives for a pull request that replaces the package: it is checked on the merge of its branch, which still holds the commits of the branch, so a package deployed from one of them passes there without --base and fails on main after the squash merge (names the commit ..., which is not in the history of <base> ... - a commit of the branch of this pull request, which the squash merge does not keep ...). Without --release, and for a name the clone holds no commit of, --base ends with exit code 2 before anything is checked. A contributor who changes a file the package holds a copy of sees drift: lines in the log of the workflow and a check that passes, and does nothing about them; a contributor who adds, moves or removes an object of the content folder lists it in the manifest, and the check then fails with ... is in the manifest but not in the package until a maintainer has exported again. CONTRIBUTING.md has this for contributors. Lines of the gate that are new with these checks: ... is in the package 2 times - one path holds one object; file '<name>' belongs to report '<path>' and is not among the files its manifest entry lists; file '<name>' of report '<path>' is not the file its manifest entry lists (SHA-256 ...); job definition '<path>' carries 2 'form' properties ...; step '<path>' carries 'properties' the .step file does not have; file 'release.json' names release '<v>', this checkout is <v>; ... names the commit <12 hex>, which is not in the history of this checkout. Neither form has run in the workflow. --release ran on two exports of a test root in the second pass of 2026-10-12 and on one in the third, not on an export of the content folder.
documents.s: The gate between two releases, and for a release

documents.t: The package is built on the system whose content folder holds the two reports. Two commits matter, and both are commits of main: the one the folder is deployed from, which release.json names, and the one the tag names. mdb package-check --release - on your machine, for the pull request of the package and for the tag - accepts only a release.json whose commit is the checked-out commit or one it descends from. Where main only takes squash-merged pull requests, this is the order: Squash-merge the release work with its final texts, then check out the commit that merge made on main: git fetch origin, git switch --detach origin/main. Final means CHANGELOG.md with the date of the release - and for release 2.3.0 without the sentences that say the package file is not in the repository yet - and everything the manifest names as a source. The release table in the package is made from the changelog, so a change to it after the export makes the gate fail until the folder is deployed and exported again. Do not deploy from a commit of a branch, also not from the branch of this pull request before it is merged: the squash makes a new commit on main, your clone holds the commit of the branch on another line of history (is not in the history of this checkout (the clone holds it on another line of history)), and the fresh clone of the workflow of the tag does not hold it at all (which this clone does not hold - ...). mdb content-deploy --dry-run, then mdb content-deploy: the folder holds the files, the custom steps and the job definitions of the checkout, each under the id it had. Read the list under Not in the manifest and left alone - it is what the export will drop. Run it again; every line says equal. A run that stops at a write that failed says what it wrote; nothing was removed, and the next run goes on from there. The reports. In SAS Visual Analytics, open the Prompt Builder report and save it once if the UI of the release has an option the report does not hold yet - the export refuses a report that lacks one. The pictures of the LLM Usage Report are listed in the manifest with their hashes: if one was replaced, the export says file '<name>' of report ... is not the file its manifest entry lists (SHA-256 <hash>) - put that hash into the entry, bring that change to main the way of step 1, and start again at step 2, because release.json names the commit. mdb package-export writes SAS-Viya-Integrations/SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json, or prints one line per difference and leaves the file as it was. The package of a release holds the defaults of the two settings of a site: a job definition of the folder whose _contextName is not SAS Studio compute context is named as a difference - set it with mdb content-deploy --compute-context "SAS Studio compute context" for the export. The command replaces the user ids in createdBy, modifiedBy and userName and prints whose ids it replaced; its last line says what the commit of the file holds and which commit is tagged. mdb package-check --release ends with exit code 0. The package file goes into a second pull request, from a branch that starts at the commit of step 1 (git switch -c release/package). It changes neither CHANGELOG.md nor a source the manifest names. For release 2.3.0 the same commit removes the four packages of earlier releases - SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator-Prompt-Builder.json, SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator-RAG-Builder.json, SAS Agentic AI Accelerator.json and Logging-Monitoring/LLM Usage Report.json - and takes --allow-missing out of the workflow; the sentences outside the changelog that say the package is not there yet (Deploying the Builder UIs, this page, the README of SAS-Viya-Integrations) can go with it, since none of them is a source of the manifest. The workflow runs mdb package-check --release --base <the base of the pull request> on this pull request. Squash-merge it. A test of mdb fails while the one package and one of the four earlier files are in the repository together. Tag the commit that merge made on main - git fetch origin, then git tag 2.3.0 origin/main while nothing else was merged - not the commit of your branch that added the file: after a squash merge that commit is not on main. A pull request merged between step 1 and the tag has to leave the changelog and every source of the manifest alone. For a version tag the workflow first asks git whether the commit of the tag is in the history of main (git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main) and fails if it is not; then it runs mdb package-check --release, where a missing package fails as well; mdb no longer honours --allow-missing once the four earlier files are gone. A maintainer who commits to main directly follows the same order with commits in place of the two pull requests. None of this has run on a real content folder: the deploy, the export and the gate were measured on test content roots, and steps 2, 4 and 5 run code that was written after the last pass. The order of the commits was followed in scratch git repositories with the gate at each place the workflow runs it - the pull request of the package, main after its merge, a fresh clone of the tag -, and the question the workflow asks git for a tag was asked there as a command; no GitHub workflow has run with it.

mdb deploy <model_id> --registry myregistry.azurecr.io renders ready-to-apply Kubernetes YAML from the SCR-LLM-Deployment-YAML templates with every placeholder filled (resource names, image, ingress host and path) — the persistent-volume variant is selected automatically for self-hosted models. --namespace (default llm) sets the namespace of the Deployment, Service and Ingress, and --tls-secret (default llm-tls-certs) the TLS secret the Ingress serves its host with.
