A retrieval model that is already registered keeps its constant until Manifest setup runs again, and RAGEMBED_SSLVERIFY=true and RAGSTORE_SSLVERIFY=true on a destination turn verification back on for a model manifested without it. While the option is not ticked, the step shows a warning at Manifest setup before the click, and the model it registers carries the tag TLS-Verification-Off in SAS Model Manager — Deployment of Decisions shows how to list such models. Manifesting the setup again with the option ticked writes SSL_VERIFY = True and removes the tag. The tag follows the score code the model holds: when SAS Model Manager refuses retrieve_context.py, the manifest stops at that stage with the HTTP status and leaves the score code and the tags as they were, and a tag that could not be written or removed is named in the outcome beside the button. When the upload of retrieve_context.py gets no usable answer — the connection drops, or an ingress answers with its error page — the page reads the file back: when the setup holds it, the manifest goes on; when it does not, the manifest stops at that stage and says so. Only when it cannot be read back either does the manifest stop with it is not known whether SAS Model Manager stored retrieve_context.py, leaving the tag as it was; until Manifest setup has run through again, the tag may then not match the SSL_VERIFY line the model holds. This was driven against a stand-in for SAS Viya, not against SAS Viya. What the option does not touch: The ingestion job, the generated flow and Test retrieval. They run in a compute session, where the bundle is mounted, and verify as before. The connection to the vector store. Its TLS is the option RAG: vector store TLS (storeSslmode) and the sslmode of the store. A model registered with the custom step RAG - Register Setup. The step does not read the options of the Prompt Builder object. It has a checkbox of its own for the same setting — see the checkbox of the custom step. A template deployed before release 2.3.0. The retrieve_context.py under <content root>/models then has no SSL_VERIFY constant. Manifest setup succeeds with it, and the model verifies whatever the option says. With the option not ticked, the outcome beside the button says that verification is still ON and that the template has to be deployed again, and the model is not tagged. Run deploy-rag-content to publish the current retrieve_context.py: the next Manifest setup writes SSL_VERIFY = False and tags the model. Switching verification off is for a destination that runs Python where the bundle is not mounted — the case found with SAS Micro Analytic Service, which Deployment of Decisions describes together with the mount that keeps verification on. That mount is the fix for production; verification off is for a test system on a closed cluster network. The mount was measured there with a decision template, and with a prompt template with the included LLM call. A retrieval model was published there after the mount as well. Without the credentials of the vector store it answered no vector-store credentials resolved; with them passed in options it returned chunks, with SSL_VERIFY = True in its score code — see the retrieval model in a decision. The call to the credentials service is not made when the credentials come with the call or from the environment — the two cases that were run — so the verification of that one call in SAS Micro Analytic Service is not measured. Both Launch ingestion and Test retrieval need the ingestion compute context option (ragComputeContext) to be set — SAS Job Execution rejects a job that does not name one, and the rejection carries no log. The Builder checks first and names the missing setting. The optimization compute context of the same Options pane does not count: it is a different option, for a different job.
documents.s: TLS verification in the retrieval model

documents.t: The custom step RAG - Register Setup registers the same retrieve_context.py from SAS Studio. It does not read the options of the Prompt Builder object; its Runtime section has the checkbox Verify TLS certificates in the registered retrieval model (_rgrg_sslVerify), ticked by default: The checkbox The registered model holds The tag TLS-Verification-Off What the step says ticked SSL_VERIFY = True not set, and removed from a model that carried it TLS certificate verification on in the summary of its log and in the registration report not ticked SSL_VERIFY = False set WARNING lines at the end of its log, and TLS certificate verification OFF in the registration report The warning. With the box not ticked, the log of the step ends with WARNING lines: the retrieval model does not verify the certificates of its two HTTPS calls — to the embedding container and to the credentials service — and RAGEMBED_SSLVERIFY=true and RAGSTORE_SSLVERIFY=true on the publishing destination turn verification back on. The registration report, the output table of the step, shows the state in the Detail column of the row of the model. The tag follows the score code that is stored. It is set or removed after retrieve_context.py has been stored on the model, so a registration that fails at that upload leaves the tag as it was — also when the model could not be read before the upload: the tag is then kept as the listing of the models shows it. Where the listing does not show the tags of the model either, nothing says whether it carries the tag, and the step writes it: a tag too many is put right by the next registration that goes through, a model that does not verify and is not tagged is found by nobody. When the upload then fails, the model carries a tag this run put there, and the log says so in WARNING lines of its own (the model could not be read before this run updated it …); that case was checked with the test suite and not run in SAS, and neither were the WARNING lines for a tag that could not be written or removed and for an upload without a usable answer. When the tag itself cannot be updated, the registration still goes through, and a WARNING says which way the tag is wrong: it could not be written to a model that does not verify, or could not be removed from one that does. A run that fails after the score code is stored. The step does more after the upload: it attaches the other artifacts and, when a flow is named under Studio Flow to generate the scheduled job from, generates the job. When one of these fails — the flow does not exist, say — the step ends with its ERROR, and the model in SAS Model Manager holds the new score code all the same. The log of the failing run then says so below the ERROR line, the step failed after the score code of the retrieval model was stored, followed by the same WARNING lines as a run that went through: that the model does not verify, and whether it carries the tag. An upload of the score code without a usable answer. When the connection drops, the request times out, or an ingress answers with a page of its own, the step cannot know whether SAS Model Manager stored the file. It reads nothing back. It ends with its ERROR and two WARNING lines: it is not known whether SAS Model Manager stored the score code retrieve_context.py, and the tag TLS-Verification-Off was not updated and may not say what the stored score code does. Run this step again. The Builder words the same case the same way beside Manifest setup. On a model whose tag the run wrote before the upload without knowing whether the model carried it (the bullet above), the second line says was not updated after the upload, as rag_core does, and the three lines about the tag written unseen follow; up to this change the step said there that the tag was not updated and, two lines on, that the run had written it. That wording was not run in SAS. An upload SAS Model Manager refuses with an answer of its own is certain: nothing was stored, and the model keeps the score code it had. It keeps the tag it had as well, with the one exception of the bullet above: a model that could not be read and whose tags the listing did not show got the tag before the upload, and carries it. The job generated from a flow. With a flow named under Studio Flow to generate the scheduled job from, the step creates the job definition RAG Ingest - <setup> from the code SAS Studio generates for the flow. Up to release 2.2 the job was that code unchanged, so a failing step ran abort 42 as it does in an interactive flow — which in a job ends the session before SAS Job Execution gets its completion handshake. The job now begins with %let RAG_ABORT_ON_ERROR = 0; and %let RAG_JOB_FAILED = 0; and ends with a check that writes ERROR: RAG ingestion failed - a step of this run reported an error (its ERROR line is above) and the steps after it were skipped. and sets SYSCC when a step failed. The check reads RAG_JOB_FAILED, which every failing RAG step sets and no step clears; RAG_PIPELINE_FAILED is no use for it, because RAG - List Documents, RAG - Purge Documents and RAG - Retrieve Context clear it when they start. Both parts are added by the step and are not part of the flow: a job that SAS Studio itself deploys from the flow does not have them, and running the step again puts them back. Measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09, with two jobs the step generated from a flow of List, Extract, Chunk, Embed and Load (pgvector), run in SAS Job Execution: the job in which RAG - List Documents failed ended as failed after 31 seconds, with the ERROR line of the step and the line of the check in its log and the four steps after it skipped; the job without a failure ended as completed. Not measured: the job that does not end, which the change is made to prevent, was not reproduced; a step other than RAG - List Documents that fails; a flow with a second chain or with a RAG - Retrieve Context node, and with it that RAG_JOB_FAILED rather than RAG_PIPELINE_FAILED is what fails the job — both flags were set in the measured flow. The About tabs of the eight other steps name the flag and claim no measurement for it. A template deployed before release 2.3.0. rag_core writes the line under the rule of the Builder: only where the MANIFEST block of the template has SSL_VERIFY. With an older template and the box not ticked, the step registers a model that still verifies, does not tag it, and warns that TLS certificate verification is still ON and that the RAG content has to be deployed again. Run deploy-rag-content, then the step once more. A flow that hands the step no value for the checkbox registers with verification on: a missing or blank value is read as ticked. Not ticked is a value that reads as the number zero — 0, which is what SAS Studio hands over for a box that is not ticked, and equally 0.0, 00 or -0 — or the word false or no, in any case. Every other value, an unknown word included, is read as ticked. The checkbox changes the registered model and nothing else. The step itself, the other eight RAG steps and the ingestion job run in a compute session and verify the HTTPS calls they make themselves — to SAS Viya and to the embedding container — with the CA bundle of that session (SSLCALISTLOC, else CAS_CLIENT_SSL_CA_LIST, else the certificates Python trusts); none of them has a control or reads an environment variable that switches that off. A prompt that RAG - Enrich Chunks runs is a manifested model with the default it was manifested with. The connection to the vector store is a database connection: its TLS is the SSL mode (PostgreSQL) or TLS (SingleStore) control of the steps that connect to it, and for the registered model the SSL mode of this step. The step and rag_core reach a site with the transfer package, or from a checkout with deploy-rag-content. The step was run in SAS Studio on 2026-10-11, on SAS Viya 2026.09, as the last of a flow of six steps — List, Extract, Chunk, Embed, Load, Register Setup. The flow was created without a value for the checkbox, which is what a flow saved before the control existed hands the step: The checkbox shows in the Runtime section, ticked. Run that way, the step ended green and its log said retrieval model: TLS certificate verification on. The score code of the model held SSL_VERIFY = True, and the model carried the tags LLM, RAG, all_minilm_l6_v2 and pgvector. With the box not ticked, the node of the step showed a warning badge in the flow. The log said retrieval model: TLS certificate verification OFF (tag TLS-Verification-Off) and held the WARNING lines, the score code held SSL_VERIFY = False, and the model carried TLS-Verification-Off beside the four tags. With the box ticked again, the score code held SSL_VERIFY = True, the tag was gone and the four tags were kept. With a retrieve_context.py without the SSL_VERIFY line under <content root>/models and the box not ticked, the log held three WARNING lines (verification still ON, the content predates the setting, deploy the RAG content again), the Detail of the report said TLS certificate verification still ON - the retrieval model template predates the setting …, the model was not tagged, and the score code held no SSL_VERIFY line. Not measured: a job generated from a flow that contains the step, and a retrieval model registered by the step running inside a decision or in SAS Micro Analytic Service. The WARNING lines of a run that fails after the upload were added after these runs and measured later the same day, with the step run as the code SAS Studio generates for a flow, in a compute session of the SAS Studio compute context and not clicked in SAS Studio: Box ticked, no flow named. The run ended with condition code 0 and no WARNING line. Its log said retrieval model: TLS certificate verification on and no flow selected, so no scheduled job was generated; the model held SSL_VERIFY = True, no tag TLS-Verification-Off, and its nine variables with the lengths of the table below. Box not ticked, and a flow that does not exist. The log held, in this order: the ERROR line of the step (no flow named …), the WARNING that the step failed after the score code of the retrieval model was stored, the three WARNING lines about a model that does not verify, the WARNING that the model carries the tag TLS-Verification-Off, and the ERROR of the abort. The same model then held SSL_VERIFY = False and the tag. The log held no Apparent symbolic reference line and no NOTE about a quoted string. Not run in SAS: the WARNING lines of an upload without a usable answer, of a tag that could not be written or removed, and of a tag written to a model that could not be read. Each needs a fault of SAS Model Manager — a model it does not return while its listing shows no tags, an upload it does not answer — and not a state a model of the test can be put in. The runs of 2026-10-11 with the steps of release 2.3.0 could not stage them either, and the logs of the two runs of the step made that day hold none of these lines. The test suite of rag_core runs the Python of the step for these cases and pins the SAS text. Two more things came out of those runs. Both are changed in this release, and both were measured afterwards on the same system: A SAS Model Manager project that does not exist yet. The step names the project the model is registered in (RAG Engineering unless changed) and creates it when it is missing. With a new name it stopped with POST /modelRepository/projects returned 400 … You must specify a value for the "folderId" parameter: the service places a project in a folder, and the request named the repository only. rag_core now creates the project in the default repository of SAS Model Manager — the one marked as default among the first 100 it lists, else the first of them — and sends the folder of that repository with the request; the same request with the folder added was answered 201 on that system. A repository that names no folder ends in a message that says so. To have the project in another repository, create it there in SAS Model Manager first: a project that exists is used as it is. Measured with a project name that did not exist: the step ended green, the project was created in the repository marked as default (Public on that system) with the folder of that repository and the tags LLM and RAG-Engineering, and the retrieval model was registered in it. A NOTE above the summary. Every run wrote NOTE: The quoted string currently being processed has become more than 262 bytes long. You might have unbalanced quotation marks. twice, above the summary of its log. The cause as it was read from the code: the summary was written into the program inside two quoted strings, and SAS writes that NOTE for a quoted string of more than 262 bytes. The same two strings stood in all nine RAG steps since release 2.0.0. The steps now read the summary with symget. The file of the step held one more pair of strings of that length, two docstrings of its Python program; nothing in the code suggests that SAS counts those, and they were shortened as well. Measured for RAG - Register Setup: the log of a run of the new step goes from %_rgrg_status; straight to NOTE: ----- RAG - Register Setup -----, with 0 errors and 0 warnings, and the two NOTE lines every earlier run had are gone. Which of the two changes removed them was not separated. The other eight steps got the same change. Measured later the same day with SingleStore: the log of a flow of List, Extract, Chunk, Embed and Load held no such NOTE. The logs of RAG - Enrich Chunks, RAG - Purge Documents and RAG - Retrieve Context were not read for it. The same NOTE above an ERROR line. A step that fails wrote its message, up to 500 characters, into one quoted string as well. Seen on 2026-10-11: a failing RAG - List Documents wrote the NOTE directly above ERROR: RAG - List Documents failed: …. The closing line of Ingest-Documents.sas was written the same way, and its message for a run lock that was not read back is longer than 262 bytes with any table name. The nine steps and the job now put that line together in a variable, its text read with symget, as the summary is. Measured on 2026-10-11 with a RAG - List Documents whose documents folder does not exist, run as a job and in a compute session: the line above the ERROR line was not the NOTE, and no log of that day's runs of the steps and of the job held the NOTE. The ERROR line had 311 characters. The log of that system is 132 characters wide, and this line, which the step writes with PUT, was cut there, inside a word and with no prefix on what follows: … { version :2, httpSta, then tusCode :404, …. A long NOTE milestone and the WARNING lines of the steps were broken at a blank before that column in the same logs. All three log lines of the message were of the type error, and so were the four of a 413-character ERROR line of the job. SAS Studio was not opened: that it shows such a line as an error is read from the type of the lines. A part of the summary longer than the log line. RAG - Register Setup printed the list of the artifacts it wrote as an empty NOTE: line followed by the text without the prefix (seen on 2026-10-11). A part of a summary is now written as one value with its NOTE: prefix, in all nine steps. Measured on 2026-10-11 for RAG - Register Setup without a flow: the line began NOTE: artifacts in … and went on in the next log line — the break stood inside a word, ingestio and n-manifest.json — with no empty NOTE: line before it.
documents.s: The checkbox of the custom step RAG - Register Setup

documents.t: A decision calls the retrieval model like any other Python model: inputs question, k, filter_json, retrieval_mode and options, outputs context_dg, context_envelope, retrieval_status and run_time. The model never raises. When it cannot retrieve, retrieval_status says why and the datagrid is empty — so a decision that uses the context should look at retrieval_status. Where a decision runs — the test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning, SAS Micro Analytic Service, a SAS Container Runtime container — there is no SAS Viya session, so the credential domain that serves the ingestion cannot be read there (Managing Credentials has the boundary). The model then needs the user and the password of the vector store from one of two places: From Names Environment variables of the runtime the Python runs in <BACKEND>_RAG_USER and <BACKEND>_RAG_PW — PGVECTOR_RAG_USER and PGVECTOR_RAG_PW for pgvector, SINGLESTORE_RAG_USER and SINGLESTORE_RAG_PW for SingleStore The options input of the call, a JSON object user and password — for a caller that manages its own secrets; a decision should not store them Host, port, database and SSL mode of the store, the embedding endpoint and the embedding model are in the model already, as they were manifested. A destination can override them with <BACKEND>_HOST, _PORT, _DB and _SSLMODE (or RAGSTORE_HOST, RAGSTORE_PORT, RAGSTORE_DB, RAGSTORE_SSLMODE for any backend), RAGEMBED_ENDPOINT and RAGEMBED_MODEL. An embedding model that calls a hosted API also needs its key: RAGEMBED_API_KEY, or API_KEY in options. The variables that decide TLS verification are in TLS verification in the retrieval model. Where the variables are set depends on the destination. For SAS Container Runtime they are part of the env of the container. For SAS Micro Analytic Service they belong to the container that runs the Python, which can be a separate runner — the variable and the Python runner shows the patch, with LLMCONTAINERPATH as its example. Measured for SAS Micro Analytic Service on 2026-10-11, with the two variables in a Kubernetes secret and set on every container of the deployment: kubectl -n <namespace> set env deployment/sas-microanalytic-score --containers=* --from=secret/<name> The pod restarts, and a call of the published decision with {} as the options of the retrieval model then returned retrieval_status ok and three hits. Which of the containers needs the variables was not separated. The command changes the running deployment only: it is not part of the manifests the deployment is applied from. Not measured: the same variables for the test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning, where it was not established where they have to be set, and for a SAS Container Runtime container. The Python packages the model imports have to be there too: requests, and psycopg2 or singlestoredb for the store. What was measured, on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09. One decision with three model nodes, all manifested in the Prompt Builder — the retrieval model of a RAG setup on pgvector, a prompt template with the included LLM call that is given the context_envelope of the retrieval, and a decision template — was tested in SAS Intelligent Decisioning and published to the SAS Micro Analytic Service destination maslocal. TLS verification was on in the score code of all three models. Without credentials for the vector store. All three nodes ran in both places; the publishing validation ended on three rows with HTTP status 201 and an empty error column. The prompt and the decision template answered. The retrieval model answered, in both places and with no chunk: retrieval failed: RuntimeError: no vector-store credentials resolved: pass user/password in options, grant a agentic-ai-keys credential holding PGVECTOR_RAG_USER/PGVECTOR_RAG_PW, or set those environment variables on the destination Neither runtime had the two variables, so this is the boundary above and the degradation the model is built for. What was measured is this status text; which requests the model made before it was not looked at. With the user and the password in options. Every row passed {"user": …, "password": …} in the options input of the retrieval model. In the test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning: 3 rows, retrieval_status ok after 0.2 to 0.7 seconds, three hits per row with the right document first, and envelopes of about 2,000 characters. The LLM answered from the context, and the decision template routed. An empty filter_json was accepted. Published to maslocal, called one row at a time: six single calls one after another each returned HTTP status 201, retrieval_status exactly ok, three hits, an envelope of 1969 characters and the answer of the LLM from the context. A whole call took 6.5 to 9 seconds. Published to maslocal, in a publishing validation with the same three rows: runs of the same validation gave different results. In one, all 3 rows returned retrieval_status ok, the envelopes, the answers of the LLM from the context (Last shuttle to the railway station departs at 19:10.) and the routes. In others, rows came back with HTTP status 201, an empty error column and every output of all three nodes empty — all three rows in one run, two of the three in the next run of the same module with the same table. SAS Micro Analytic Service had ended those executions after 30 seconds: the validation sends its rows at the same time, and the LLM and the decision model, both self-hosted on one CPU node, then took longer than that. Several rows at once has it. Direct calls of the published module without credentials, and with made-up ones, completed normally. To the made-up ones the database answered password authentication failed, so the PostgreSQL driver is there where SAS Micro Analytic Service runs the model on that system. With the user and the password as environment variables. With PGVECTOR_RAG_USER and PGVECTOR_RAG_PW set on the containers of the deployment sas-microanalytic-score (the command is above) and {} as options, a call returned retrieval_status ok and three hits. Not measured: the two environment variables for the test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning and for a SAS Container Runtime container; SingleStore; outputs longer than 32000 characters; and a retrieval model registered with RAG - Register Setup inside a decision. One more thing showed in the first of these tests. A decision hands a character input to a model padded with blanks to the length the variable is declared with: a question declared with 1000 characters arrived with about 900 trailing blanks in the test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning, and with one in SAS Micro Analytic Service. Up to release 2.2 the model returned the padded text as query in context_envelope — 1134 characters for a short question — and sent it to the embedding model as it was. From release 2.3.0 the model drops the blanks around the question before it embeds it and before it returns it. It treats the other inputs the same way: a filter_json of blanks only is no filter, a retrieval_mode of blanks only is the default mode, and a k of blanks only is the default number of chunks. A k that is no number at all falls back to the default as well and says so in retrieval_status — ok (k … is not a number - used 4) — where it failed the call before; a missing number and an infinity, also as the texts nan and inf, are the default without that note. A question of blanks only is still answered with question is empty. Measured with the model of release 2.3.0, on 2026-10-11: a question followed by 200 blanks arrived as 56 characters in query in SAS Micro Analytic Service, and in the test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning the three questions arrived with 103, 91 and 56 characters. A blank retrieval_mode, a k of 0, a missing k and a blank filter_json each gave retrieval_status exactly ok, in single calls of SAS Micro Analytic Service and in the test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning. The collection has three chunks, so these runs do not show that the default number of chunks was used: it cannot be told from 3. Not measured: a k that is no number.
documents.s: The retrieval model in a decision

documents.t: A decision that chains a retrieval model, an LLM and a decision model is as slow as its models are when they are called together, and SAS Micro Analytic Service ended an execution that took longer than 30 seconds (measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09). What comes back then does not say so: HTTP status 201, an empty error column and every output of every node empty. A direct REST call of the module answers "executionState": "timedOut" with "outputs": []. One call at a time Three rows at once (publishing validation) Retrieval node 0.2 s 0.2 to 2.2 s LLM node 1.3 to 4.2 s 5 to 6 s for the first row, more than 29 s for the two others Decision model node 1.7 to 4.1 s 24 to 25 s while the LLM container was busy A whole call 6.5 to 9 s all three rows empty in one run; one row complete after 29.65 s and two empty in the next The retrieval itself is the smallest part of it. What it adds is the prompt: with the retrieved context the prompt of the LLM was about 900 characters instead of about 50, and the LLM and the decision model were self-hosted on the same CPU node. The Troubleshooting Guide has how to recognise the case in the log of the service, the rest of what was measured and what a site can do: fewer calls at once, a faster model or models that do not share a node, a shorter prompt — a smaller k or smaller chunks. The lengths of the variables below have no part in it.

SAS Model Manager keeps a length for every variable of a model, and SAS Intelligent Decisioning declares the model in the code it generates for a decision with those lengths. The Prompt Builder writes every variable of the retrieval model with a length, and the custom step RAG - Register Setup registers the same ones: Variable Role Length question input 32000 k input 8 (a number) filter_json input 4000 retrieval_mode input 32 options input 4000 context_dg output 32000 context_envelope output 32000 retrieval_status output 512 run_time output 8 (a number) Up to release 2.2 the two did not agree. The Prompt Builder wrote context_dg and context_envelope without a length, for which SAS Model Manager stored 99, and the code of a decision then declared in_out varchar(100) "context_dg", in_out varchar(100) "context_envelope" The step registered the two context outputs with 32000 and its inputs shorter than the Builder's (4096, 1024, 16 and 2048). The lists are now the same, so that a model is the same model whichever of the two wrote its variables last, and a test of the repository compares them entry by entry. A value that is longer than its declared length arrives complete. That was measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09, as a control: with context_dg and context_envelope set back to 99 on the model — the generated code of the decision then declared in_out varchar(100) for both — and the decision published again, single calls of the published module in SAS Micro Analytic Service returned HTTP status 201, retrieval_status ok, the correct answer and context_envelope complete, with its 1969 characters. The test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning had returned the longer values complete with the length 99 as well. So a longer value neither failed the execution nor was it cut there, and the lengths above describe the model; nothing that was measured depends on them. The empty outputs of a publishing validation, which were first seen with a model that held 99, are another matter: the execution had taken longer than 30 seconds (several rows at once). What a site does. Nothing has to be repaired. A setup gets the lengths of this release the next time it is saved or manifested in the Prompt Builder of this release, which the upgrade asks for anyway; a published decision keeps the declaration it was published with until it is published again, and by the measurement above it runs the same with either. Measured on 2026-10-11 with the Prompt Builder page of this release, the bundle that ships: Manifest setup wrote question 32000, k 8, filter_json 4000, retrieval_mode 32, options 4000, context_dg 32000, context_envelope 32000, retrieval_status 512 and run_time 8. Measured earlier that day with the page as it was before eleven of its German texts were reworded: the same nine lengths, and the code SAS Intelligent Decisioning then generated for a decision declared varchar(32000) for both context outputs. Measured the same day for the step: a model that RAG - Register Setup registered held the same nine lengths in SAS Model Manager. The verify suite of the page checks the same against a stand-in for SAS Viya: a save writes the nine lengths, every update of the model during a manifest carries 32000 for both context outputs, and a manifest of a setup that held 99 leaves 32000. Not measured: a datagrid or an envelope longer than 32000 characters. Both hold the text of every hit, so their length grows with k and with the size of the chunks; three hits of the measured setup made 1969 characters. Also not measured: a value longer than its declared length for a model of another kind, in a SAS Container Runtime container, and a retrieval model registered with RAG - Register Setup with these lengths inside a decision.

Off by default. A chunk that reads perfectly in place is often meaningless on its own — "revenue grew 12%" says nothing about whose revenue, or when — and the published remedy is to prepend a short LLM-written statement situating it in its document, then embed the two together. The Builder's Enrichment section is that slot, and it is general: the same call can classify a chunk, pull out an effective date, or flag personal data. Which of those it does is decided by the prompt, not by the pipeline. The prompt is a Prompt Builder artifact, not a setting here. Build and evaluate it in the Prompt Builder, manifest it, and point the RAG setup at that Model Manager model. The prompt then has its own documentation, versions and permissions, and improving it does not mean editing a RAG setup. It must be manifested with the integrated LLM call. That option makes the score code perform the call and return the answer, which is what the ingestion reads. The other form returns llmBody/llmURL for the Call LLM node of SAS Intelligent Decisioning — the request to make rather than its result — and the Builder and the ingestion both refuse it by name. Only prompts manifested with output parsing are offered. Those are the ones whose answer is a set of named variables, which is exactly what this stage stores — the Prompt Builder tags them Output-Parsing when you manifest them that way. The project list is built from those prompts, so a prompt project holding none of them never appears rather than appearing and then being empty. If a prompt you expect is missing, re-manifest it with output parsing.
documents.s: Enrichment: an LLM call per chunk

documents.t: The stage is a list. Situating a chunk and extracting fields from it are different jobs, and one prompt asked to do both is worse at each — so Add another prompt runs a second, a third, over the same chunks, in the order shown. Each sees the chunk as the chunker produced it, not as the previous prompt left it. Two rules hold across the chain, and both are refused rather than resolved silently, in the Builder and again in the ingestion: Only one prompt may write the context header. A chunk has one, so a second would overwrite the first — after you had already paid for it, one LLM call per chunk. Two prompts may not store the same column, for the same reason and with no way to tell afterwards which prompt wrote what. enrich_version holds every prompt that contributed to a chunk, comma separated, so a chunk can say that its header came from one prompt and its clause_type from another. The cost is the obvious one: each prompt is its own LLM call per chunk, so two prompts cost twice as much as one. The run log prices each separately and rag_runs records the total. You choose, per prompt What it does Prompt project and prompt Which manifested prompt is called, once per chunk Prompt version Latest follows the prompt; a pinned version freezes exactly the prompt that version carried A chunk field for each prompt input What the prompt is given: the chunk, the whole document (capped at 20,000 characters), the neighbouring chunks, the heading path, the file name, the full source location, or the position ("chunk 3 of 42") The output stored as the context header Prepended to the chunk and embedded with it — this is the part that changes retrieval Outputs stored as columns Each becomes its own typed column on the chunk table, so it can be selected, filtered and aggregated Parallel calls How many chunks this prompt enriches at once — per prompt, because two prompts may call two different LLMs Nothing is guessed for a prompt input whose name is unfamiliar: a silently wrong mapping produces a whole corpus of confident nonsense, so the setup will not save until every input is mapped.
documents.s: Several prompts, one after the other

documents.t: A stored output is a real column, named after the output and typed from the prompt's registered output variables — a string becomes text, a decimal becomes a double, so a confidence score can be averaged rather than parsed out of a JSON blob. Retrieval returns them alongside the chunk. Three rules govern the schema, and all three are reported in the run log rather than applied quietly: A new column is not backfilled. Add an output to the prompt and the column appears on the next run, holding null for every chunk written before it. That is indistinguishable from an LLM that had nothing to say, so the log states it explicitly; only a full re-ingestion (bump the pipeline version) fills it in. A column you stop producing is not dropped. It keeps whatever the prompt that wrote it said. Removing data is never a side effect of editing a prompt. A name the table already uses is refused, by name, in the Builder and in the ingestion. score, content, page and rank are all plausible things to ask an LLM for and all belong to the chunk schema — rename the output in the prompt, or don't store it. The column is the output name in lower case. Both pgvector and SingleStore fold an unquoted identifier, so an output called Department becomes a department column. Nothing else about the name changes — a stored output is never prefixed or abbreviated.

Latest re-reads the prompt on every run, so improving it in the Prompt Builder changes what the next ingestion writes — without re-processing anything already stored. Pinning freezes a version, which is what you want once a corpus is in production and you want a prompt change to be a deliberate act. Either way, every enriched chunk records which prompt at which version wrote it in enrich_version, so a collection that legitimately holds work from two prompts can be read that way rather than merely being that way. Version labels (1.0, 1.1) are not unique — the Builder shows the date beside each and stores the version's id. A pinned version can lose its files A version's snapshot does not always keep its score code — an older model on our own environment returned its file listing but no content. Both the Builder and the ingestion refuse an empty prompt rather than running one, naming the version. If a pin stops working, pin a different version or return to Latest.

One LLM call per chunk, repeated on every re-chunk — this is normally the largest line in an ingestion, an order of magnitude above the embedding. It is priced in the run log while the run is happening, and recorded per run in rag_runs (enrich_calls, enrich_input_tokens, enrich_output_tokens, enrich_seconds, enrich_failed) so RAG_RUN_COST reports embedding and enrichment side by side with a total. A prompt manifested without the prompt_length and output_length outputs returns no token counts, and a token-priced model then has nothing to multiply. That reads as unknown rather than as zero — select those outputs when you manifest the prompt if you want the cost. On the benefit: the widely cited 35–49% reduction in retrieval failures comes from one vendor on one corpus, with a Claude-class model generating the headers, and the affordable price in that write-up depends on prompt caching over the parent document, which a self-hosted container does not have. Treat it as a technique to measure on your own corpus, not as a number to expect. The cheapest first check is Test retrieval, which shows the stored header beside each chunk once a collection has been enriched.
documents.s: What it costs, and what that buys

documents.t: Enrichment is deliberately NOT part of the drift fingerprint. Changing the prompt, the mapping or the stored outputs applies from the next run onward and never demands a re-ingest. The trade is explicit: a collection can hold headers written by two different prompt versions, and enrich_version on each chunk is what makes that visible. The drift guard still covers the chunker, the token window and the embedding model — the settings that change the vectors themselves and would make a collection unreadable. A hallucinated header is permanent and invisible at query time. It is baked into the vector and into the stored chunk. Read a few through Test retrieval before building a large corpus on a new prompt. Failure is per chunk. A call that fails, or a response that was not the JSON the prompt asked for, leaves that chunk without a header and it is embedded plain rather than failing the run. A parsed output is never stored from the prompt author's default value — a plausible answer no model generated is worse than none. The count is named in the run log and in the run summary, because a corpus where a tenth of the chunks have no header retrieves differently from one where all of them do. The prompt's score code is executed in the ingestion compute session, exactly as SAS Container Runtime would execute it. That is what scoring a model is; the control is Model Manager permissions on the prompt project. Do not point a setup at a model you would not run. A prompt calling a hosted LLM needs that provider's key in the same credential domain as the store credentials, under the provider's name (OpenAI, Anthropic, …). A prompt whose LLM runs as a local container takes no API key and needs nothing. The mapping from model to provider lives in rag_core/providers.py; a model missing from it fails at load with that said, rather than sending a wrong key on its behalf. In a SAS Studio flow the stage is the RAG - Enrich Chunks step, wired between Chunk Documents and Embed Chunks. The Builder adds one step per prompt to the generated flow, in order, and adds none at all for a setup that does not enrich. Chaining the step by hand does the same thing: each run adds to what the last one wrote rather than replacing it.
documents.s: Consequences worth knowing before you turn it on

documents.t: Both of these produce confusing failures if missed, so check them first.
documents.s: Two prerequisites that are not optional

documents.t: The steps create a CAS session in SAS and reuse it from Python, because the staged table has to be visible to the promote that follows. CAS only lets an identity reconnect to its own session. The stock SAS Job Execution compute context runs the server as a service account (sas-be-sa on a default deployment) while the CAS session belongs to the user who launched the job. The two do not match, and the first step fails. The step detects this and says so, but the fix is environmental: Run RAG flows and jobs in a context that runs as the requesting user. The SAS Studio compute context does; a full five-step ingestion is verified running there as a job. Submit with that context explicitly: { "arguments": { "_contextName": "SAS Studio compute context" } } For jobs launched from the Builder, that context is the option RAG: ingestion compute context (ragComputeContext) of the Prompt Builder object. It is deliberately not the option Optimization: compute context (computeContext): the prompt optimization job is commonly run in the stock context, which is exactly the one that does not work here. The same service-account mismatch also prevents credential-domain lookups, so one context change fixes both.
documents.s: 1. A compute context that runs as the requesting user

documents.t: Vector-store credentials come from a SAS Viya credential domain (default agentic-ai-keys), never from the flow. Entries are backend-prefixed so one domain can serve several stores: PGVECTOR_RAG_USER PGVECTOR_RAG_PW SINGLESTORE_RAG_USER SINGLESTORE_RAG_PW The same domain also carries where each store lives. These are not secrets, but the domain is the one place every identity can already read, so the Builder resolves the connection instead of asking users for a hostname they should never have to hold: PGVECTOR_HOST PGVECTOR_PORT PGVECTOR_DB PGVECTOR_SSLMODE SINGLESTORE_HOST SINGLESTORE_PORT SINGLESTORE_DB SINGLESTORE_SSLMODE RAGSTORE_HOST RAGSTORE_PORT RAGSTORE_DB RAGSTORE_SSLMODE RAGSTORE_* is the unprefixed fallback for any backend, the same precedence the runtime already applies to a .env. A value passed explicitly — a host typed into a step — still wins over the domain, so the steps are unaffected. Without <BACKEND>_HOST and <BACKEND>_DB the Builder shows the store as unresolved and refuses to save a setup that could not ingest. Author them with create-credential-domain.ps1/.sh, which reads your git-ignored .env. See Managing Credentials. Equip every identity that will run a flow or job — including the service account, if you are not using a run-as-requesting-user context.
documents.s: 2. A credential domain holding the store credentials

documents.t: rag_core cannot install anything: sas-pyconfig environments are read-only. The compute context's Python needs: Package Needed for requests, pandas, swat Always psycopg2-binary The pgvector backend singlestoredb The SingleStore backend (already present on many builds) pypdfium2 PDF text extraction markitdown .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .epub, .rtf, .msg .eml needs nothing beyond the standard library. A missing package disables only the extractor that needs it — the registry reports it rather than failing the run. Source-code files are skipped by default. .py, .sas, .r, .js, .ts, .sql and around thirty more are not ingested unless a setup ticks Ingest source-code files as plain text, because a documents folder that sits inside a project would otherwise fill the collection with build scripts. They are listed as skipped with the reason, never dropped silently.

Both backends carry the same feature set: chunk history, as-of reads, rollback, the portable filter grammar and the governance DDL. pgvector SingleStore Live-row marker valid_to IS NULL sentinel 9999-12-31 Cosine native <=> normalized vectors, dot product ANN index HNSW, on by default opt-in — see below Index covers only live rows yes (partial index) no Cutover transactional rename rename, not transactional The SingleStore ANN index is opt-in for a reason Measured on a live cluster, an HNSW index there loses rows: the same query returned 1, 2, 1, 0, 1 and 1 rows for LIMIT 1 to 9 on a six-row collection, where exact search returned the correct 4 every time. Neither SEARCH_OPTIONS nor OPTIMIZE TABLE changed it. Approximate search may return an imperfect order; returning fewer chunks than exist is a different thing, and for retrieval that feeds an answer it fails silently. Exact search is therefore the default. If a collection is large enough to need the index, enable it with schema={"ann": True} and validate recall on your own data first. pgvector was checked for the same defect and does not have it.

Three different operations, deliberately separate: Operation Where Reversible Retire (default) Automatic on re-ingestion Yes — restore() Deleted-document policy RAG - Load Vector Store No Erasure RAG - Purge Documents No History retention retainDays on the Load step Live rows untouched Retiring keeps previous chunk generations so a collection can be read as it stood on an earlier date and a bad run can be rolled back. Purging removes chunk rows including retired generations and drops the ledger entries. Erasure is not deletion from the source If a purged document still exists at its source, the next ingestion run adds it again. Erasure has to happen at the source as well. On SingleStore, retention matters more than on pgvector: a vector index there cannot be limited to live rows, so retained history is index the search walks. A preview only reads. RAG - Purge Documents in its default mode, Preview, says what a purge would remove and ends its summary with PREVIEW - nothing was changed. Measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09 with SingleStore, with the step as it was before the change described here: the preview said would remove 1 chunk rows for 1 documents, and the rows of the ledger were the same afterwards — but the step had appended a run lock, promoted and saved the ledger again and written the run lock was released so the run can be retried. A preview now takes no run lock and neither promotes nor saves the ledger. It is still refused while another run holds a lock that is less than 30 minutes old, and an ingestion can start while a preview reads. A preview of a project that has no ledger fails with no ledger table for this RAG project - check the project name and caslib and no longer leaves a ledger behind. Measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09 with pgvector and the step of release 2.3.0, run as the code SAS Studio generates for a flow: a preview ended with PREVIEW - nothing was changed and 1 documents named, 1 chunk rows would be removed (live and retired), appended no lock, promoted and saved nothing, and the saved file of the ledger kept its size and time. Under the lock of a flow that was running, and under a fresh lock row appended by hand, it ended with ERROR: RAG - Purge Documents failed: another ingestion run holds the lock on this ledger - wait for it to finish, or retry in 30 minutes if it crashed. On a project without a ledger it ended with ERROR: RAG - Purge Documents failed: RuntimeError: no ledger table for this RAG project - check the project name and caslib, and no ledger was in memory or saved afterwards. A purge in the mode purge promoted and saved the ledger once and wrote no line about a released lock. Not measured: an ingestion that starts while a preview reads. A purge is not in the run history. RAG - Purge Documents writes no row to rag_runs or rag_doc_events. Measured on 2026-10-11 with SingleStore: both tables held the same number of rows before and after a purge, 13 and 50. The purged document shows in the history only when a later run brings it back, as a second new event.

Each run is recorded in three tables in the vector store's own database, beside the chunks they describe: Table Contents rag_runs One row per run: document counts, chunk counts, embedding cost, and the enrichment cost when the setup has an Enrich stage rag_doc_events Append-only; one row per document per run where something happened rag_configs The parameters behind a config_id, so the hash has an inverse They are not in CAS because a CAS table here is overwrite-in-place by construction, has no transactional append and no constraints, and an empty run deletes the saved file outright. The cost of that choice — history invisible to Visual Analytics — is paid explicitly: both ingestion paths publish rag_runs and rag_doc_events to CAS after each run as <project>_RUNS and <project>_DOC_EVENTS. The database copy is authoritative; the CAS copy is disposable and rebuildable. RAG - Load Vector Store, the step of the flow, and Ingest-Documents.sas — Launch ingestion, or the ingestion job of a setup — publish the same two tables: every run the store holds for the collection (the newest 500) and their document events (the newest 5,000), not only the run that publishes, with the 35 and 10 columns, the measures as numbers and everything else as text, promoted and saved in the caslib of the pipeline tables. For the job <project> is its ledger table without the ending _LEDGER, which is the table prefix of a setup. A run that finds nothing to do publishes too, so one more run of a setup brings the runs before it into CAS, as far as the store recorded them. The job publishes since release 2.3.0; before, only the step did. Measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09, with the job as it was: <project>_RUNS still had 3 rows after a job run on pgvector, and on SingleStore the store held four runs of a collection while the CAS copy held three. On 2026-10-11 and on 2026-10-12 the pull of the log chain found the ledger of a setup that the Prompt Builder had ingested in memory and its <project>_RUNS not. The job as it publishes ran on the test system later on 2026-10-12, in six SAS Job Execution jobs with a content folder, a table prefix and a collection of their own; every job ended as completed: A first run of three documents, with one file excluded: <project>_RUNS with 1 row and 35 columns - 13 VARCHAR and 22 DOUBLE - and <project>_DOC_EVENTS with 4 rows and 10 columns, both promoted and saved, with the NOTE below above the last line of the log. Set against a run table the step had published on 2026-10-11, no column differed in name, type or label; two differed in length, and one of the document events. A run that found nothing to do: 2 rows and 5 events. A run with one changed document: 3 rows and 7 events. With the run history switched off the log had no line about the history, and both tables and their saved files were as the run before had left them. Both tables dropped and their files deleted, then a run: 4 rows and 8 events - every run the store held. The run with the history switched off is not among them: it is not in the store. With the rag_core of before this change in the content folder the job wrote the milestone rag history: not read for CAS (ImportError: …) - the ingestion itself is unaffected and the WARNING, left both tables as they were and ended as completed. The tables were read back in a compute session, not in jobs. The pull and the link of the log chain then found those runs - see The Third Run. Not provoked: an upload that fails, a row count that differs, a promote or a save that is refused. Changed after those runs and not run in SAS: the reason of a history that could not be read reaches SAS through the function of the logging programs, so in the WARNING and in the milestone a quote shows as a backtick, % as pct, & as + and a semicolon as a comma, a comment mark is split, and the reason ends after 200 characters. The two differ in three points. With the history switched off, and for a table the store holds no rows for, the step drops the CAS table and deletes its saved file (read from its program); the job leaves the table as it is. The job puts an upload in the place of a table only when it holds every row that was read. And a history the job cannot read or publish is a WARNING in its log — WARNING: RAG ingestion: the run history ... was not published ... — while the run stays one that went through; the next run publishes the history again. A run that published writes this line above its last line: NOTE: RAG ingestion: the run history was published to CAS, promoted and saved - <caslib>.<project>_RUNS with <n> rows and <caslib>.<project>_DOC_EVENTS with <m> rows. The job definition RAG Ingest - <setup> holds a copy of Ingest-Documents.sas from the time the setup was manifested. After the RAG content is deployed again, Manifest setup has to run once for a setup before its job publishes. RAG - Purge Documents writes no row to either table (retention and erasure). started_at of a run is the epoch in its run id, read as UTC, and the steps and the job take that epoch from the SAS clock of the compute session. On the test system, whose sessions run in UTC, started_at was the start of each run (measured on 2026-10-11, for 20 runs of one collection). In a compute session whose SAS clock is not UTC — the option TIMEZONE — it is off by the offset to UTC, while finished_at, which Python writes from its own clock, is not. For a run of the job that is new with release 2.3.0: up to release 2.2 the Python program of the job made the id from its own clock. Read from the code, not measured. History never fails a load. If the store refuses the write, the ingestion still stands and the log says so.

A document the pipeline decided not to ingest — no extractor for its format, a source file with code ingestion off, a scanned PDF with no text layer — is recorded as skipped with the reason. failed is reserved for something a person can fix. Collapsing the two made every run look broken and hid the rows that were. Both are counted separately in rag_runs (docs_skipped, docs_failed), and every skipped document is named in the run log, grouped by reason. The summary of RAG - Extract Text counts such a document as skipped as well. A new document in which the extractor finds no text — an empty file, a PDF that holds only scans — was counted there under documents extracted and under extractors used, although rag_core hands it back as skipped. It is now counted as skipped, with the reason in the line rag skipped: 1 - <extractor> found no text (empty or scanned-only document) above the summary: three unchanged documents and one empty file give 0 documents extracted, 0 failed, 3 skipped as unchanged, 1 skipped and no line extractors used. Measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09 with an empty .txt file: the step logged rag extract: 0 extracted, 1 skipped, 0 failed and rag skipped: 1 - plaintext found no text (empty or scanned-only document) with the path of the file, and no line extractors used. The summary of that run read 0 documents extracted, 0 failed, 3 skipped as unchanged, 1 deleted, 1 skipped, because a file had been taken out of the folder before it. With one more new document it read 1 documents extracted, 0 failed, 3 skipped as unchanged, 1 skipped, followed by extractors used: plaintext=1. Measured the same day for an excluded code file beside three unchanged documents: 0 documents extracted, 0 failed, 3 skipped as unchanged, 1 excluded. docs_skipped is added to an existing rag_runs table by an additive migration on the next run, and so are docs_excluded — the documents the deployment excludes, a source file with code ingestion off — and the six enrichment columns: a collection built before the Enrich stage existed keeps answering, and its runs simply record no LLM cost. A run reads which columns rag_runs has and adds only the missing ones, so an upgraded deployment needs no manual DDL where the store user of the ingestion may alter the table — on PostgreSQL that is its owner. Where it may not, the Load step logs rag history: not recorded (… must be owner of table rag_runs, nothing is written for that run and the ingestion itself is not affected, until the owner runs an ingestion or a DBA runs ALTER TABLE rag_runs ADD COLUMN docs_excluded integer DEFAULT 0 once. Before release 2.3.0 a run wrote docs_excluded to a table that had no such column, so by the code every write to rag_runs failed and no run was recorded; the runs of that time are not backfilled. Measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09, with pgvector and with SingleStore 9.0.40: Every run wrote its row. The logs said rag history: run … recorded, and rag history: not recorded stood in none of them. On pgvector the CAS copy <project>_RUNS held 35 columns, docs_excluded among them, and grew with the runs of the flow, to 19 rows. The column is added to a table that exists. On SingleStore rag_runs had 34 columns and no docs_excluded before the first run and 35 with it after; the two runs in between added two rows to rag_runs and three events to rag_doc_events. That table is shared by every collection in the database, and the accelerator does not take the column out again: the first run of this release changes rag_runs for good. The count is written. With one source-code file in the documents folder and code ingestion off, the two runs that followed — the job and the flow, on pgvector — had docs_excluded 1, and the 17 runs before them 0. Not measured: a store whose user may not alter rag_runs, and with it the line must be owner of table rag_runs; a store that does not say which columns a table has; whether an older runtime that is still deployed elsewhere writes its rows to a rag_runs that has the new column; and docs_excluded other than 0 on SingleStore. The tests run the first two against a stand-in for the connection. The run log also states what the embedding and the enrichment cost while the run is still on screen, and spells out where the chunk token budget came from — it is the setup's chunk window minus the estimator's safety margin, not a limit the model imposed.

Secrets. Store credentials live only in the credential domain, resolved per identity at run time. They are never written to a flow, a CAS table, a WORK file or a log. The .env file is git-ignored and is read only by the admin scripts on your workstation. On SCR and MAS destinations — which have no SAS Viya session — the same names are supplied as environment variables. The address of the vector store. Host and database are configuration, not a credential, and they stand in the log: the summary of RAG - Load Vector Store names the vector store. One line of it reads NOTE: <backend> collection <collection> on <host>/<database>, with the host as it is set for the step — an IP address on the test system (seen on 2026-10-11 with SingleStore: singlestore collection zz_verify_s2_v1 on <host>/SASModel). The line after it names the credential domain and the name of the entry the user was read from (<BACKEND>_RAG_USER), not its value: user and password come from the credential domain, and the summary holds neither. Seen on 2026-10-11 with pgvector, as two lines that follow each other: NOTE: pgvector collection zz_verify_r12s_v1 on <host>/postgres and NOTE: credentials resolved from domain agentic-ai-keys (PGVECTOR_RAG_USER). A search of that flow log for the words password, user name, credential, secret and API key found that one line outside the echoed program; such a search does not show that the name of the account stands nowhere as a bare value. The summary is part of the log of every run that reaches the step, so the address of the store is in the job log of every run of a flow that is scheduled as a job, for everyone who may read that log. What crosses which boundary. Document text leaves the source only to reach the extractor, the embedding container and the vector store, all inside your deployment. The embedding model runs as a governed SCR container you publish. Two settings can change that, and both are explicit choices: an embedding model that forwards to a hosted API (the fact sheet's deployment_type says which) sends the chunk text to that provider; an Enrich stage whose prompt calls a hosted LLM sends the chunk, and whatever else the mapping gives it — including up to 20,000 characters of the surrounding document — to that provider, once per chunk. Both are visible on the setup, and neither happens by default: the shipped embedding default and every enrichment prompt built on a locally served model stay inside the deployment. Identity. Everything runs as the identity that launched it, which is why the run-as-requesting-user context matters: it keeps the audit trail truthful as well as making the steps work. Error text. Database error messages are stored in the ledger's error_text and shown in step summaries. Some stores put internal cluster hostnames in their own error messages, so that column can contain infrastructure detail. Treat the ledger table as internal, or restrict the caslib holding it. What is not encrypted by the accelerator. Chunk text and embeddings sit in your vector store in the clear. Encryption at rest is the database's responsibility. TLS to the store is configurable per backend (sslmode for PostgreSQL, on/off for SingleStore) and defaults to enabled.

Symptom Cause "cannot run the RAG steps … different identities" Wrong compute context — see above "no credential resolved from domain" The running identity has no credential, or a service account is running the job A step renders as an empty editor The .step file was uploaded as a plain file instead of registered A saved flow reports a missing step A step was re-registered instead of updated, minting a new id Code generation returns HTTP 500 The .flw was uploaded as a file, or a node declares an input port nothing is wired into Retrieval returns fewer chunks than exist A SingleStore ANN index is enabled — see the warning above The run refuses to start Another run holds the ledger lock; it expires after 30 minutes RAG - List Documents fails with the run lock could not be written to … - refusing to ingest unguarded, below ERROR: The variable doc_id has been specified with incompatible data types The flow runs on a ledger the ingestion job wrote, with steps from before release 2.3.0 (or the job on a ledger a flow wrote) — see one ledger for the job and the flow RAG - Register Setup fails with POST /modelRepository/projects returned 400 and You must specify a value for the "folderId" parameter The SAS Model Manager project named in the step does not exist, and the rag_core on the site is from before release 2.3.0. Import the package of the release or run deploy-rag-content, or create the project in SAS Model Manager first — see the checkbox of the custom step A RAG step writes NOTE: The quoted string currently being processed has become more than 262 bytes long above its summary or above its ERROR line Steps from before release 2.3.0; nothing is wrong with the run. The steps of release 2.3.0 write neither the summary nor the ERROR line as a quoted string. Above the summary the NOTE was gone in RAG - Register Setup and in a flow of List, Extract, Chunk, Embed and Load; above the ERROR line it was gone in a failing RAG - List Documents (measured on 2026-10-11) — see the checkbox of the custom step A publishing validation on a SAS Micro Analytic Service destination returns HTTP status 201, an empty error column and empty outputs in some or all rows, for a decision that uses a retrieval model SAS Micro Analytic Service ended those executions after 30 seconds. The validation sends its rows at the same time, and the models behind the nodes took longer when they were called together; a direct call of the module answers "executionState": "timedOut". The lengths of the model's variables are not the cause — see several rows at once and the Troubleshooting Guide RAG - Register Setup fails, and its log holds WARNING: … the step failed after the score code of the retrieval model was stored A request after the upload failed (a flow that does not exist, an artifact that could not be attached). The model holds the new score code; the WARNING lines below say whether it verifies TLS certificates and whether it is tagged — see the checkbox of the custom step RAG - Register Setup fails, and its log holds WARNING: … it is not known whether SAS Model Manager stored the score code The upload of the score code got no usable answer. The tag TLS-Verification-Off was not updated; run the step again The ingestion job ends with the run lock could not be written to the ledger … - refusing to ingest unguarded The lock row of the job was not in the ledger when the job read it back. Look in the SAS log above the message: CAS refused the append (its ERROR is there), or the second export of the ledger failed. The refusal of the job was not provoked on the test system: no measured run of the job of release 2.3.0 wrote it. The lock row with its run id was read from another session during one of those runs and is named in the release step of the runs that failed; for the other runs it is taken from the job not refusing. RAG - List Documents wrote the same refusal there once, for a ledger in a caslib of the CAS session, below ERROR: The caslib '…' is a session caslib. You cannot promote tables to global scope in session caslibs. See one ledger for the job and the flow The ingestion job ends with another ingestion run appears active for this ledger (run lock held) - retry later The ledger holds a lock row of another run that is less than 30 minutes old: a flow or a job is ingesting, or a run crashed, or a job definition from before release 2.3.0 failed and left its row. The run took no lock and did not touch the ledger. Wait for the other run, or 30 minutes. A run of the job of release 2.3.0 that fails takes its own lock out and writes the run lock was released so the run can be retried — see one ledger for the job and the flow. Measured on 2026-10-11: a job refused this way ended as failed, left no lock row of its own, and was not refused when it was run again after the other run had ended A step fails with the saved table … could not be loaded into memory (CAS messages above) - stopped, because an empty table would re-embed the corpus and overwrite the saved file The ledger or the embedded chunks of the project are saved in the caslib but not in memory, and CAS could not load the file. The CAS messages above the ERROR say why. The step stops before it takes a lock or starts a ledger, and the job stores no ledger after a run that failed, so the saved file is not touched — also in a SAS session that ran the job before, where up to this release the job stored the ledger of the earlier run over it. A saved file that cannot be loaded could not be staged on the test system and was not run in SAS; that the job stores no ledger after a run that failed was measured for a run that the lock of another run refused. See a saved ledger is loaded back A run writes WARNING: RAG: … is not in memory, and the files of the caslib … could not be listed (CAS messages above) - a saved copy could not be looked for. and WARNING: RAG: the run continues without the table and saves over a copy that may be there. The table is not in memory and CAS could not list the files of the caslib, so the run could not look for a saved copy and goes on without the table. For a ledger that means that every document counts as new and is embedded again, and that a saved ledger is overwritten. Stop the run if a saved copy should exist, and look at the CAS messages above the WARNING and at the caslib. The wording of the two messages - they stood on four log lines - was measured on 2026-10-11 in RAG - List Documents, for a ledger in a caslib of the CAS session; a run that goes on to its end behind them was not. See a saved ledger is loaded back Launch ingestion shows The ingestion run did not succeed with the milestone Ingestion failed: the saved table … could not be loaded into memory The ledger of the setup is saved in the caslib but not in memory, and CAS could not load the file. Nothing was ingested and the saved file is not touched; the CAS messages in the log of the job say why. The milestone was not run in SAS: no file that CAS cannot load could be staged on the test system. See a saved ledger is loaded back The ingestion job of a setup ends as failed in SAS Job Execution The run failed: the last ERROR line of its log, ERROR: RAG ingestion failed: …, says why, and the record of the job holds the same text. SAS Job Execution reports its own error code there, 5713 (A procedure in the SAS program provided for the job completed execution with at least one error.), and inside it an error with the code 1012 and the text of that line. Up to release 2.2, and with a job definition that was not manifested again, the job ends as completed with the same ERROR line — see one ledger for the job and the flow. The failed state was measured for the job RAG - Register Setup generates from a flow and, on 2026-10-11, for Ingest-Documents.sas, with these two codes in the record of the job The log of the ingestion job holds NOTE: RAG ingestion: rag_ledger_in.json of an earlier run of this SAS session was deleted from WORK The program ran before in the same SAS session. The file is the export of that run and is removed so that this run cannot read it; nothing is wrong. A job started by SAS Job Execution has a WORK of its own and does not write the line. The line comes once for each of the two files that is there, rag_ledger_in.json and rag_ledger_lock.json (measured on 2026-10-11) The ingestion job ends with … of an earlier run of this SAS session could not be deleted from WORK - stopped, because the run would read the ledger of that run as its own The export of an earlier run is still in WORK and SAS could not delete it. Start a new SAS session and run the job there. The log of such a run also holds three ERROR messages of PROC JSON above its milestone, on six log lines - ERROR: Invalid file, …/rag_ledger_in.json., ERROR: Due to the previous error, the JSON output file is incomplete and invalid, … and ERROR: The JSON writer is in an error state at this point and no more items may be inserted. They have the same cause: the export still runs after the delete failed, and writes to the file that is in the way. Measured on 2026-10-11 with a directory of that name in WORK; by the code, the last line names the lock instead of the file where another run holds a fresh lock at that moment Test retrieval says The probe failed: the Python environment of this compute context lacks the requests package The Python of the compute context named in ragComputeContext has no requests — see Python packages. Up to release 2.2 the page showed a probe that returned no chunks in that case. The line the page reads - RAGRETRIEVE FAILED the Python environment of this compute context lacks the requests package - see the RAG administration guide - was measured on 2026-10-11 in a session in which the import of requests was made to fail; the text of the page was not run in SAS, because the test system has no compute context without the package deploy-rag-content stops with (409) Conflict on the upload of a file Seen on 2026-10-11 with deploy-rag-content.ps1, on a content folder that held an earlier runtime: the Files service refused the upload of a file whose old copy the script had just deleted, and answered the same upload with 201 a minute later. Run the script again - the second run completed. Until a run has completed, the file the script stopped at is missing from the folder. The script calls mdb content-deploy since release 2.3.0, which deletes no file - it replaces the content of a file that differs in place - and stops at the first write that fails; that has not run against SAS Viya — see what gets deployed The Load step logs rag history: not recorded (… must be owner of table rag_runs The store user of the ingestion may not alter rag_runs, which release 2.3.0 widens by the column docs_excluded. The ingestion itself is not affected. A step of the flow failed. The line is written by the job, not by a step: the ERROR of the step that failed is above it — see The job generated from a flow under the checkbox of the custom step retrieval_status of a retrieval model in a decision says no vector-store credentials resolved The runtime the decision runs in has no <BACKEND>_RAG_USER and <BACKEND>_RAG_PW — see the retrieval model in a decision The Builder says the store is unresolved The domain has no <BACKEND>_HOST / _DB — rerun create-credential-domain after adding them to your .env No embedding model can be chosen, and no setup can be saved No embedding model project is configured (embeddingProjectID), it holds no registered embedding model, or the user cannot read it Documents are missing from the collection Read the run log's rag skipped: lines — they name every document and why.
