The optimization computeContext is a different option A setup shows its vector database as not offered for new setups The deployment withholds that database in the Options pane. The setup keeps it and can still be saved, launched and tested The Builder is switched off, or points at the wrong environment, after an upgrade A report import replaced its Options — restore them with mdb options-restore A published retrieval model returns CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED ... self-signed certificate in certificate chain in retrieval_status The model runs where the CA bundle is not mounted — see TLS verification in the retrieval model A report named RAG Builder still exists and shows an older page It is the retired standalone UI of release 2.2 or earlier — see the retired RAG Builder report Browsing the ledger shows nothing after a run The ledger is written by the run's final step; a large corpus takes minutes. The run panel's clock shows whether it is still going

The folder Embedding-Definitions contains a definition per embedding model, each packaged so that it can be deployed using the SAS Container Runtime (SCR). More on the SCR in the SAS Documentation. Embedding models are registered and published with the same mdb command line as the LLMs — one tool covers both kinds — so this page is short by design. See Register & Publish LLMs for the full description of register, publish, --update, --wait and ship. If you have not installed the CLI yet: pip install -e "Model-Definition-Builder/cli[viya]" Register and publish embedding models by their ids exactly as you would an LLM: # Register mdb register titan_embed_text_v2 bge_base_en_v15 # Publish (destination from -d or SAS_PUBLISH_DESTINATION in .env) mdb publish titan_embed_text_v2 bge_base_en_v15 --wait # ...or both at once mdb ship titan_embed_text_v2 mdb register --all / mdb publish --all cover every managed definition of both kinds in one go, so you rarely need to think about LLM versus Embedding when registering. If you want to add your own embedding model, use mdb add and remember to contribute back. If you are adding a new proprietary model provider, the API_KEY option's default (the manifest's key_name) is the name under which the RAG Builder looks the key up in the credential domain - see Managing Credentials.

The folder LLM-Definitions contains a definition per model, each packaged so that it can be deployed using the SAS Container Runtime (SCR). More on the SCR in the SAS Documentation. Registering and publishing is done with the mdb command line, part of the Model Definition Builder. If you have not installed it yet: pip install -e "Model-Definition-Builder/cli[viya]" To register one or more models into SAS Model Manager: # Register specific models mdb register gpt_41_mini claude_sonnet_4_5 # ...or register every managed LLM and Embedding definition mdb register --all mdb register reads the SAS Viya connection from your .env (see Providing credentials without the command line) and signs in with a token, a username and password, or the SAS Viya CLI login (see Signing in to SAS Viya). It creates the LLM Repository and the model projects on first use if they do not exist yet, so a fresh environment needs no separate setup step. Updating an already-registered model Re-run with --update to refresh a model in place — a new minor version, the content replaced, and the attributes and tags refreshed, without deleting and recreating it: mdb register gpt_41_mini --update If you want to add your own LLM, use mdb add (an interactive wizard, or non-interactive flags) rather than editing files by hand, and remember to contribute back. If you are adding a new proprietary model provider, the API_KEY option's default (the manifest's key_name) is the name under which the Prompt Builder and the RAG Builder look the key up in the credential domain - add the matching entry to create-credential-domain.ps1/.sh, mdb's PROVIDER_ENTRIES and the table in Managing Credentials.

Once the models are registered, publish them to the SCR publishing destination: # Publish specific models and wait for each image build to finish mdb publish gpt_41_mini claude_sonnet_4_5 --wait # ...or publish everything mdb publish --all --wait The --destination (-d) can be given on the command line or, more conveniently, set once as SAS_PUBLISH_DESTINATION in your .env. --wait polls the SCR image build to completion so you learn immediately whether it succeeded. Register and publish in one step mdb ship <model_id> runs a live provider smoke test, register --update and publish --wait in a single, resumable command: mdb ship gpt_41_mini Run any command with --help for the full set of options.
documents.s: Publishing the LLMs to the SCR Destination

documents.t: Open-weight models can get their weights in one of two ways. This page describes both, and explains when the second one is worth the extra setup.

Baked in (the default). The container build downloads the weights from Hugging Face and stores them inside the image. Simple, self-contained, and fine for small models. Staged on a shared volume. The weights are downloaded once into a shared Kubernetes volume, and every model container reads them from there at run time. The image contains only the score code and its Python dependencies. Staging is worth it as soon as any of the following apply: Container size. A 7B model in float16 is roughly 14 GB. Baked in, that 14 GB is in the image, in your registry, and on every node that pulls it. Staged, the image stays in the tens of megabytes. The same weights serve several containers. Model variants, replicas of one model, and a redeployment after a score-code change all read the same staged copy. The data does not have to exist in more than one place — with a ReadWriteMany volume, many pods mount the same directory at once. Publish time. Downloading many gigabytes during the build is the slowest part of publishing, and it happens again on every republish. Staged weights are downloaded once. Gated models. Models with a license you must accept — see the LLM Definitions page — need a Hugging Face token. Staging is the supported way to provide one, because the token is used by a normal Kubernetes Job you control rather than by the container build. Superseding the pre-2025.10 setup Earlier releases documented mounting a Hugging Face token into the Build Kit pod so the container build could authenticate. That mount no longer reaches the build, so definitions carrying a hf login --token $(cat /etc/secret-volume/huggingfacetoken) step in their requirements.json should move to the staged-weights approach below. mdb generate no longer emits that step.
documents.s: Two ways to get weights into a container

documents.t: Apply this once per namespace. Copy SCR-LLM-Deployment-YAML/llm-weights-pvc-template.yaml, replace the two placeholders, and apply it. The template names the namespace llm; for models rendered with mdb deploy --namespace <name>, change its namespace: line - and the one of stage-weights-job-template.yaml - to that namespace and apply it with -n <name>: kubectl apply -f llm-weights-pvc.yaml -n llm ReadWriteMany is required, because several model pods mount the claim at the same time. Storage classes that only support ReadWriteOnce — Azure managed-csi-premium, for example — will not work; use Azure Files, NFS or an equivalent. Size it for the total of every model you intend to stage, plus headroom.

Run a one-off Job that downloads a model into the volume. Only this Job needs a Hugging Face token, and only for gated repositories. For a gated model, create the token secret first: kubectl create secret generic huggingface-token \ --from-literal=huggingfacetoken='*yourToken*' -n llm Then apply SCR-LLM-Deployment-YAML/stage-weights-job-template.yaml with the model repository and target directory filled in. The target directory must be named after the model_id of the definition, since that is where the scorer looks: /mnt/weights/<model_id> The Job itself is named stage-weights-<job name>, where the job name is the model_id with every _ replaced by - (stage-weights-von-1-2 for von_1_2): a Kubernetes name takes no underscore, so kubectl apply refuses a Job named after the model_id itself. The first call a model container answers loads the weights from the volume - tens of seconds for a checkpoint of a few GB on Azure Files - and every later call of that container reuses them: the score code keeps the loaded model for the life of the worker process, because SAS Container Runtime runs the score file again for each request. So a running container keeps the weights it loaded. After you stage new weights into the same directory, restart the model's Deployment (kubectl -n llm rollout restart deploy/<model deployment>), or scale it to 0 and back to 1 where a node lacks the CPU for a second pod. Until then the container answers with the old model. Measured on 2026-10-20 on the test system, from a workstation through the Ingress: with the score code before 2.3.0, which loaded the model on every call, a call of von_1_2 took 2.4 to 2.8 seconds. With the score code of 2.3.0 the first call after the restart took 14.3 seconds and every later call about 0.6 seconds, about four times faster. Four calls sent at once right after the start each took about 15 seconds, the time of one shared load. The models with weights in the image gained less: qwen_25_05b went from about 1.3 to 0.75 seconds a call, all_minilm_l6_v2 from about 0.65 to 0.45 seconds. Check that it landed: kubectl -n llm exec deploy/<any-model> -- ls -la /pybox/model/mount Weights for a public model need no token — delete the env block referencing the secret before applying.

Set weights_source in the model's definition.yaml: runtime: template: hf_transformers requirements_profile: hf-transformers weights_source: mounted Then regenerate, register and publish: mdb generate <model_id> mdb register <model_id> --update mdb publish <model_id> --wait mdb generate drops the weight download from requirements.json and points the score code at /pybox/model/mount/<model_id>. The publish therefore builds a small image containing only the score code and its dependencies. Omitting weights_source — or setting it to baked — keeps the previous behaviour, so existing definitions are unaffected until you change them.
documents.s: Point a definition at the staged weights

documents.t: mdb deploy selects the persistent-volume deployment variant automatically for self-hosted models: mdb deploy <model_id> --registry <your-registry> --host <your-ingress-host> kubectl apply -f deploy-<model_id>.yaml -n llm The rendered Deployment mounts the llm-weights claim read-only at /pybox/model/mount. Because the mount path is the same for every model, one staged copy serves all of them. Verify before publishing kubectl apply --dry-run=server validates a rendered manifest against the API server, including whether the volume a container mounts actually exists. The client-side --dry-run only checks the schema and will not catch a missing volume.

Gated repositories cannot be downloaded during a container build, so they must use weights_source: mounted. mdb generate reports an error rather than producing a definition whose build would fail at the download step: <model_id>: '<repo>' is a gated Hugging Face repository, which cannot be downloaded during the container build. Set 'runtime.weights_source: mounted' in definition.yaml and stage the weights on the shared llm-weights volume instead. Accept the model's license on Hugging Face first, otherwise the staging Job fails with a 403 even with a valid token.

The Prompt Builder is not required, but it is the no-code tool that puts an otherwise code-only workflow in front of the people who own the work. It is one application that builds up to three kinds of things, chosen on its Setup card: a prompt template for LLMs lets prompt engineers test new prompts across LLMs, compare the results, version their experiments, and turn the best prompt into a model for further consumption in the platform (for example in SAS Intelligent Decisioning); a decision template for decision models does the same for the typed questions a decision model answers — see Decision Definitions; a RAG setup lets a data or decision engineer configure a document pipeline — sources, chunking, embedding model, vector store — save it as a governed RAG setup, and generate the ingestion job and SAS Studio flow that run it. This part is the RAG Builder. One single-file build, one Job Execution definition and one Data-Driven Content object serve all three. Which of them a deployment offers is decided by three switches among the object's options (see Configuration): decision templates are on by default, prompt optimization and RAG are off until an administrator switches them on. RAG additionally needs its runtime in SAS Content — see RAG Ingestion and Retrieval. Standalone build The Prompt Builder is shipped as a standalone application in the LLM-Prompt-Builder directory of this repository. It has no dependency on the SAS Portal Framework for SAS Viya — it is a single self-contained HTML file that you embed directly in a SAS Visual Analytics report through SAS Job Execution. Up to release 2.2 the RAG Builder was a second application with a build, a job definition and a report of its own; all three are retired, and a site that still has them follows the upgrade steps of the 2.3.0 changelog.

The content folder /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator ships as one transfer package, SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json in the folder SAS-Viya-Integrations of the repository. It holds the Prompt Builder ready to run — the Visual Analytics report that hosts the object, the SAS Job Execution definition that serves the single-file app and the optimization job — and with it the RAG runtime, the logging programs with their two custom steps and the usage report, the files the tables of the reports are loaded from, and a first page with an installation check. Importing it takes the place of building the app and wiring it up by hand (steps 1–2 below). The commands of this section ran on the test system in eleven passes, twice on 2026-10-12, three times on 2026-10-13, three times on 2026-10-14, twice on 2026-10-15 and once on 2026-10-16, in test content roots and as they were then: what the first found changed the import, the second measured the import in place, the third what was built after the second, the fourth what was built after the third, the fifth what was changed after the fourth, the sixth what was changed after the fifth, the seventh what was changed after the sixth, and each pass after it what was changed after the pass before. What was measured, and what has not run has all eleven.
documents.s: Install or upgrade with the transfer package

documents.t: With mdb installed and your .env filled in (Setup SAS Model Manager): # first install mdb setup # the repository, the projects, the release table, the authorization commands of the repository mdb builders-import # the content folder # upgrade mdb builders-import A site that created the Call LLM node of SAS Intelligent Decisioning with Create-Custom-SAS-Intelligent-Decisioning-Node.sas of an earlier release has it under an id of its own, and the package brings it under f9efcbb7-f57b-4a62-b56d-1a89595e2039. There mdb builders-import asks the site before it uploads anything of the decisions: it leaves the decision Decisions/Call LLM Node and the node type out, imports everything else, and ends with exit code 1 and the command to run once, before the import: mdb decision-node-migrate # dry run: the node type and every decision version that uses it mdb decision-node-migrate --apply # give the node the id of the package and move those decisions mdb builders-import The Call LLM node and its id says what the migration does and why the old node is never deleted while a decision uses it; --no-decisions imports without the decision instead. Then open Start Here, in a compute context that runs as you: https://<your SAS Viya host>/SASJobExecution/?_program=/SAS Agentic AI Accelerator/Start Here&_contextName=<a compute context that runs as you> Go through the lines of its installation check, run the commands of Access to the content folder, and — on a first install — continue at step 3 (the credential domain), step 4 (the Content Security Policy) and the optional object options of step 5. mdb builders-import does in one run what an import otherwise leaves to hand work afterwards: It reads the options of the Prompt Builder report at its place, <content root>/Prompt Builder/Prompt Builder — and of the retired report <content root>/RAG/RAG Builder, while that still exists — and keeps them in a file builder-options-captured-<time>.json in the current directory. A report of that name elsewhere is not read and not written. Importing a report replaces the options an administrator set on the object, see Preserving builder options across a report import; this is what makes an upgrade one command. A report that is there and cannot be read, or that holds no option at all, stops the command here, before anything is loaded or imported. It loads the release table the Prompt Builder report binds to (--no-releases skips that): from Data/ACCELERATOR_RELEASES.csv of the package where the package holds it, so that the table says what was imported, and otherwise from the changelog of the checkout. The reports go through the SAS Viya transfer service: the two reports, the files that are children of a report (the pictures of the usage report) and the folders they sit in, cut out of the package. The command rewrites the import mapping before the job starts, so that nothing is edited after the fact: the data source of the Prompt Builder report is retargeted from the shipped Public.ACCELERATOR_RELEASES to SAS_CAS_LIBRARY.SAS_RELEASES_TABLE on your CAS server, and the placeholder host https://your-sas-viya-host in the Data-Driven Content URL becomes SAS_VIYA_URL. With --report-caslib <library> the other tables the reports read — LLM_LOGS, LLM_FACT_SHEET, EMBEDDING_FACT_SHEET, PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS — are pointed at the tables of the same name in that library; without it they stay bound to Public. It waits for the job and reads every task of it: a task that did not end completed is printed and ends the run with exit code 1. The decision Decisions/Call LLM Node and the Call LLM node type it carries go through the transfer service too, in an import job of their own (--no-decisions leaves them out). The command asks the site first: a node type with the id of the package is overwritten in place - local edits of its code and its terms are replaced, and the line says so -, a missing one is created under that id, and a Call LLM node under another id stops this part before anything of it is uploaded, with exit code 1 and the line mdb decision-node-migrate, because the transfer service would skip the decision without a failed task. A decision or a node type without a completed task of the job ends the run with exit code 1. A decision that is not imported gets no folder in place either. See The decision that carries the Call LLM node. Every file, custom step and job definition is written in place, by the requests mdb content-deploy sends, with the package as the source: an object that is at its path on your site is updated under the id it has there, and a missing one is created. One line per object says equal, updated, created or FAILED — see What an upgrade does to what a site has. Every file, custom step and job definition below the root folder of the package is brought, and every empty folder — the manifest of your checkout does not limit what is brought. The never-ship rule and the rule for a path do: an object whose name, or the name of a folder above it, is empty, . or .., holds a slash or a blank at either end is not taken, and gets a not imported: line with its reason. release.json is written last, and only when every object in front of it was written. It writes the options back: the ones it read; or, with --options <file>, a file saved with mdb options-save — the way to change a value before the import; or, on a site that has no Prompt Builder report yet, the values mdb setup discovers — the repository, the LLM and the embedding project ids, the SCR endpoint and the deployment type. On such a first install the three switches keep the defaults of the package, so RAG and prompt optimization are off until you enable them in step 5. Either way every placeholder host that is left in the report becomes SAS_VIYA_URL. A repository or project id the report holds no value for is discovered from the deployment, for that kind only; a value the report holds is kept. A run that writes every option back removes its builder-options-captured-<time>.json. It writes sas-viya-cli-content-commands.txt, see Access to the content folder. mdb builders-import --dry-run says what a run would do and writes nothing: every request it sends, the sign-in aside, is a GET, nothing is uploaded, and its mapping: lines are what the package itself says about its tables and its host. A run that did not do everything ends with exit code 1 and prints the command to run next, on a line of its own; that command names the kept options file, so that the second run does not read the options again from a report the import may have replaced already. A kept file stays in the directory the command ran in until a run writes every option it holds back. It holds option values and no key. The release table needs no clone, the rest of the command does: the clone of the repository gives the manifest — the default package file and content root, and the site settings of the job definitions it lists —, configures a site without the Prompt Builder report by discovery from the model definitions, and gives the release table of a package that holds none. Where a run stops: A report that is there and cannot be read: <report>: it is on this site and its content cannot be read (...), Nothing was imported. A report that is read and holds no option at all stops the same way: <report>: it is in <folder> and holds no option at all - .... Run the command again when the report can be read, name the options with --options <file>, or pass --no-options-capture — then the imported report is configured from the deployment, and what an administrator set is gone. A task of the import job that did not end completed: the import job ended completed, and n of its tasks did not: with a line per task. The options are not written into a report the command cannot be sure was replaced; the command to repeat names the kept options file. A write of the in-place part that is refused or gets no answer: that object is FAILED, every object behind it is listed as not attempted, and Stopped at the first write that failed: ... says what was written before it. A folder that cannot be created stops the run the same way. Nothing is removed, and a second run leaves what is equal by then as it is. release.json is written last, and only when every entry in front of it was written: after a run that stopped, the folder's release.json is the one an earlier run wrote — Start Here shows that release and its commit, and checks the entries that file lists —, and after a first install that stopped there is none, and Start Here shows release.json as missing.

A custom step that a flow uses is referenced by its id, and so is a job definition behind a link or a schedule. The in-place part of the import therefore never replaces an object by a new one: updated step RAG/steps/RAG - Embed Chunks.step (templates; id <the id on your site> kept) updated file RAG/rag_core/tokens.py (content replaced in place; id <the id on your site> kept) updated jobDefinition Start Here (code; id <the id on your site> kept) equal step RAG/steps/RAG - List Documents.step (id <the id on your site>) created file Logging and Monitoring/Link-Logs-To-Models.sas (id <a new id>) An object at its path is updated under its own id, whatever id the package carries for it — a site that got its content from an earlier package, from mdb content-deploy or from the earlier deploy script has other ids than the system the package was exported from. A file keeps its id too: its content is replaced, the file is not deleted. Nothing of the exporting system — an id, a link, a user — reaches your site with the in-place part. A second import changes nothing: every line says equal, and nothing is written. Two objects of one name in one folder are both named with their ids, and neither is written; the same holds for an object and a reference of its name to an object of its kind elsewhere, and such a reference alone fails its entry. A reference of that name to an object of another kind fails nothing: the run lists it at the end as <path> (reference to a <kind> - not the <kind of the entry> that is listed under this name). The kinds are spelled as the other lines spell them: file, folder, report, registered step, job definition; an object of no kind of the manifest is called by the content type the Folders service gives it, or by its address. The rest is brought and the run ends with exit code 1. Remove the one that is not used, or the reference, and run the command again. What is not at its path is not touched. A step you registered in a folder of your own — the starter package of earlier releases put LLM - Log Parser into the folder Custom Steps, and a step may live in the folder of a user — stays as it is, and the import creates the step of this release at its path beside it. Update yours in place from a checkout with mdb content-deploy --only "<its path in the manifest>" --to "<path or id of your step>", see One part, somewhere else. The settings of a site in a job definition stay. A compute context a site set in the parameter _contextName of a job definition — Start Here, Load-Accelerator-Tables, SAS-LLM-Prompt-Builder-UI — stays: an import and a deploy leave an existing value alone. The option RAG: ingestion compute context (ragComputeContext) of the options the import writes back is given to a job definition the import creates and to one on the site that has no _contextName; a _contextName a job definition on the site holds is kept. It has to be a context that runs as the requesting user; where the options name none, the default of the package (SAS Studio compute context) takes its place, and computeContext, the context of the optimization job, is not taken. --compute-context <name> writes that context into every job definition that has the parameter. contentRoot is always written with the content root the content goes to. The other values a site points Start Here and the loader at — the CAS library and server, the credential domain, the names of the repository and the projects, the compute contexts the page looks for, the release table — are settings of the site as well; the address of the guides is the release's. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-12: the import kept the _contextName a test root had set on Start Here and wrote that root into its contentRoot. Measured on 2026-10-13, with options that name an ingestion compute context: Start Here kept the _contextName the root had set, the job definition Load-Accelerator-Tables, which the import created, got the context of the options, and --compute-context wrote its context into Start Here. A job definition on the site without the parameter was not part of that pass. Another content folder. --content-root <folder> brings everything but the reports into that folder and writes it into the parameter contentRoot of the two job definitions that have one; a folder that is not there is created only with --create. The reports and the decision Decisions/Call LLM Node are imported only into the folder the package was exported from, /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator, and only because that folder is at the root of SAS Content: the transfer service takes no target folder, and no mapping to another folder is known to work. With another content root the command says Reports (...): NOT imported and Decisions (...): NOT imported with the reason and ends with exit code 1; --no-reports --no-decisions says that this is meant, and the transfer service is then not called at all. The command it names to run again adds both. After an upgrade, reload the Prompt Builder report. On a site that had the report RAG Builder, the switch Enable RAG setups in the Options pane of the object is ticked and the RAG: options below it hold the values of the old report; the Setup card offers RAG setup for a document collection as a third kind, and an existing setup opens. If the RAG card is shown and cannot be chosen, the credential domain is none — see The retired RAG Builder report. Enable prompt optimization (DSPy) shows what the report stored: ticked where optimization was enabled before. What an import does not bring, and what it replaces: No tables, no projects, no credentials, no option values. A transfer package cannot carry CAS tables, SAS Model Manager projects, credentials or the option values of a site. mdb setup creates the repository and the projects, the command above writes the options, Managing Credentials has the credential domain, and the tables are loaded as The tables of the reports says. A job definition holds a copy of its program and of its form. An import replaces both, and the parameters with them, except the two that are settings of a site: a compute context an administrator set in the parameter _contextName of SAS-LLM-Prompt-Builder-UI stays. The job definition of a RAG setup that a site generated is not part of the package and keeps the ingestion program of the day it was manifested — see After an upgrade: manifest every setup once. The logging programs are replaced as files. Settings that were written into Log-Parser-Code.sas or Get-All-Prompts.sas are gone with the old file; from release 2.3.0 on a site sets them in a program of its own — see Settings that stay yours. An import removes nothing. What a site has in the folder beside the content of the package stays, the retired report RAG Builder among it. The Call LLM node comes under one id, f9efcbb7-f57b-4a62-b56d-1a89595e2039, with the decision that carries it. A site that has a node named Call LLM under another id — created with Create-Custom-SAS-Intelligent-Decisioning-Node.sas of an earlier release — runs the migration mdb decision-node-migrate before the import. mdb builders-import refuses the decisions there before it uploads them and ends with exit code 1 and the migration command. A transfer import of the package in SAS Environment Manager is not asked: it fails the task of the node, and skips the decision without a task, while the import job ends completed. See The Call LLM node and its id. The reports go into one folder. The files, custom steps and job definitions follow --content-root; the two reports and the decision are imported into /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator or not at all, see What an upgrade does to what a site has. The uploaded package is deleted. The command uploads the reduced package for the reports and deletes it once the import job has ended; a delete that is refused is a line with the id of the package and how to delete it. That delete has not run against SAS Viya.
documents.s: What an upgrade does to what a site has

documents.t: What the package brings, as SAS-Viya-Integrations/package-manifest.yaml lists it — one entry per object, with the repository file it is a copy of: Path below /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator What Start Here Job definition: the first page, with the links and the installation check release.json The release, the commit the folder was deployed from, and every object of the folder with a hash of its content Prompt Builder/ The report Prompt Builder; the job definitions SAS-LLM-Prompt-Builder-UI (the single-file app) and Optimize-Prompt-DSPy; Create-Optimization-Dataset.sas RAG/ steps/ with the nine RAG custom steps, rag_core/, jobs/ with Ingest-Documents.sas and Test-Retrieval.sas, models/ with the retrieval model template Logging and Monitoring/ The report LLM Usage Report with its images; the custom steps LLM - Log Parser and LLM - Get All Prompts; Log-Parser-Code.sas, Get-All-Prompts.sas, Link-Logs-To-Models.sas, Build-RAG-Cost-View.sas, Load-Fact-Sheets.sas Data/ llm_fact_sheet.csv, embedding_fact_sheet.csv, decision_fact_sheet.csv, ACCELERATOR_RELEASES.csv; the job definition Load-Accelerator-Tables Custom Steps/ LLM - List Available LLMs, LLM - Get Options, LLM - Create LLM Call and the four MM - steps Decisions/ The decision Call LLM Node: it holds only the Call LLM node and brings that custom node type of SAS Intelligent Decisioning under the id f9efcbb7-f57b-4a62-b56d-1a89595e2039. It is not meant to be published - see The Call LLM node and its id 62 objects: 37 files, 18 custom steps, four job definitions, two reports and one decision, which carries the Call LLM node type as its dependency. The folder names are the ones sites have had; Start Here, release.json and Data/Load-Accelerator-Tables are new in release 2.3.0, and so is the folder Custom Steps for a site that never imported the starter package of earlier releases. That package held LLM - Log Parser in Custom Steps; the step of this release is in Logging and Monitoring. LLM - Get Options ships, although its program is an earlier copy of LLM - Create LLM Call with the same lookup of the options and the same generated code: the repository lists it as a step of the accelerator, and a flow that holds it keeps its step after an import. LLM - Create LLM Call is version 1.7, and LLM - Get Options 1.6: the code clears the fileref llmIn of the temporary file of the request right behind the call - also behind a call that failed -, and SAS deletes the file, which holds the provider key where the options have API_KEY; versions 1.6 and 1.5 left it in the WORK folder of the SAS session until the session ended. Measured on 2026-10-20 with the code each of the two steps and Create-LLM-Call.sas of this release wrote for gpt_5_mini, run in a session of the SAS Studio compute context with a stand-in in the place of the key: before the call the request file held the stand-in, behind it the fileref was not assigned and the file was gone - for a call whose host did not resolve (an ERROR line of PROC HTTP, which sets SYSCC 3000) and for a call answered with HTTP 404 (SYSCC 0) -, and the WORK folder held no temporary file behind the code of the script, only the catalogs, the registry and the lock file of the session. Versions 1.6 and 1.5: the code for a model whose options file has the option API_KEY reads the provider key from the credential domain when it runs, from the entry the option names, and sends it in the place of the name - see Managing Credentials. The domain is the one of the line %let API_KEY_DOMAIN=agentic-ai-keys; of the generated code, which the steps write as it stands and do not take from the Credential domain option of the Prompt Builder: a site whose keys are in another domain edits that one line. Versions 1.5 and 1.4 wrote %let API_KEY=<entry name>; and their code sent the name as the key: measured on 2026-10-20 for gpt_5_mini, the container answered 422 and its log held the 401 of the provider, while the step had ended without a word. Measured the same day with versions 1.6 and 1.5 and the program: the NOTE of the step, the key read (NOTE: The key of the entry OpenAI was read from the credential domain agentic-ai-keys.) and gpt_5_mini answering with HTTP 200 - also for code written to SAS Content and included from inside a macro -, no value of the domain in the log, and for an entry the domain does not hold the WARNING and HTTP 422. Versions 1.5 and 1.4: an options file without any option - the options file of an LLM that reads its key from its container (mdb add --auth env) can be {} - gets code that sends an empty options object, where the versions before wrote no code for it and ended with an ERROR line (read from the program and followed by the tests, not run in SAS). Version 1.4: with Save the code to a filename? ticked and no path chosen it writes the code to a temporary file and leaves the fileref _slo_LLM assigned, where version 1.0 held an ERROR line and an ABORT statement for that; measured with version 1.1 on 2026-10-12 for a model whose options.json has no values list. For a model whose options.json holds one, version 1.1 failed in PROC TRANSPOSE and wrote its code without that option; version 1.2 reads the options with one PROC SQL step, and a run that cannot read every default writes no code and ends with an ERROR line and SYSCC 1012. Measured with version 1.2 on 2026-10-13, with the values of manual entry: for gpt_5_mini a code file of 34 lines with %let reasoning_effort=medium; and SYSCC 0, for gpt_41_mini 36 lines, and for an options file that is not there the ERROR line and SYSCC 1012. LLM - Get Options 1.1, changed the same way, failed that day with the box ticked and no path, the values it comes with: it wrote the code file (34 records) and then ended with ERROR 180-322, SYSCC 3000 and a failed job, because its closing NOTE resolved the statement that assigns the temporary file with its semicolon. Version 1.2 keeps that statement without the semicolon and reads it in the NOTE through %SUPERQ. Both steps now write a path into the statement that assigns the file with the QUOTE function, so an apostrophe in a folder or file name is doubled where it ended the text of the statement before. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-13 with LLM - Create LLM Call 1.3 and LLM - Get Options 1.2: with a model entered by hand, the box ticked and no path, each step wrote its code file - 34 lines for gpt_5_mini, as a program and through the code SAS Studio generates for the step - and ended with SYSCC 0, and LLM - Get Options wrote its closing NOTE on one line; with a path in SAS Content, and with a path of the form sasserver:/tmp/<folder>_o'brien/call.sas, both wrote the file there. A quotation mark in a path reaches the DATA step whole: measured in that pass with the code SAS Studio 2026.09 generates for a path control that holds sasserver:/tmp/zz_verify_r20a_p;q'r"s&t%u/call.sas - SAS Studio writes the value masked, %nrquote(%nrstr(...)) with a percent sign in front of each quotation mark -, a DATA step that read it as "&_slo_fl_path.", the way both steps read it, held the 50 characters of the path, and SYMGET gave the same 50; the steps were not run with such a path. Two defects of that pass are changed in LLM - Create LLM Call 1.4 and LLM - Get Options 1.3. With Select name from a table and a model table whose column optionsFileURI was 200 characters wide, both steps asked for <uri><blanks>/content, got HTTP 404 and wrote no code, in 3 of 3 runs, where a column of 49 characters, which is what LLM - List Available LLMs writes, gave the code: the URI is read with TRIMMED now. And run as they come - the selector on table, no table connected, no model name selected - they wrote warnings of macro variables that were not resolved and a syntax error of PROC SQL, and then named an empty options file and HTTP 404: a run without a model name or without an options file now asks SAS Viya for nothing and ends with one ERROR line that says that no model with an options file was chosen, and SYSCC 1012. Measured in the third pass of 2026-10-13 with versions 1.4 and 1.3: as they come, through the code SAS Studio generates for the steps, each wrote no WARNING, ran neither PROC SQL nor PROC HTTP and ended with that one ERROR line and SYSCC 1012; with a model table whose column optionsFileURI is 200 characters wide both wrote their code file - 34 lines for gpt_5_mini, 36 for gpt_41_mini - and ended with SYSCC 0, in 4 of 4 runs. The script Create-LLM-Call.sas of SAS-Code-LLM-Calls, a third copy of that program, has the same lines since that pass and ends a run without a model name and an options file the same way. Measured on 2026-10-14 as a program: as it comes, with a model name alone and with a URI alone, no request, that one ERROR line of the script and SYSCC 1012; with both, for gpt_41_mini, 36 lines of code and SYSCC 0. MM - Get Model Information 1.1 took out the statement at the end of its program that deleted the macro of MM - Get Models in Project (not run in SAS). MM - Get Model Information is version 1.2: it reads a model with the properties it has, and writes a table only for a part the model has. Version 1.1 transposed a fixed list of properties, and for an LLM of the accelerator, which lacks six of them (trainTable, targetEvent, candidateChampion, publishTimeStamp, externalModelId, sasOptions), it ended with an ERROR line for each, SYSCC 3000 and tables without rows - measured on 2026-10-20 with a model table and with an ID entered by hand. A model that was never published has no published models: the step then writes a NOTE in place of work._mgi_publishedModels, where 1.1 named a table that is not there. The tables of an earlier run are deleted first, and a run without a model ID, or for one SAS Model Manager does not answer with HTTP 200, ends with one ERROR line. MM-Get-Models-Information.sas of SAS-Viya-Integrations/SAS-Code-Model-Manager-Interaction is changed the same way. Measured on 2026-10-20 with version 1.2 and the program: six tables for gpt_5_mini, five and the NOTE for an LLM that was never published, 37 properties for a model of SAS Model Studio, SYSCC 0 for each, and the ERROR line with status 404 for an unknown ID. What never ships. An object that the manifest does not list is not deployed, not exported and fails the check of the package when it is found in it. And whatever the manifest says, an object is refused where a part of its path has Showcases or Example in its name, is a folder named generated, or starts with ZZ_VERIFY: showcase and example content — it lives outside the product, for instance in a folder /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator Showcases of a site, and is not in the repository; RAG/generated, where the Prompt Builder writes the ingestion job and the flow of a site's own RAG setups; test objects. Not in the package either: the retired report RAG Builder and its job definition RAG-Builder-UI; model definitions, which reach a site with mdb register; the log collection script, which runs where kubectl runs; and the custom step LLM - Get Prompt Experiments of the repository: it is the step of August 2024 that reads the experiment tracker of one model as one table and shows the options of a run as they are stored, where LLM - Get All Prompts pulls the experiments of every model and leaves out the options whose names say that they hold a secret. Its file stays in Custom-Steps/ of the repository. A site that takes a fix from a checkout without waiting for a package uses mdb content-deploy, and maintainers build the package with it — see The content folder: deploy, export, check.

Start Here is a job definition at the root of the content folder. Open it in a browser: https://<your SAS Viya host>/SASJobExecution/?_program=/SAS Agentic AI Accelerator/Start Here&_contextName=<a compute context that runs as you> The page shows what its SAS session may read, so it is opened in a compute context that runs as you. The parameter _contextName of the job definition names that context - SAS Studio compute context as shipped; the ingestion compute context of your options is given to a job definition the import creates and to one on the site that has no _contextName, a _contextName a job definition on your site holds is kept, and --compute-context writes the one you pass -, so the address works without the parameter where that context runs as you, and &_contextName= names another one for one request. Measured on SAS Viya 2026.09 on 2026-10-12, when the job definition did not have the parameter: opened without it the job ran in the SAS Job Execution compute context, which runs its sessions under a service account on that system. SAS Viya answered every request with 401, and the page read 13 ok, 0 missing, 15 not checked, twelve of the fifteen lines with the advice to ask an administrator. With &_contextName=SAS Studio compute context the same page had 97 lines that were ok. In the second pass of that day the job definition carried the parameter: opened without it in the address the job ran in the SAS Studio compute context and the page read 97 ok, 2 missing, 1 not checked; opened in the SAS Job Execution compute context - with the parameter, and from a job definition without it - the page was built completely (97 and 96 ok), no request was answered 401, and a probe in that context printed that the user of the session was not the user it was started for. What a session of a compute context may read depends on how the system configures the context. Where every request is refused the page has one line at its top in place of those lines: in a session of another user, that it does not run as you and where to open it; in a session that ran as you, to ask for the rights (403) or about the sign-in (401). One user written with a domain behind @ or in front of a backslash is one person. Neither user id is written to the page. In a session of another user the page links itself in each compute context it found, but the one it ran in. Measured on 2026-10-13: opened in the SAS Job Execution compute context the page carried the note that what a session may read depends on how the system configures its compute context, and one link, Open this page in the compute context: SAS Studio compute context; opened without the parameter it had no such link. The one line for a session that is refused everything and the comparison of two users who are written differently are not run in SAS: no request was refused in the second, the third or the fourth pass. The job writes one HTML page: what the accelerator is, links to the Prompt Builder report and the LLM Usage Report by the address they have on your system, links to these guides, and the installation check. Every line of the check has one of three states — ok, missing, not checked — with what was found and one sentence what to do: Section What is looked at Release release.json in the content root: release, commit and date. The file is asked for at the Files service only Content Every entry release.json lists: present in this content root or not. A custom step is registered - by the import of the package or by mdb content-deploy -, so a .step file that was uploaded to the folder is not the step: the step is missing while only that file is there, and the line of a registered step names a file of its name that lies beside it and says to delete it. What a folder holds under the name of an entry is told the way mdb content-deploy tells it: a member has the name of the entry to the letter - a step that is registered under the name without .step is not the step of the entry -, and is of its kind by what its uri starts with. A member of a folder that is a reference to an object elsewhere is no entry of the folder, whatever it names: it is not followed. A reference of the name and kind of an entry stands in the way of the entry, alone or beside the object, and so do two objects of that name and kind: the line is missing with the advice to remove the reference, or to remove or rename all but one; where the object is there the entry is counted as present. Below a name two folders have nothing is read and the entries are not checked. A report that is there is ok whatever lies beside it, and for a report that is missing the advice names the import of the package and mdb builders-import - mdb content-deploy writes no report. One difference to mdb stays: below a folder with a reference to a folder beside it the page reads that folder, where mdb lists the entries below as FAILED CAS tables of the reports ACCELERATOR_RELEASES (Prompt Builder) and LLM_LOGS, PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS, LLM_FACT_SHEET, EMBEDDING_FACT_SHEET, DECISION_FACT_SHEET, RAG_SETUPS, RAG_RUNS (LLM Usage Report): there or not, their rows, when they were loaded CAS tables of the logging chain The two tables Get-All-Prompts.sas writes for Link-Logs-To-Models.sas that no report binds: PROMPT_OPTIMIZATIONS, MODEL_CATALOG SAS Model Manager The repository and the projects of the LLM, the embedding model and the decision model definitions, by their names, with the number of models of each; a project without a model is missing Options of the Prompt Builder report modelRepositoryID, llmProjectID and, with RAG switched on, embeddingProjectID: whether each names the object that was found by its name Credentials The credential domain of the provider keys, by its name. No entry of it is asked for Python packages For each part what the Python of the compute context needs: pandas, swat and requests for logging; for the RAG runtime also psycopg2-binary, singlestoredb, pypdfium2 and markitdown; dspy, requests and optuna for prompt optimization Publishing destinations Whether one is defined, and their names Compute contexts The contexts the options computeContext and ragComputeContext of the Prompt Builder name, and the ones the parameter computeContexts names What holds for the page: It changes nothing. Every request is a GET, and the one file the program writes is the page, in the WORK folder of its session. A site that lacks something gets a line, not a failed job. A service that does not answer, a right the session lacks and a folder that is not there are lines of the page: not checked with the HTTP status, or missing. Where PROC PYTHON does not run in the compute context, the page says that and nothing else. It shows what its session may read. Open it in a compute context that runs as you (_contextName). In a compute context that runs under a service account the session is the service account: what it may not read is not checked with the HTTP status, and a session that is refused everything gets one line at the top. No token and no user id is written to the page, and of an answer that was refused only the status. The content root is a parameter. The job definition checks the folder its parameter contentRoot names: /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator as shipped, and the folder a deploy or an import was given with --content-root. Add &contentRoot=<folder> to the address to check another one. The parameters name the CAS library and the CAS server of the report tables (caslib, casServer), the credential domain, the repository and the three projects by the names mdb setup gives them, the compute contexts to look for and the address of the guides; all of them but the address of the guides are settings of the site, which a deploy and an import leave as the site has them. The guides are links only on https://sassoftware.github.io or on this SAS Viya; another address is shown as text, with a line that says why. SAS-Viya-Integrations/Setup/README.md lists them. Measured on SAS Viya 2026.09 on 2026-10-12, with the program as it was then, from a test content root that mdb content-deploy had filled: The page is served as a page. Opened the way a browser opens it, with _contextName=SAS Studio compute context, the job answered HTTP 200 with text/html and no Content-Disposition. The page began with <!DOCTYPE html> and held no script, link or image element. What it read. 97 ok, 2 missing, 1 not checked, with release 2.3.0, the commit and its date, and 70 of 72 entries of release.json are present in this content root - the two that are missing are the reports, which a deploy does not bring. With copies of the two reports in the folder a run through the jobExecution API logged the page holds 102 checks - 102 ok, 0 missing, 0 not checked. Such a run has no _webout: the program says so in a NOTE and names the file in WORK, and no page of that run was kept. What is missing gets its line. A file that was deleted: missing | not in its folder. A .step uploaded as a file in the place of a registered step: missing | a file of that name is there, and no registered step. A content root that does not exist: Content root | missing | the folder was not found, with the other sections filled. Against the content folder of the test system: 29 ok, 1 missing - release.json, which that folder did not hold yet. It changed nothing and showed no secret. A listing of the folder before and after a page differed in nothing. No page held a token, a password, a host name or an e-mail address, and the user id only inside the folder path the page was given; the publishing destinations are listed by their names. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-12, from a second test root: the parameter _contextName of the job definition (above); with the registered step deleted and its .step uploaded as a file, the row missing | a file of that name is there, and no registered step with the advice to import the package or run mdb content-deploy; after an import registered the step, ok | present, and a file of that name lies beside it with the advice to delete the file; after the file was deleted, ok | present; and release.json read through the check of its address. Not measured: the page for a user without administrator rights, and the program pasted into SAS Studio. Measured on 2026-10-13 for a test root, with the page as it was then - opened in the SAS Job Execution compute context, without a parameter, and with a guideUrl of another site: 105 checks each time (98 ok, 6 missing, 1 not checked); the section CAS tables of the logging chain with five rows, one of them ok; the link to the other compute context in the session of another user only; and with the other guideUrl the five guide entries as text, without a link. In that pass, with a file of the test root replaced by a reference of its name that pointed at a file of another folder, the page read RAG/rag_core/tokens.py (file) | ok | present and 70 of 72 entries of release.json, while mdb content-deploy reported that entry as FAILED. The page had read the kind of a member from its contentType, which for a reference is the kind of the object it names. It now takes a member whose type says reference for no entry. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-13: for that state the page read RAG/rag_core/tokens.py (file) | missing | a reference of that name is in its folder, and the object it names lives elsewhere with the advice to remove the reference and 69 of 72 entries of release.json are present, and for two test roots, each in both compute contexts, 105 checks (98 ok, 6 missing, 1 not checked). The page judges a reference as mdb does: one that has the name of an entry and names an object of the kind of the entry stands in the way of that entry. In the same pass, with the file and a reference of its name both in the folder, mdb content-deploy and mdb builders-import failed the entry and the page said ok | present. Such an entry is now missing | present, and a reference of that name is in its folder, which names an object that lives elsewhere, with the advice to remove the reference; it is still counted in N of M entries of release.json are present, and its line is shown above the folded list. A report that is there stays ok | present whatever lies beside it: mdb writes no report and fails none over a reference. A reference to an object of another kind is no part of the check, and the line of release.json is judged the same way. Measured in the third pass of 2026-10-13, with the file and a reference of its name to a .csv file in one folder: that line, 70 of 72 entries of release.json are present as without the reference, and 97 ok and 7 missing against 98 and 6; with a reference of that name to a folder the row was ok | present. The page was changed once more after that pass: it tells what a folder holds under the name of an entry the way mdb content-deploy does (the row Content above). Measured on 2026-10-14 for two test roots, against a dry run of mdb content-deploy: a reference named like the step without its ending, and a reference of the name of the step to a .csv file beside it, left the step ok | present and equal; a folder replaced by a reference to a folder elsewhere was missing on the page and FAILED in mdb, with the entries below it; and the rows of the two reports read missing | not in its folder with the advice to import the package or run mdb builders-import. SAS Viya refused with HTTP 409 to put two objects of one name and kind into one folder, and a reference beside an object of its name and kind. Not run in SAS: two objects of one name and a name two folders have, which SAS Viya did not let a pass set up, a report with a reference beside it, the one line for a session that is refused everything as it is now, and a project without a model as missing.
documents.s: Start Here: the first page and the installation check

documents.t: A package cannot carry a CAS table. The two reports read five: Table Report Loaded by ACCELERATOR_RELEASES Prompt Builder mdb setup, mdb builders-import and mdb load-releases; or the job Load-Accelerator-Tables LLM_FACT_SHEET, EMBEDDING_FACT_SHEET, DECISION_FACT_SHEET LLM Usage Report mdb load-facts; or the job Load-Accelerator-Tables, which loads the sheets of the release LLM_LOGS, PROMPT_EXPERIMENTS, RAG_SETUPS, RAG_RUNS LLM Usage Report The log parser and the pull of your own system, see Logging & Monitoring Data/Load-Accelerator-Tables is a job definition for a site that imported the package without mdb — through SAS Environment Manager, for example — and so has neither the release table nor the fact sheets: it loads ACCELERATOR_RELEASES from Data/ACCELERATOR_RELEASES.csv and the three fact sheets from the files beside it, promoted and saved, into the CAS library of its parameter caslib (default Public). Its other parameters are _contextName - a compute context that runs as you -, contentRoot and releaseTable, the name of the release table, and _output_type with the value html, for its page. Started from its address in SAS Job Execution, the job answers with a page: each of the four tables with its rows and what this run did with it - Loaded by this run, Left as it was or Not in the CAS library - under a line that says whether the four are in the CAS library. Whether this run loaded a table is read from CAS: the rows of each table and the time CAS made it are read before the tables are loaded and again at the end, and a table with another time, or one that was not there before, is one this run loaded. The log has every line. SAS Job Execution answers a run that fails with its own page Job Error, which names the ERROR line of the job. A table the upload could not take the place of - two runs at the same time, where the promote of the second is refused because the first loaded the table - is Left as it was, Loaded again from its saved file or Loaded by this run and not saved, with its WARNING in the log; the job then ends with warnings, not as a failed job, so the page shows (measured on 2026-10-20: two runs started 3 seconds apart, the second refused with The target table DECISION_FACT_SHEET of the promotion already exists, ended with Job Error before this change). A job definition without _output_type=html gets no page, with a NOTE, and the program run in SAS Studio writes none. Measured on 2026-10-20 in a test folder with test table names: four rows Loaded by this run for a run that loaded the four tables, the release table Loaded by this run and the three fact sheets Left as it was for a content root without decision_fact_sheet.csv and Load-Fact-Sheets.sas, and Job Error with the ERROR line for a run without the release file. Before, the job answered with an empty page SAS Output: its job definition had no _output_type, and what it loaded was in its log only. The fact sheets are loaded by Load-Fact-Sheets.sas, which the job includes from the folder Logging and Monitoring of the content root. The fact sheets in Data are the ones of the release. The job replaces a fact sheet table with them, and with it the rows of definitions a site keeps of its own. Such a site loads its sheets with mdb load-facts and starts the job with factSheets=0: it then loads the release table only, and a fact sheet that is not in the CAS library is a WARNING instead of a failed job. The release table gets the eleven columns of mdb in their order, the three numbers as DOUBLE and the eight text columns as VARCHAR. Measured on the test system on 2026-10-12 against the table mdb load-releases loaded: 707 rows, the same eleven columns, types and lengths, and no difference in PROC COMPARE. One thing differs: the formatted length - the width CAS keeps for display - is 16 in the table of the job for the four text columns whose longest value is shorter than that (version, release_date, change_type, builder_part), and 6, 10, 8 and 8 in the table of mdb. A width of 16 cuts no value of these columns, and the page of the Prompt Builder reads nothing from the table; what a SAS Visual Analytics object shows with it was not measured. A table that exists is replaced only by an upload that holds every row of its file. A file that is not in the folder, a first line with other columns and an upload that is short leave the table as it is, with a WARNING. So does a folder that is not there. Measured on 2026-10-13 with a content root that had no folder Logging and Monitoring: the FILENAME statement for the program of that folder wrote ERROR: Folder denoted by path ... was not found. and ERROR: Error in the FILENAME statement. in front of the WARNING. The job and Load-Fact-Sheets.sas now ask the Folders service for a folder first - GET /folders/folders/@item?path=, the request Start Here asks with - and assign no fileref where the answer is 404; every other answer assigns it as before. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-13 with the job as changed and a content root without Logging and Monitoring: PROC HTTP wrote NOTE: 404 Not Found and no ERROR line, no ERROR line of a FILENAME statement followed, the log held the WARNING that Load-Fact-Sheets.sas was not found, and the release table was loaded. The job still ended as failed - ERROR: Load-Accelerator-Tables: not in the CAS library casuser at the end of the run: LLM_FACT_SHEET EMBEDDING_FACT_SHEET DECISION_FACT_SHEET. and SYSCC 1012 -, because none of the three fact sheet tables was in that CAS library: the WARNING is what the job writes for the folder, and the check at its end is the last point of this list. A table that has the name the job or Load-Fact-Sheets.sas loads a table of its session under - <table>_NEW for an upload, _LAT_SAVED for the saved file of a release table - is not touched. Both programs ask table.tableExists before they load under the name, and load only where CAS answers 0. With another answer nothing is uploaded and both tables stay as they are, with a WARNING that says to rename or drop <table>_NEW; a saved file is then not looked at and is left as it is, with an ERROR line of its own: it names the table _LAT_SAVED, says what table.tableExists answered - tableExists said <n>, and 0 is no table - and that the table is to be renamed or dropped before the job is run again. Where CAS refuses the question for <table>_NEW, or the PROC CAS step that asks it halts, nothing is uploaded either: the job ends with ERROR: Load-Accelerator-Tables: CAS did not say whether there is a table <caslib>.<table>_NEW, the name the file is uploaded under first. ... and SYSCC 1012, and Load-Fact-Sheets.sas writes WARNING: CAS did not say whether there is a table <caslib>.<table>_NEW, ... (not run in SAS). Before, the programs loaded under the name with replace and dropped it again; whether that can take a global table of a site rests on what CAS does with a session table that has the name of a global one. Measured in the third pass of 2026-10-13, in casuser with test table names. With a global table <releaseTable>_NEW of 19 rows made first: the WARNING with tableExists said 2, no upload, and both tables with the rows and the created time of before. Load-Fact-Sheets.sas, from a copy with three test table names: the same WARNING for <table>_NEW, that sheet not loaded, the other two loaded. With a table _LAT_SAVED of the session and a release table that was only its saved file, the job as it was then wrote the ERROR line of a file that could not be loaded, which named a cause that was not the case - the next run, without that table, loaded 796 rows from the same file -; that is what the line of its own is for. A name a session table and a global table both had, in one run: tableExists said 1 in the session that held both and 2 in another session; the first table.dropTable took the table of the session, the second the global one. Not measured: _LAT_SAVED as a global table, Load-Fact-Sheets.sas with the table names it ships with, and the condition code of a run whose only message is the WARNING - every run of the pass ended with SYSCC 1012 for the three fact sheet tables its test root lacked. The ERROR line for _LAT_SAVED as it is now was measured on 2026-10-14 with a table _LAT_SAVED of the session of 19 rows and a release table that was only its saved file: tableExists said 1, SYSCC 1012, that table with its 19 rows, and the saved file with its size and its time. A table of such a name that the session may not see is not found by the question. Load-Fact-Sheets.sas replaces each fact sheet table the same way: the upload of the sheet whose rows were counted is promoted under the name of the table and saved, and the sheet is not loaded a second time. Where the promote is refused, a table of that name that is in memory - the table could not be dropped - is left as it is; where none is, the table is loaded again from the file it was saved to before. Each of these outcomes, and a load from the file that fails as well, is a WARNING of its own. Where CAS refuses the question whether such a table is in memory, nothing is loaded either; the WARNING then says that the table was not loaded again from the file it was saved to before. A sheet whose count CAS refused is a sheet CAS did not take (-1 stands for a table that CAS did not say is there or did not count). A swap whose PROC CAS step halted writes WARNING: Nothing said what became of the sheet - messages above -, the table <caslib>.<table> may not hold it. Not run in SAS. As first built for this release the program dropped its trial and loaded the sheet a second time, so a failure of CAS between the drop and that load left the site without the table. The swap ran on 2026-10-13, from a copy of the program with test table names in casuser: 30, 16 and 5 rows, each table global and saved, no WARNING, one load per sheet, and the same rows after a second run; the program that ran on 2026-10-12 was the one with the second load. In the second pass of 2026-10-13 such a copy ran with the request for the folder: pointed at a folder that is not there it wrote NOTE: 404 Not Found, one WARNING per sheet and no ERROR line and ended with SYSCC 0, and with the folder Data of a test root it loaded 30, 16 and 5 rows. Not run in SAS: a drop or a promote that is refused, and the program as it ships, whose table names are not settings. In a compute context whose session is another user than the one who started the job, the log holds one NOTE that says so. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-12 in the SAS Job Execution compute context: the NOTE, and then the file was read and the table loaded. One user written with a domain is one person; that comparison is not run in SAS. releaseTable names a release table only: a table of that name that lacks one of the ten columns every release table has - all but builder_part, which the table of 2.2.0 lacks - is left as it is, and the job ends with an ERROR line and SYSCC 1012. Measured on 2026-10-13 with a table made from sashelp.class: the ERROR line, the table unchanged (19 rows, 5 columns, the same time stamps), no _NEW table left, SYSCC 1012. That check looked at a table in memory only. Where no table of that name is in memory, the job now lists the files of the CAS library, loads <name>.sashdat - what a restart of the CAS server leaves of a saved table - as a table of its session, reads its columns and drops it. A file that lacks the columns or cannot be loaded is left as it is, with an ERROR line of its own; a saved release table is loaded again. Where CAS refuses to list the files, the job drops the upload again and loads no table, with ERROR: Load-Accelerator-Tables: no table <caslib>.<table> is in memory, and CAS refused to list the files of the CAS library <caslib> (the ERROR lines above), so it is not known whether a file a table of that name was saved to is there. ... and SYSCC 1012. Measured in the second pass of 2026-10-13 in casuser, which held files of other tables: with a table of 19 rows that was only its saved file and is no release table, the job loaded the file as _LAT_SAVED, wrote its ERROR line - no table casuser.<name> is in memory, and the file a table of that name was saved to in the CAS library casuser could not be loaded or lacks columns of a release table. The file was left as it is and nothing was loaded (the wording of that build; the line now says the upload of ACCELERATOR_RELEASES.csv was dropped again and no table <caslib>.<table> was loaded) - and the file had the size and the time of before; with a release table that was only its saved file, the job loaded the file the same way and then loaded, promoted and saved the table (781 rows). What table.fileInfo answers for a CAS library without any file is not measured. Where CAS refuses another action the job goes by there - the question whether the upload, the release table or _LAT_SAVED is there, the count of the rows of the upload, or the listing of the columns of a table - the job drops the upload again and loads no table, with ERROR: Load-Accelerator-Tables: CAS refused an action the job goes by to decide whether the upload takes the place of the table <caslib>.<table> - the ERROR lines above. ... and SYSCC 1012. Before, a refused listing of the columns gave the line of a table that is no release table. Not run in SAS. The job writes an ERROR line and sets SYSCC to 1012 when a parameter is refused, when the release table is left as it is with an ERROR line of its own, and when one of the four tables is not in the CAS library at its end or CAS does not say whether it is - a question CAS refused, or a PROC CAS step of the check that halted: the line names every table the check got no answer for. A check whose PROC CAS step halted ran in the ninth pass, on 2026-10-15, and its line named all four tables; a question CAS refused is not run in SAS. mdb load-releases and mdb load-facts load the same tables from a checkout and stay the way to load them from a workstation.
