The credentials commands, in the domain and for the group of the pass and for the test account: credentials-init, credentials-add for the group and for the user, credentials-apply after its dry run (4 entries stored for each), credentials-report (2 of 2 named identities hold a credential), credentials-remove for both, credentials-apply after its dry run, and credentials-report (2 of 2 identities marked state: absent hold none), each with exit code 0. The job programs of the first root, each in three states of the CAS sessions, and the steps LLM - Log Parser 2.12 and LLM - Get All Prompts 2.7: see The Pass of 2026-10-14. Create-Optimization-Dataset.sas failed where the option SESSREF named a session that was ended while _optbuild was connected. The Prompt Builder of the first root - the bundle the deploy wrote there, given to the browser at an address of the test system and opened without a write; the address of its form in SAS Job Execution (_action=form) answered the shell of the web application of SAS Job Execution 3.1.5 instead. A stand-in in the browser added throw-away LLMs and decision models to the listings and answered their options.json. An LLM whose options.json holds an enum whose values are numbers, an enum without values or whose default is not one of its values, a bool with the default 1, an API_KEY whose default is 5, or a base_url whose default is an object or null was shown disabled with the note The options.json of this model is not one this page can read, in English and in German, and was in none of the lists. One with a label and a description of temperature that are no texts and an API_KEY with a number as its label was usable, its temperature a number field; one with the temperature low, an enum of texts and a bool whose default is the text true was usable with a text field, a choice and a ticked box. A decision model with further options of any kind was usable, one whose API_KEY default is 5 was disabled with that note. Every LLM and decision model of the test system was usable. On the workstation: mdb generate, validate and retire of a manifest with an option the rule refused - an enum without values or whose default is not one of its values, a bool whose default is 1, an API_KEY whose default is 5, a default of .nan - each printed its one line and ended with exit code 1 without changing a file. Not run against SAS Viya: what was changed after the eleventh pass - in mdb the refusal by import of an options.json where what it reads of it breaks the rule of an option, the one line of validate and add for an option whose name holds a line break, the refusal by retire of a generated file edited by hand before it saves the manifest, and the refusal of an option name with a comma or a colon and of a text default or an enum value with a comma, all run on the workstation; in the job programs the option SESSREF that Create-Optimization-Dataset.sas sets to a connected _optbuild where the option names a session that was ended; and in the Prompt Builder the id of each option's control (optionControlId), the temperature 0 of a judge only where its temperature is a number, and the refusal of an option name with a comma or a colon and of a text default or an enum value with a comma (bundle da79bbf8…), driven against the mock of the harness only. Of what was changed after the tenth pass, all but what the eleventh pass measured: in mdb the rule of an option of options.json that register checks before it writes (run on the workstation with SAS Viya replaced by a stand-in), and the order of retire, which renders before it saves the manifest (run on the workstation); and in the Prompt Builder what a run sends of each option, and the polls of an optimization job and of an ingestion sent one at a time (oneAtATime). Of what was changed after the ninth pass, all but the job programs and the two steps, which the eleventh pass ran: in mdb the traceback of an exception that neither a command of mdb nor the audit script caught and the message of a usage error of click, both now printed without control characters, the text of each exception in that traceback on the one line that names it (a line break in an answer is a blank), the same one line for the text of a caught exception in every line of mdb that can show an answer, the refusal of an empty port in SAS_VIYA_URL, and the refusal of a value of a credentials manifest that YAML does not read as text (or as a list for only, as true or false for verbatim) and the quotes that credentials-init, and credentials-add without a manifest, put around a value of the starter manifest where YAML would read it otherwise; and in the Prompt Builder the read back of a launch by the name in its request and the line of a launch whose job is not among the running jobs, the guard on the window, also for a click on a node inside a control, the box Best Decision Model and every text of the manifest of a decision template that names it, the check of every JSON file the page reads from SAS Model Manager, field for field, a tracker whose entries are not rows of a run among them, the prompts and model names of a saved run drawn as text, the chairman list and a loaded run without an LLM that cannot be used, one Best Decision Model per decision run, a model named like a field every object has that a saved run keeps, and a model of a name the page reads as a field of a run, or __proto__, that is not offered, and the reason its note gives. Of what was changed after the eighth pass, all but what the ninth pass measured - in mdb the line where the HEAD of a sign-in with SAS_VIYA_TOKEN or the SAS Viya CLI login gets no answer, which went to an address on the workstation, the HEAD of a CLI login, the line of a certificate that fails, and the refusal of an identity id or a credential domain outside printable ASCII, which ends before a request; in the job programs what a PROC CAS step that halts does to the parser (LLM - Log Parser 2.11) and to Load-Fact-Sheets.sas, and the severity the Python of the link takes for an answer; and in the Prompt Builder every page of a listing, the read back of a write without an answer, the lines for a history, a documentation or a result that cannot be read and for a file that holds nothing the page can read, the delete of an optimization run, Launch ingestion that waits for every question, Try again after Create setup, an action whose button is off, and the box of a decision run that Manifest takes, now Best Decision Model. Of what was changed after the seventh pass, all but the lines of mdb package-export for a test folder, which the eighth pass measured - in mdb the one line of a credentials request that gets no answer, the comparison of the answer of a refused write, the default a prompt shows, the lines for a 200 without a readable token, for a redirect to a page that answers 200 and for an address where nothing answers, the refusal of every empty value, of a --manifest that names a folder, of --env-file, --keys-file and --identity-type with a manifest, of an identity named twice with --identity and of an id with a line break, the line of mdb retire where SAS Viya cannot be used, the refusal of an identity id with another control character, a character of format or a blank at an end; in the job programs what a listing of saved files that CAS refused does to the parser (version 2.10), the link and Load-Accelerator-Tables, and what another action CAS refused does to the link, Load-Accelerator-Tables, Load-Fact-Sheets.sas, Build-RAG-Cost-View.sas and Get-All-Prompts.sas (LLM - Get All Prompts 2.5); and in the Prompt Builder the buttons that are off while a write is out, Launch ingestion and Run test among them, the trackers replaced in one upload, a Delete project that stops part of the way, a read that fails and the message of a delete of an optimization run whose answer is lost. Of what was changed after the sixth pass: the control characters mdb takes out of a value - the seventh pass saw an ESC taken out, on the workstation and in a file - and the quotes around a value in its sentences, the refusal of an identity listed twice, the line for a redirect whose target answers an error and for a 200 without a token, and in the credentials commands the comment on the state: line and the count of a credential that could not be read in the report; and in the job programs the ERROR line of the parser for a table whose rows can not be counted. Of what was changed after the fifth pass: the line for another status of the token address and one sign-in for Unauthorized grant type, which the sixth pass sent to a stand-in on the workstation; the row of a credential that cannot be read, which needs a second sign-in; the commands a line names but for the report mdb credentials-apply names; and in Start Here two objects of one name and a report with a reference beside it. Of what was changed after the fourth pass: one sign-in for an answer that says Bad credentials and the line for a 401 that sasctl cannot read, which the fifth pass sent to a stand-in on the workstation and not to SAS Logon; the two commands for two packages of which one is refused its reports, and the repeat with --no-reports, because no pass imported a report; the answer of a refused request whole and on one line in the messages other than the line of a refused write; mdb package-check for an id that is no commit; and the step of the workflow for a tag, which has not run on GitHub. And of what was built before it: a folder that cannot be created stopping the run, the other site settings, a report that is found at its place in the content root - the test roots held none -, the delete of the uploaded import package, and a delete the export is refused with its exit code 3. Never measured: an import of a package that holds the reports, and with it the capture and the write-back of the options, the import mapping and the commands file - that needs a system whose Prompt Builder report may be written; an import of a package whose root folder is at the root of SAS Content, which is how every release so far was installed; what the transfer service does with a folder or a report of the same name under another id, and with the neutral createdBy / modifiedBy / userName of the release package.
documents.s: What was measured, and what has not run

documents.t: An import without mdb leaves everything to the transfer service Measured on 2026-10-12 (see What was measured): the transfer service did not replace a file that was in the target folder under the same name with another id - it wrote the file of the package into no folder and reported its job as completed. An object has another id than the package names where it did not come from an import of a package of the same origin: created by mdb content-deploy, by the earlier deploy script, or by hand. After an import without mdb, read the tasks of the import job, and run mdb content-deploy --dry-run from a checkout of the release: it says of every file, custom step and job definition whether it equals the checkout. The one file imports like any transfer package. What mdb builders-import does beside the import is then hand work: the options of the Prompt Builder report are the defaults of the package afterwards — save them first, see Preserving builder options across a report import —, the tables stay bound to Public, the release table and the fact sheets are loaded by the job Load-Accelerator-Tables, and the access rules are yours to write. SAS Environment Manager. Import the JSON from SAS Environment Manager → Content → Import. Then correct the host in step 5: open the report and update the Data-Driven Content object's base URL to your SAS Viya server. SAS Viya CLI. Use the transfer plugin of the sas-viya command-line interface. This assumes you have installed the CLI, created a connection profile, logged in and installed the plugin as described in Introduction — SAS Viya CLI Setup. In the commands below substitute https://viya.example.com with your own SAS Viya URL. Point the package at your host. The package ships the Prompt Builder object pointing at the placeholder host https://your-sas-viya-host. Replace it in the JSON so that the imported report loads the app from your server (the percent-encoded program path after the host is left untouched): # bash / Linux / macOS sed -i 's#https://your-sas-viya-host#https://viya.example.com#' SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json # PowerShell / Windows (Get-Content SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json) ` -replace 'https://your-sas-viya-host','https://viya.example.com' | Set-Content SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json Upload the package — the command prints the new package's id: sas-viya transfer packages upload --file SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json Import it by that id: sas-viya transfer packages import --id <package-id> Or do both in one go, capturing the id (requires jq): pkg=$(sas-viya --output json transfer packages upload \ --file SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json | jq -r '.id') sas-viya --output text transfer packages import --id "$pkg" (On older transfer plugin versions the same commands are sas-viya transfer upload / sas-viya transfer import — they still work, marked deprecated.) The host is a transfer substitution The placeholder lives in the package's substitutions block, which is what SAS's import machinery is designed to remap. Editing the string before upload (step 1 above) is the simplest fix. Alternatively, remap it at import time with a mapping file: pass --mapping mapping.json to the upload and the CLI writes a JSON file whose substitutions block holds the entry with the placeholder URL — edit that value to your host, then pass the same file to the import: sas-viya transfer packages upload --file SAS-Agentic-AI-Accelerator.json --mapping mapping.json # edit mapping.json: replace https://your-sas-viya-host in the substitutions block sas-viya transfer packages import --id <package-id> --mapping mapping.json (sas-viya transfer get-mapping --id <package-id> regenerates the file for an already-uploaded package.) If you do neither, the report still imports; you then correct the object's base URL in step 5. After the import, continue at step 3 — the Job Execution definition and the report already exist under SAS Content > SAS Agentic AI Accelerator > Prompt Builder. A package from before 2.3.0 brings the old RAG UI back Packages exported before release 2.3.0 hold a report named RAG Builder and a job definition RAG-Builder-UI — the standalone RAG UI that is retired. Importing such a file through SAS Environment Manager or the CLI puts both back. mdb builders-import names such a package before it imports it; use the package of a current checkout.

Importing a report overwrites your configuration Every option you set on the Prompt Builder object — repository and project IDs, the SCR endpoint, the credential domain, the three switches, and for RAG the content root, the ingestion compute context and which vector stores the deployment offers — is stored inside the Visual Analytics report, not alongside it. A transfer package carries those values too, so importing a newer version of the report replaces your settings with whatever the package was built against. This does not fail loudly. The report still opens and the app still runs; it simply shows the package's defaults — RAG switched off, no project IDs. mdb builders-import reads the options before it imports and writes them back; for an import made any other way, save your options first. mdb builders-import without --options does both steps below by itself and keeps what it read in builder-options-captured-<time>.json. The two commands are for a file to keep with your deployment records, to edit before an import, to carry to another deployment, or for a package that is imported without mdb (see Model Definition Builder for installing the CLI and its [viya] extra): # BEFORE importing a new report package mdb options-save --file builder-options.json # AFTER the import mdb options-restore --file builder-options.json --dry-run # check what would change mdb options-restore --file builder-options.json # write it back options-save discovers the Model Manager repository and the LLM and embedding projects exactly as mdb setup does, then overlays whatever your live Prompt Builder report already holds — so a deployment that has been tuned is captured as tuned, not as freshly bootstrapped. Keep the resulting file with your deployment records; it supersedes the llm-prompt-builder.json seed as the record of how this environment is configured. options-restore writes back only the options named in the file. The newly imported report keeps its new layout, data items and objects, and regains your configuration. It also replaces the shipped placeholder host your-sas-viya-host - in the object's Data-Driven Content URL and in the viyaHost / SCREndpoint defaults - with SAS_VIYA_URL, so a report imported by hand needs no URL edit afterwards (mdb builders-import does both in one run). Points worth knowing: The report is matched by name (Prompt Builder). If you have renamed the report in your deployment, rename it in the file to match, or the restore skips it. An option the report does not have is reported, not inserted. That usually means the option was renamed or removed in the newer version of the app — worth reading the message rather than ignoring it. When the missing option is one the current Prompt Builder report has, the report on the site is an older one: everything it can hold is still written, and the command ends with exit code 1 so that the gap is not taken for a finished restore — import the package of this release and restore again. It is also why the shipped report already holds every option, including the ones that only show while a switch is on. A switch is saved as the word true or false, which is what its checkbox in the Options pane stores. A file saved with 2.2.x holds the same two words for enableOptimization, so it restores unchanged. sslVerify is saved and restored like every other option, as the same two words. A file saved with 2.2.x does not name it, and nothing supplies a value for it: the imported report keeps its own default, which is ticked. A package is exported with the option ticked: on a report that would ship it switched off, mdb package-export ends with exit code 1 and writes nothing. API keys are deliberately not saved. This file is meant to be kept with deployment paperwork and reviewed in a diff, which is no place for a provider key. The Prompt Builder reads its keys from the credential domain at run time — see Managing Credentials. The file records which deployment it came from. Restoring it against a different SAS Viya URL still works — moving configuration between environments is a legitimate thing to do — but the command says so first, because doing it by accident is exactly the failure this guards against. Concurrent edits fail loudly. The write is conditional on the report being unchanged since it was read, so a colleague editing the report in Visual Analytics at that moment causes an error rather than silently losing their work. A sign-in that is refused can pass. Seen on 2026-10-11 and again on 2026-10-12: a call of mdb ended with 401 Client Error at the sign-in and went through when it was repeated; the sign-in service of that system refused password grants that overlapped. mdb asks a refused sign-in again, up to three times (MDB_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS sets the number, and 1 switches the repeat off). A sign-in that is answered Bad credentials is not asked again. Neither is one answered Unauthorized grant type: the client may not use the password grant, whenever it is asked. Measured on 2026-10-13: /SASLogon/oauth/token answers a password grant with a wrong password with status 401, Content-Type: application/json, the 64-byte body {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Bad credentials"} and the header WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="UAA/client", error="unauthorized", error_description="Bad credentials". So a wrong password costs one failed sign-in per command. A refusal that stays ends the command with one line and exit code 2, which says how many sign-ins were made and what SAS Logon answered: SAS Viya at <url> refused the sign-in of <user> with SAS_VIYA_USER + SAS_VIYA_PASSWORD (1 sign-in made): Authentication failed for user '<user>' - sasctl says so for an answer whose error_description says "Bad credentials". ... or, for any other 401, ... (3 sign-ins made): HTTP 401 from /SASLogon/oauth/token with error "<error>" and error_description "<text>". .... That includes a 401 whose body sasctl cannot read as it expects - no JSON object, an error_description that is no text, Unauthorized grant type -: the line then names error and error_description where the answer has them. Both are shown whole and as SAS Logon wrote them. Any other status of the token address - a 500, a 503, a 400 - is not read as a refusal and not asked again; the command ends with one line, SAS Viya at <url> did not answer the sign-in of <user> ... with a token: HTTP <status> from /SASLogon/oauth/token ..., and exit code 2. So do a redirect of the token address to a page that answers an error, or to one that answers 200 without a token, and a 200 that carries no token mdb can read - no JSON, no access_token, or one that is null, no text or empty. With SAS_VIYA_USER + SAS_VIYA_PASSWORD, an address where nothing answers - a port nothing listens on, a certificate, a timeout - ends the command at the sign-in with SAS Viya at <url> could not be asked for the sign-in of <user> with SAS_VIYA_USER + SAS_VIYA_PASSWORD: <kind of exception> (<what requests says>). Check SAS_VIYA_URL and that SAS Viya can be reached from here. and exit code 2. With SAS_VIYA_TOKEN or the SAS Viya CLI login, the sign-in sends one HEAD of the address and does not read its answer. Where it gets no answer the command ends with SAS Viya at <url> could not be asked with the access token (SAS_VIYA_TOKEN): <kind of exception> (<what requests says>). Check SAS_VIYA_URL and that SAS Viya can be reached from here. - (the SAS Viya CLI login) for a login - and exit code 2. A certificate that fails ends the command with such a line, with SSLError in it, for every way in, the password grant too. mdb retire, which tags the definition without SAS Viya, prints the line of an address it cannot use or of a sign-in that failed after The registered model's status was not updated: and goes on, with exit code 0. A port in SAS_VIYA_URL (https://host:8443) is used. SAS_VIYA_URL is the address with its scheme, https://<host> or https://<host>:<port>: host:8443 without a scheme, a port that is no number or empty (https://<host>:), a second // behind the scheme, a blank inside the address and a user or a password in front of the host (shown as ***@) end the command with one line before anything is asked of SAS Viya; a host alone is taken as https. Blanks, tabs and line breaks at either end of the value are taken out. Not recorded: the body of the 401 that was seen while sign-ins overlapped. The output saved on 2026-10-12 shows that sasctl 1.11.8 passed that refusal on as the HTTPError of requests, which it does for a 401 whose error_description does not say Bad credentials; a refusal like it is asked up to three times, as before. On 2026-10-13 twelve and then 24 correct password grants sent at the same moment were all answered 200 (2.6 to 3.5 s): the refusal did not come back, and the 124 sign-ins of the second pass of that day were each answered 200. In the third pass of that day a wrong password and three other refusals were sent to a stand-in on the workstation, not to SAS Logon - one sign-in and the line for Bad credentials, and for the rest three sign-ins, or one with MDB_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS=1, and the other line, as the command was then -, and with :443 in SAS_VIYA_URL a dry run sent the system the 73 requests of the run without it. The repeat, the single sign-in for Bad credentials and for Unauthorized grant type, the lines of a refusal, the line for another status, and the lines of a redirect, of a 200 without a token and of an address where nothing answers are not run against SAS Viya, and neither is the HEAD of a sign-in with a token or a CLI login: the answer SAS Viya gives it was not measured. The refusal of an address that cannot be used was measured in the two passes of 2026-10-14 (What was measured). Measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09 with the Prompt Builder report of this release, after the report had been saved once in SAS Visual Analytics with Enable RAG setups ticked: in a round of mdb options-save and mdb options-restore, the dry run of the restore named six options to write and none that the report lacks, and the restore wrote them. On a brand-new environment with no live report to capture from, run mdb options-save anyway: with nothing to overlay it writes the discovered values alone, which is the same content the seed file carries.
documents.s: Preserving builder options across a report import

documents.t: Up to release 2.2 the RAG Builder had a report of its own, named RAG Builder, with its own options. A site that upgrades still has it, and its options are carried into the Prompt Builder report by a fold that all three commands share: mdb options-save reads the live RAG Builder report when one exists and writes one Prompt Builder section. mdb builders-import without --options reads both reports the same way before it imports. Run mdb options-save before the import and before deleting the old report — afterwards the new report holds its own defaults, and what the Prompt Builder report holds always wins over the old report. A site that imported first still has a way back while the old report exists: options-save names every value of the old report that it did not carry, with what the old report held. Copy the ones you want into builder-options.json and run mdb options-restore. mdb options-restore and mdb builders-import --options fold a file saved with 2.2.x, which has a RAG Builder section, in the same way before they write. Nothing is ever written to the retired report, and nothing is deleted. What the fold does, and prints as it does it: In the old report In the Prompt Builder section The RAG options (embeddingProjectID, contentRoot, casServer, storeSslmode, deletedPolicy, retainDays, recordHistory, embedReplicas, persistElements, persistChunks, enable_pgvector, enable_singlestore) Carried under the same name with the stored value, where the Prompt Builder section has none computeContext Becomes ragComputeContext. It is never written to the Prompt Builder's computeContext, which is the context of the optimization job viyaHost, modelRepositoryID, SCREndpoint, deploymentType, credentialDomain The Prompt Builder value is kept; a different value in the old report is printed. If the credential domains differ, the RAG part now reads its secrets from the kept one — add the vector-store entries to it. If the kept value is none, there is no domain to add them to and RAG cannot be used: the message names the domain of the old report — set credentialDomain to it in the file before restoring, or in the Options pane afterwards. Models without an API key are called as before enabledBackends Dropped — it has been unused since the per-store switches exist (nothing) enableRag is set to true when the site had the report RAG Builder — live, or as the RAG Builder section of a file saved from one — and only if the Prompt Builder section does not hold an enableRag yet. The sign is a content root or a CAS server in the old section, which the report shipped with 2.2.x holds from the start The old report does not record whether anyone used it, so the fold switches RAG on at every site that had it. A site that does not use RAG runs mdb options-save, sets "enableRag": "false" in the Prompt Builder section of builder-options.json and imports with mdb builders-import --options builder-options.json, or clears Enable RAG setups in the Options pane afterwards. A 2.2.x file that was saved while no RAG Builder report existed holds only discovered values in its RAG Builder section; enableRag is then not set and RAG stays off. While a report named RAG Builder is still on the site, options-restore and builders-import say so on every run: it keeps serving the old standalone UI with its own options. Once the Prompt Builder report shows your RAG setups, delete the report RAG Builder and the job definition RAG-Builder-UI next to it (SAS Environment Manager → Content, or SAS Drive), and give the people who used it Read access to the Prompt Builder folder if they did not have it - see Access to the content folder. mdb deletes nothing; mdb content-deploy and the in-place part of mdb builders-import name the two objects - RAG/RAG Builder (report) and RAG/RAG-Builder-UI (job definition) - among what is in the folder and not in the package. Afterwards bookmarks to that report and to the URL of RAG-Builder-UI are dead. A package that was exported before 2.3.0 still holds both objects, and importing one brings them back.

You have two options: Option A — use the prebuilt file (recommended). Download the ready-to-use dist/index.html from the repository. No Node.js or build step is required — skip straight to step 2. Or copy the code from there to your clipboard and move to step 2. Option B — build it yourself. With Node.js (^20.19 || >=22.12) installed: git clone https://github.com/sassoftware/sas-agentic-ai-accelerator.git cd sas-agentic-ai-accelerator/LLM-Prompt-Builder npm install npm run build This produces the same single-file dist/index.html, with all three kinds in it — there is no separate build for the RAG Builder. See the project README for local development and customization details.

The single-file app is served to Visual Analytics through SAS Job Execution: In SAS Data and AI Studio, click on New > Job definition to create a new Job Definition In the Job Definition (edit) tab go to the right hand side bar and click on the first icon (Associate a Form) and change it from Prompt designer to HTML form. Copy the full contents of dist/index.html and paste it into the Job Definition (edit) tab Save the job to the place you want it in SAS Content - note that people that should be using it need read access. On the right hand side bar click the second icon (Properties), expand the Details section and copy the value under Job URL - it should look something like this: https://your-viya-host/SASJobExecution/SASJobExecution/?_program=path-to-your-job-definition after the path value add the following: &_action=form, as this enables us to view the HTML form without having to provide any SAS code. Save that URL as we will need it in fifth step. Why the build base64-encodes its scripts SAS Job Execution serves HTML through a Go template engine that treats {{ … }} as directives. The build base64-encodes every inline <script> and decodes it at runtime so the minified bundle — which inevitably contains {{/}} — is not corrupted. This is automatic and requires no action.
documents.s: 2. Create a SAS Job Execution definition

documents.t: The Prompt Builder resolves provider API keys from a SAS Viya credential domain (default agentic-ai-keys) under the identity of the signed-in user — a user credential overrides a group credential, and models the user holds no key entry for are shown disabled with a note. RAG setups take the vector-store credentials, and where each store lives, from the same domain. Set the domain up once with the CLI-based scripts as described in Managing Credentials; no data source, table, or report assignment is involved. Keys stay governed Keys live encrypted in the Credentials service — never in the report definition, the URL, or a data table. Who holds a credential in the domain (directly or via group membership) is who can run paid model calls.
documents.s: 3. Provide the API keys via the credential domain

documents.t: To let the app run inside SAS Visual Analytics, set the following Content Security Policy directives via SAS Environment Manager → Configuration → View Definitions. SAS Visual Analytics — sas.commons.web.security → SAS Visual Analytics → content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src * blob: data:; frame-src * blob: data: mailto:; connect-src 'self' *.sas.com login.microsoftonline.com graph.microsoft.com *.arcgis.com *.arcgisonline.com; object-src 'none' SAS Job Execution — sas.commons.web.security → SAS Job Execution → content-security-policy (replace <sas-viya-host> with your environment's URL). The 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' in script-src are what allow the base64-decoded single-file bundle to run: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https://<sas-viya-host>; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src * blob: data:; child-src 'self' blob: data: ; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; IFrame sandbox — verify the sas.visualanalytics definition's IFrame Sandbox Attribute Value contains at minimum allow-same-origin allow-scripts. note That sandbox does not include allow-popups, which is why the links that leave the page — "Open in SAS Model Manager", the link to a saved prompt-test, the links to a decision in the delete dialogs — copy their URL instead of forcing a new tab on a normal click (use the browser's right-click → Open link in new tab). Add allow-popups to the IFrame Sandbox Attribute Value to let these links open a tab directly. A link is copied only where no tab opened: with allow-popups a click opens the tab and leaves the clipboard alone. The page carries the referrer policy same-origin, a meta element in its head: what it asks of another origin than its own carries no Referer, what it asks of its own origin keeps it. A link to another site — the user guide link of the Optimize step — therefore does not tell that site the address of your SAS Viya host. A tab the page opens on SAS Viya itself, such as SAS Model Manager, is told where the click came from, as before, and the calls to SAS Viya keep their Referer; that holds where the page is served from the SAS Viya origin, as in the setup described on this page, and not where the viyaHost parameter names another origin. A call to a model container on another host carries no Referer either, but that host still learns where the page runs: a browser names the origin of the page in the Origin header of every cross-origin call, whatever the referrer policy. Restart the following kubernetes pods of your SAS Viya environment if saving the changes didn't trigger a restart automatically: sas-job-execution sas-job-execution-app sas-logon-app sas-visual-analytics sas-visual-analytics-app Example kubectl command: kubectl get pods -n <your-namespace> -o name | grep -E 'pod/sas-job-execution|pod/sas-logon-app|pod/sas-visual-analytics' | xargs kubectl delete -n <your-namespace>

If you imported the transfer package then open up the SAS Visual Analytics report under SAS Content > SAS Agentic AI Accelerator > Prompt Builder > Prompt Builder and then continue. In a Visual Analytics report, add a Data-Driven Content object and in the Options pane under Web Content enter the URL from the previous step or if you imported it update the base URL to your SAS Viya server. Assign the release table to the object: in the Data pane pick Public.ACCELERATOR_RELEASES (loaded by mdb setup or mdb load-releases; the library and name follow SAS_CAS_LIBRARY / SAS_RELEASES_TABLE) and add any of its columns to the object's role. A Data-Driven Content object does not render until it has a data assignment; the Prompt Builder itself reads nothing from it, and provider keys still come from the credential domain (step 3). The table carries the accelerator's changelog - one row per release and per change, with a component column - so the same report can show what changed for the Prompt Builder next to the object. A change to the Prompt Builder is one row for each part of it that it concerns, named in the column builder_part (Prompt, Decision, RAG): a page that lists the changes keeps its filter on component and gets a button bar on builder_part, with which a reader picks the part - see The release table for the rows and for what a page built before the column shows. Open the object's Properties panel and set the configuration values (see below).
documents.s: 5. Add the object to a Visual Analytics report

documents.t: The object publishes one list of options, in the order of the tables below: first the options every kind shares, then the three switches, each directly followed by the options that only matter while it is on. Visual Analytics writes every value into the object's URL under the URL parameter name and reloads the app, which is how a changed switch makes its options appear or disappear. The five environment-specific values are exactly those captured in your llm-prompt-builder.json — the file produced in the Setup SAS Model Manager chapter (regenerate it by re-running mdb setup if you have lost it), where each stands under the name of its URL parameter: modelRepositoryID, llmProjectID, embeddingProjectID, SCREndpoint and deploymentType. mdb builders-import writes the same five into the report by itself, so copying them by hand is only needed for a report you built yourself. Shared by every kind — always shown: Properties-panel field URL parameter Default Meaning SAS Viya host viyaHost the embedding origin SAS Viya base URL. Leave blank to default to the embedding origin. Model Manager repository ID modelRepositoryID blank Model Manager repository in which new prompt projects, decision projects and RAG projects are created. Required by every kind. LLM project ID llmProjectID blank Model Manager project holding the available LLM definitions (each with an options.json). Required for prompt and decision templates; a page that only builds RAG setups can leave it blank. SCR endpoint SCREndpoint blank Base URL of the SCR endpoint hosting the LLM and decision model containers and, for RAG, the embedding containers. Required for prompt and decision templates; RAG reads a blank value as <SAS Viya host>/llm, the host being the SAS Viya host option or the address the page is opened at. For a RAG setup the one resolved value goes to the ingestion job, Test retrieval, the Embed step of the generated SAS Studio flow and the retrieval model, so it has to be reachable from the compute session of the ingestion and from the publishing destination — set the option where the address of the page is not. Deployment type deploymentType k8s k8s or aca (Azure Container Apps / Instances) — how the model containers are deployed. See Container Deployment. Default judge model judgeModel blank Optional. Name of an LLM in the LLM project used by default for the LLM-as-a-Judge comparison; prompt engineers can still override it in the app. Leave blank for no default. Model card report URI modelCardReportURI blank Optional. A SAS Visual Analytics report path (/reports/reports/<uuid>). When set, manifesting the best prompt embeds that report on its model card as the custom chart, hosted from the SAS Viya host above. Leave blank to omit. Credential domain credentialDomain agentic-ai-keys Credential domain that provider API keys and, for RAG, the vector-store credentials resolve from (see step 3). Enter none when only key-less self-hosted models are used: no credential is then looked up for prompt and decision templates. RAG needs a domain — with none its card is shown disabled with that reason. The SAS code of an LLM call that LLM - Create LLM Call, LLM - Get Options and Create-LLM-Call.sas write does not read this option: it names agentic-ai-keys in its line %let API_KEY_DOMAIN=agentic-ai-keys;, which a site with another domain edits. Verify TLS certificates in manifested models sslVerify ticked A checkbox. Ticked: a model manifested in the Prompt Builder verifies the certificate of the model container it calls. Not ticked: models manifested from then on do not verify it, carry the tag TLS-Verification-Off in SAS Model Manager, and the step that manifests them shows a warning. See below. Verify TLS certificates in manifested models​ Three kinds of manifested model make an HTTPS call themselves when they are scored: a prompt template manifested with Include the LLM call in the manifested model, a decision template, and the retrieval model of a RAG setup. Each verifies the certificate of what it calls against the CA bundle of the SAS Viya deployment. sslVerify decides what is written into the score code of such a model when it is manifested: It is a default written at manifest time. Changing the option changes the models manifested from then on. A model that is already manifested keeps what it was manifested with, in SAS Model Manager and on every destination it is published to, until it is manifested again. It changes nothing else. The calls the Prompt Builder page makes in the browser, the ingestion job of a RAG setup, and a prompt manifested for the Call LLM node (where the node makes the call) are as before. The SAS Studio custom step has a checkbox of its own. A retrieval model registered with RAG - Register Setup is not manifested on this page, and the step does not read sslVerify. Its checkbox Verify TLS certificates in the registered retrieval model (Runtime section, ticked by default) writes the same line into the same score code and sets and removes the same tag — see RAG Ingestion and Retrieval. A destination can overrule it in both directions with an environment variable: LLMCONTAINERSSLVERIFY for prompt and decision templates, RAGEMBED_SSLVERIFY and RAGSTORE_SSLVERIFY for the retrieval model. true switches verification on for a model manifested with it off, false the reverse — see Deployment of Decisions. Off is visible. A model manifested while the option is not ticked carries the tag TLS-Verification-Off, on all three kinds, and manifesting it again with the option ticked removes the tag. The step shows a warning before the click that names this option and the variable that turns verification back on: Finalize for a decision template, Finalize for a prompt only while Include the LLM call in the manifested model is ticked, and Manifest setup for a RAG setup. Finding the models that do not verify lists such models and names the line to look for in a score code. A report saved before the option existed shows the checkbox ticked, and so verifies. The state of the checkbox is stored with the report: it is there again after the report is saved and reopened. Leave it ticked unless a destination cannot verify. The case it exists for is SAS Micro Analytic Service running Python in a container that does not have the CA bundle; Publishing to SAS Micro Analytic Service: the certificate bundle describes it, the fix that keeps verification on, and when switching it off is acceptable — a test system on a closed cluster network, not production. In the URL the option reads like a switch: Visual Analytics writes sslVerify=true or sslVerify=false; in a URL written by hand 0, no and off also switch verification off, in any case. A blank, missing or any other value keeps it on. The three switches — always shown, each a checkbox: Properties-panel field URL parameter Default Ticked Not ticked Enable decision templates enableDecision ticked The Setup card offers decision templates for decision models, with the question designer, the Evaluate step and the typed manifest. The kind is not offered and nothing is shown for it. The Decision Model Project is not looked up and no decision model is called. Existing decision projects and templates are not listed; they stay untouched in SAS Model Manager. Enable prompt optimization (DSPy) enableOptimization not ticked Prompt templates gain the Optimize step, and the three Optimization: options below appear. See Enabling Prompt Optimization. No Optimize step, and no request to SAS Job Execution or to the folder of the optimize job. Enable RAG setups enableRag not ticked The Setup card offers the RAG setup, and the RAG: options below appear. Nothing is requested for RAG until a user chooses that kind — the RAG Builder is loaded on first use. The kind is not offered; nothing of the RAG Builder is loaded and no RAG project, embedding project, CAS library or content folder is requested. Stored RAG setups stay untouched. A switch that is off costs nothing at run time, which is the point of having it: a site that does not publish decision models, or has no vector store, should neither show the kind nor make requests that can only fail. With one kind left, the question What are you building? is not shown at all. The report stores a switch as the word true or false. Up to release 2.2 Enable prompt optimization (DSPy) was a dropdown with Enabled and Disabled that stored the same two words, so a report saved then keeps its setting: a stored true shows as a ticked checkbox. Only while prompt optimization is enabled: Properties-panel field URL parameter Default Meaning Optimization: compute context computeContext blank SAS Compute context the optimization job runs in. It must run as the requesting user — SAS Studio compute context does, the stock SAS Job Execution compute context does not, and the job ends there before its first model call. Its Python needs dspy. Not used by RAG. Optimization: job path optimizeJobProgram blank SAS Content path of the optimize job definition, e.g. /Public/Jobs/Optimize-Prompt-DSPy. Optimization: minimum samples minOptimizeSamples 30 Minimum dataset rows before an optimization run is allowed; the Optimize panel warns below 50. Only while RAG is enabled — what each one governs is explained in RAG Ingestion and Retrieval: Properties-panel field URL parameter Default Meaning RAG: embedding model project ID embeddingProjectID blank Model Manager project holding the registered embedding models. The RAG Builder lists that project instead of asking for a model name; without it no embedding model can be chosen and no setup can be saved. RAG: content root contentRoot /SAS Agentic AI Accelerator/RAG SAS Content folder that holds the RAG runtime - the folder RAG of the content folder, which the transfer package brings. Generated job definitions go to its generated subfolder unless a setup names another. RAG: CAS server casServer cas-shared-default CAS server of the ingestion ledger and the pipeline tables. RAG: ingestion compute context ragComputeContext blank SAS Compute context the ingestion job and the retrieval test run in. It must run as the requesting user — SAS Studio compute context does, the stock SAS Job Execution compute context does not. Launching and testing are refused until it is set. RAG: vector store TLS storeSslmode prefer How the ingestion connects to the vector store: prefer, require, verify-ca, verify-full, allow or disable. Stores other than PostgreSQL read disable as no TLS and anything else as TLS on. RAG: when a document disappears from the source deletedPolicy retire retire keeps its chunks as history that no retrieval returns; purge removes them for good. RAG: keep retired chunks for (days) retainDays 0 Retired chunk generations older than this are dropped after each load. 0 keeps them forever. RAG: record run history recordHistory on A checkbox. Writes rag_runs, rag_doc_events and rag_configs beside the collection and publishes the first two to CAS. RAG: embedding container replicas embedReplicas 1 How many replicas of the embedding container the deployment runs; the ingestion sizes its parallel calls from it. RAG: save the element table to disk persistElements 1 1 saves <prefix>_ELEMENTS to disk, 0 keeps it in memory only. The value is recorded on each setup; the SAS Studio flow that Manifest setup generates does not apply it yet and keeps this table in memory either way. RAG: save the chunk table to disk persistChunks 1 The same for <prefix>_CHUNKS; in the generated flow it reaches the enrichment step only so far. The ledger and the embedded chunks are always saved. RAG: offer pgvector (PostgreSQL) enable_pgvector on A checkbox per vector database: whether users may choose it for a new setup. A setup that already uses a withheld database keeps it and says so. RAG: offer SingleStore enable_singlestore on As above. Two compute contexts, two options computeContext is the context of the optimization job and ragComputeContext the context of the RAG ingestion; neither is ever read for the other. Both have to run as the requesting user: the stock SAS Job Execution compute context runs its servers as a service account, where an ingestion cannot reuse its CAS session (see the two prerequisites) and the optimization job ends before its first model call (see Enabling Prompt Optimization). They are two options because a site may give each job a context of its own, with the Python packages that job needs. Before release 2.3.0 the RAG Builder's own report called its context computeContext too; mdb options-save renames it when it carries that report's options over. info Until the object is configured it shows a "Configuration required" message and does not call SAS Viya, so it never fails against placeholder IDs. The message names what is missing for each side, and completing either is enough for the page to load: prompt and decision templates need the repository ID, the LLM project ID and the SCR endpoint; RAG setups need the repository ID, Enable RAG setups ticked and a credential domain other than none. A site with no LLM project therefore gets the RAG Builder alone. Every field can also be appended to the object's URL by hand using its URL parameter name above (for example &judgeModel=...&modelCardReportURI=/reports/reports/<uuid>), which is a reliable fallback if your Visual Analytics version does not render the options panel. For a switch, Visual Analytics writes true for a ticked checkbox and false for one that is not; in a URL written by hand a switch also reads 1, yes or on as on and 0, no or off as off. Anything else, and a blank or missing value, is its default.

The SAS Agentic AI Accelerator will create an additional model repository in your environment called LLM Repository. This repository will be used both to store the project which contains the LLMs, all the different prompting projects, the embedding models and the RAG setups. The repository and its projects are created by mdb setup, part of the Model Definition Builder. It creates the LLM Repository, the LLM Model Project and the Embedding Model Project if they do not already exist, and it is idempotent — running it again on an environment that is already set up changes nothing. (You do not have to run it explicitly at all: mdb register performs the same check automatically for the kind it registers. Running mdb setup up front is simply the tidiest way to bootstrap a fresh environment.) Install the CLI once, then run setup from within the locally cloned repository. The connection details are read from a .env file — see Providing credentials without the command line: # Install the CLI with the Viya extra (one time) pip install -e "Model-Definition-Builder/cli[viya]" # Create the repository and both model projects, and write the seed files mdb setup mdb setup reads the SAS Viya server from SAS_VIYA_URL and signs in with whichever credential you provide (see Signing in to SAS Viya - a password is not required), the point of contact from SAS_RESPONSIBLE_PARTY, the SCR base URL from SAS_SCR_ENDPOINT, and the deployment type from SAS_DEPLOYMENT_TYPE (k8s by default, or aca for Azure Container Apps/Instances). All of these live in your .env. It also loads the release table Public.ACCELERATOR_RELEASES into CAS (the caslib from SAS_CAS_LIBRARY, the name from SAS_RELEASES_TABLE) - the accelerator's changelog as one row per release and per change, a change to the Prompt Builder as one row for each of its parts (builder_part: Prompt, Decision, RAG) that it concerns. That is the table you assign to the Prompt Builder object in SAS Visual Analytics, see Deploying the Builder UIs; mdb builders-import reloads it with every import, mdb load-releases does it alone, and --no-releases skips it here. A first install is this command and then mdb builders-import, which imports the content folder - the Prompt Builder, the RAG runtime, the logging programs and the usage report -, and then the page Start Here with its installation check: see Install or upgrade with the transfer package. Running it produces two files as outputs: llm-prompt-builder.json, the seed for the Prompt Builder - the one object behind No-Code Prompt Engineering, decision templates and No-Code RAG pipeline setups. It holds the five values that differ per environment, each under the name of the option it belongs to: modelRepositoryID, llmProjectID, embeddingProjectID, SCREndpoint and deploymentType. mdb builders-import writes the same values into the report by itself, so the file is only needed to fill the options in by hand - see the page Deploying the Builder UIs. sas-viya-cli-commands.txt, the authorization commands described below. Use --out <dir> to write those files somewhere other than the current directory, or --no-files to create only the repository and projects. Run mdb setup --help for the full list.

mdb reads any parameter from an environment variable or a .env file instead of the command line. This keeps your credentials out of your shell history and the process list. The order of precedence is: command-line argument, then environment variable, then .env file, then the built-in default. To use a .env file, copy the template and edit it (mdb reads it itself, nothing else to install): cp .env.example .env The available variables (documented in .env.example) map to the arguments as follows: Environment variable Purpose SAS_VIYA_URL SAS Viya server URL (falls back to the SAS Viya CLI profile's sas-endpoint) SAS_VIYA_TOKEN An OAuth access token - the first credential tried SAS_VIYA_USER / SAS_VIYA_PASSWORD Username and password for the password grant - tried second SAS_VIYA_VERIFY_SSL Set to false only for an unrecognized self-signed certificate SAS_SCR_ENDPOINT Base SCR endpoint URL SAS_DEPLOYMENT_TYPE k8s (default) or aca SAS_RESPONSIBLE_PARTY Point of contact recorded in Model Manager SAS_PUBLISH_DESTINATION Default SCR publishing destination (mdb publish, overridable with -d) SAS_CAS_LIBRARY / SAS_CAS_SERVER CAS library (default Public) and server for the tables mdb setup, load-releases and load-facts load SAS_RELEASES_TABLE Name of the release table (default ACCELERATOR_RELEASES) The .env file is git-ignored, so your credentials are never committed. With the connection details in .env (or a SAS Viya CLI login, below), mdb setup needs no arguments at all.
documents.s: Providing credentials without the command line

documents.t: Every mdb command that talks to SAS Viya signs in the same way, trying three credentials in this order and using the first one that is set. Each command prints which one it used (SAS Viya: <server> with ...). SAS_VIYA_TOKEN - an OAuth access token from any source. mdb reads its expiry from the token and tells you when it has run out instead of failing on the first request. SAS_VIYA_USER + SAS_VIYA_PASSWORD - the password grant. This is the classic route and still the simplest for a service account, but it does not work when SAS Viya authenticates through an external identity provider (SSO / SCIM / OIDC), where the only account with a password is typically sasboot. The SAS Viya CLI login. If neither of the above is set, mdb uses the access token the SAS Viya CLI keeps in ~/.sas/credentials.json: sas-viya profile init # once: the server URL sas-viya auth loginCode # opens the browser and completes the SSO login mdb setup # -> SAS Viya: https://... with the SAS Viya CLI login (profile Default, expires ...) sas-viya auth login (username and password at the prompt) fills the same file. The profile is Default unless SAS_CLI_PROFILE - the CLI's own variable - names another, and a login for a different server than SAS_VIYA_URL is refused rather than silently used. When the login expires, mdb says so; run sas-viya auth loginCode again. On an SSO site, route 3 is all you need: leave SAS_VIYA_USER and SAS_VIYA_PASSWORD out of .env, log in with the CLI, and the repository, projects and registered models are created in your name rather than a service account's. Route 1 exists for the cases where the token comes from somewhere else - a CI secret, the VS Code SAS extension, or an authorization-code flow you completed yourself.

By default newly created SAS Model Manager repositories are only authorized for access for the SAS Administrators group, please adjust the access rights as you require it for your environment - it is recommended add authorization on a group basis. Running mdb setup will produce a file called sas-viya-cli-commands.txt which contains the following groups and rules as a template to apply authorization to your environment. Of course this is just a basic template, please read through it carefully and adjust it to your needs: # Each command comes with a description, please read it and the documentation before running anything # First a Custom Group is created called LLM Consumers - if you do not want use this group, skip this step and replace the name in subsequent commands sas-viya identities create-group --id LLMConsumers --name "LLM Consumers" --description "This group enables a general access to the LLM repository. This group is meant for anybody that requires access to it." # Add members to the LLM Consumers group sas-viya identities add-member --group-id LLMConsumers --group-member-id GroupYouWantToAdd # Second a Custom Group is created called Prompt Engineers - if you do not want use this group, skip this step and replace the name in subsequent commands sas-viya identities create-group --id PromptEngineers --name "Prompt Engineers" --description "This group enables its members to create, update and delete Prompt Engineering projects in the LLM repository" # Add members to the Prompt Engineers group sas-viya identities add-member --group-id PromptEngineers --group-member-id GroupYouWantToAdd # Create two rules that open up access to the LLM Repository for the LLM Consumers sas-viya authorization create-rule -o /folders/folders/folder-uuid -g LLMConsumers -p Read,Add,Remove -d "Enables the LLM Consumers to interact with the LLM repository" --reason "You are not part of the LLM Consumers group" sas-viya authorization create-rule --container-uri /folders/folders/folder-uuid -g LLMConsumers -p Read,Add,Update,Remove,Delete -d "Enables the LLM Consumers to interact with the LLM repository" --reason "You are not part of the LLM Consumers group" # Create a rule to enable the Prompt Engineers to create new projects in the LLM repository sas-viya authorization create-rule -o /modelRepository/repositories/repo-uuid -g PromptEngineers -p Read,Add,Create,Update,Remove,Delete -d "Enables the group to create prompt engineering projects in the LLM repository" --reason "You are not part of the prompt engineering group"

The Troubleshooting Guide tries to provide solution orientied fixes to reported issues. If your issue is not on this please raise an issue or if you already have a solution please contribute it as a pull request.
This part of the troubleshooting guide describes issues that can occur when working with this in SAS Intelligent Decisioning.

This error can be encountered during testing within SAS Intelligent Decisioning. Here is how the issue might show up for a variable called llmurl: ERROR: Compilation error. ERROR: Line 167: Duplicate declaration for llmurl. This error occurs when your model (for example the prompt template model) has the same variable twice in its Variable tab inside of SAS Model Manager. If that is the case, you have identified the source of the error. In order to fix this, please ensure that you are using the current version of the Prompt Builder UI (compare the versions using the project CHANGELOG). If you created the model not using that tool, please make sure that model variables are correctly updated when creating new versions of the model.

This error can be encountered when testing or running a decision that contains a prompt template that was manifested with the Include the LLM call in the manifested model option: ERROR: Line 53: DS2 "pymas" package encountered a failure in the 'execute' method. It means that the Python score code of the model raised an unhandled error. The most common cause is the LLM call itself failing — for example because the certificate of the endpoint hosting the LLM containers is not trusted or the endpoint is not reachable from where the model runs. Here is how to address it: Ensure that you are using the current version of the Prompt Builder UI (compare the versions using the project CHANGELOG) and manifest the prompt again. Since version 1.0.0 a failing LLM call no longer raises an error: the failure reason is returned through the response output of the model (e.g. LLM call failed: ...) and parse_status returns 0. Keep the response output selected while validating a decision, so you can see why a call failed. If the response output reports a TLS/certificate problem: the model verifies the connection against the CA bundle at /security/trustedcerts.pem, which SAS Viya mounts into the pods of CAS and of the compute servers and which covers LLM containers hosted behind the SAS Viya ingress. If your LLM containers are hosted elsewhere, point the LLMCONTAINERCABUNDLE environment variable to a CA bundle that covers them — see Deployment of Decisions for all supported environment variables and how to set them per runtime. If the problem only shows once the decision is published to MAS, see CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED in the response of a published model below. If the model fails at publish time instead (py.publish() failed), the requests package is most likely missing from the Python environment. The manifested model ships a requirements.json, so SAS Container Runtime destinations install the package automatically during publishing; for runs in SAS Intelligent Decisioning tests, CAS or MAS, an administrator has to make the requests package available in the configured Python environment. Please note that the Call LLM node path (prompt templates manifested without the included LLM call) is not affected by this — for that path see the Micro Analytic Service and SAS Container Runtime sections below.
documents.s: DS2 "pymas" package encountered a failure in the 'execute' method

documents.t: This part of the troubleshooting guide describes issues that can occur when publishing decisions or models that call the LLMs to the SAS Micro Analytic Service (MAS).

This error occurs because the endpoint under which the LLMs are hosted doesn't have a valid certificate from the standpoint of your SAS Micro Analytic Service. This fix has to be done by an administrator with the ability to patch the SAS Viya deployment - for more information check out the SAS documentation: Go to $BASE_PATH/sasinstall/sas-bases/examples/sas-microanalytic-score/config and copy the mas-add-environment-variables.yaml Then adjust the yaml in the following way - this assumes that you have deployed the LLMs behind the same ingress as SAS Viya if not you need to point it to your certificate accordingly: --- apiVersion: builtin kind: PatchTransformer metadata: name: mas-add-environment-variables patch: |- - op: add path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/- value: name: SSLCALISTLOC value: /security/trustedcerts.pem target: group: apps kind: Deployment name: sas-microanalytic-score Add the transformer to your kustomization.yaml and apply it. Check the environment variables of the sas-microanalytic-score pod definition and there under the sas-microanalytic-score container check that the environment variable was added accordingly. Now rerun your the decision/model call and check that the error has been actually fixed.
documents.s: 500 Internal Server Error - EXECUTEMETHOD failed for HTTP POST method with URL

documents.t: This error can be encountered in the publishing validation of a decision on a MAS destination, when the decision contains a model that calls the LLM or decision model container itself: a prompt template manifested with the Include the LLM call in the manifested model option, a decision template, or the retrieval model of a RAG setup. The validation ends without an error, and every row carries the message in the model's text output (response, answer or retrieval_status) while the other outputs are empty: Decision model call failed: HTTPSConnectionPool(host=..., port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /llm/von_1_2/von_1_2 (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError(1, '[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: self-signed certificate in certificate chain'))) The same decision returns answers in the in-app test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning, and a decision that uses the Call LLM node works on the same destination. The cause is that MAS runs the Python code of the model in a separate runner container that does not have the CA bundle (/security/trustedcerts.pem) the main container has. This fix has to be done by an administrator with the ability to patch the SAS Viya deployment: Confirm the cause and mount the bundle file into the Python runner container as described in Publishing to SAS Micro Analytic Service: the certificate bundle — the one file with a subPath mount, not the whole security volume, which also holds the private key directory of the pod. That keeps TLS verification on and is the fix for production. Check that /security/trustedcerts.pem is listed inside the runner container, and that nothing else is under /security there, with the commands given there. Run the publishing validation again and check that the rows carry answers. On a test system with a closed cluster network, verification can be switched off instead — with the option Verify TLS certificates in manifested models of the Prompt Builder, followed by manifesting the model again (for a retrieval model registered with the custom step RAG - Register Setup: with the step's checkbox Verify TLS certificates in the registered retrieval model, followed by running the step again), or with the environment variable LLMCONTAINERSSLVERIFY=false on the destination (RAGEMBED_SSLVERIFY=false for a retrieval model). The model then no longer checks which container answers; the same section says when that is acceptable. Where MAS runs Python in the runner container, set the variable on the runner as well — see the variable and the Python runner.

documents.t: The publishing validation of a decision on a MAS destination ends without an error, a row has HTTP status 201 and an empty error column — and every output of the decision is empty in that row, also the outputs of nodes that have nothing to do with each other. The log of the validation job has no ERROR and no WARNING line. The same decision returns its outputs in the in-app test of SAS Intelligent Decisioning, and the same validation, run again without any change, can return other rows empty than before. SAS Micro Analytic Service ended the execution of such a row because it took longer than 30 seconds. That was measured on 2026-10-11 on SAS Viya 2026.09, with a decision of three model nodes that were all manifested in the Prompt Builder: the retrieval model of a RAG setup, a prompt template with the included LLM call that is given the retrieved context, and a decision template. Three places show it: The table of the publishing validation: HTTP status 201, an empty error column, every output empty. Nothing in it names a timeout. A direct REST call of the step of the published module answers HTTP status 201 as well, with "executionState": "timedOut" and "outputs": []. The log of the pod sas-microanalytic-score: Failure encountered during execution in revision … of module context '…'. Return code: 0x8b3ff145. and Micro Analytic Service failed to execute method. With the log level debug, the scheduling thread writes 0x803fc006=tkWait() exactly 30.0 seconds after its line Scheduled work on worker thread, and the two failure lines follow. What was measured about the 30 seconds: The publishing validation sends the rows of its input table at the same time. Three rows were scheduled within 12 milliseconds. One call at a time stayed within them. In single calls the retrieval node took 0.2 seconds, the LLM node 1.3 to 4.2 seconds and the decision model node 1.7 to 4.1 seconds; a whole call took 6.5 to 9 seconds. Six single calls one after another all returned HTTP status 201, retrieval_status ok, three hits, an envelope of 1969 characters and the answer of the LLM from the retrieved context. Three rows at once did not. The durations the service logs for each node (NODE DURATION) were 0.2 to 2.2 seconds for the retrieval node, 5 to 6 seconds for the LLM node of the first row and more than 29 seconds for the two others, and 24 to 25 seconds for the decision model node while the LLM container was busy. The LLM and the decision model were both self-hosted and ran on the same CPU node; with the retrieved context the prompt of the LLM was about 900 characters, where it was about 50 without. The same validation gave two results. The same module with the same table, run twice without any change: the first run returned all three rows empty, the second returned one row complete — its three nodes had taken 29.65 seconds in total — and two empty. Three direct calls at once all answered timedOut, after 30.8, 31.7 and 36.5 seconds. In the measured decision a row was lost by the time its models took when they were called at the same time: the same rows came back complete in single calls, with nothing in the decision or in a model changed. That is one decision on one system, with two self-hosted models on one CPU node; another decision can be slow for another reason. What was ruled out for the measured one: the lengths of the variables of a model are not the cause: with the two context outputs of the retrieval model declared with 100 characters, single calls returned the envelope complete, with its 1969 characters (the lengths of the variables). A publishing validation that returned every row after a change to the decision or to a model had finished within the 30 seconds that time; run it more than once before reading a change as the remedy. What a site can do follows from the durations above; none of it was measured as a remedy: Fewer calls at once. Validate with a table of one row, or call the module row by row. A caller of the published decision that sends its requests one after another is the case that stayed within the time. A faster model, or models that do not share a node. The time was spent in the two self-hosted models on one CPU node: the decision model took 24 to 25 seconds while the LLM container was busy, where it took 1.7 to 4.1 seconds alone. Whether a GPU node, a node for each of the two or a hosted model for one of them brings a validation of several rows under the 30 seconds was not measured. A shorter prompt. With the retrieved context the prompt of the LLM was about 900 characters instead of about 50. A smaller k of the retrieval model, or smaller chunks, shorten it. No setting for the time limit is named here because none was found: the configuration definition sas.microanalyticservice.system of that system holds no timeout property (it holds core.numthreads 4 and, under asynchronousexecution, corepoolsize 5 and maxpoolsize 10), and no way to change the 30 seconds was tried.
documents.s: HTTP status 201, an empty error column and empty outputs in a publishing validation: the execution timed out

documents.t: This part of the troubleshooting guide describes what can be found in the log of a job that runs a program of the accelerator - the RAG ingestion job, a job generated from a RAG flow or the log parser.

On the test system (SAS Viya 2026.09, 2026-10-11) every job log of the SAS Studio compute context began with two ERROR messages, before the first source line of the program. They stand on three log lines, because the second is longer than the line: ERROR: Failed to connect to host '<SAS Viya host>', port 5570. ERROR: Unable to connect to Cloud Analytic Services <SAS Viya host> on port 5570. Verify connection parameters and retry. They stood in the logs of the RAG ingestion job, of the jobs generated from a RAG flow and of the log parser, and equally in a job that held none of the accelerator's code. The jobs ended as completed when nothing else failed, SYSCC was 0 after the log parser had run, and the CAS session the ingestion job starts itself connected on the same port. Why that system writes the two messages was not established: this is an observation of one system, and another system may not show it. What follows from it where a log shows these lines: A check that counts the ERROR lines of a job log never finds 0 there: it finds three when it counts the lines of the type error, the continuation included, and two when it counts the lines that start with ERROR. Start at the first source line of the program, or read the state of the job. The lines of the accelerator name their program: ERROR: RAG ingestion failed, ERROR: RAG - <step> failed, ERROR: The log could not be parsed. An ERROR line before source line 1 is none of them. Since release 2.3.0 the RAG lines are written from a variable and not as a quoted string; they are still of the type error (measured on 2026-10-11).
documents.s: Two ERROR messages about Cloud Analytic Services before the first line of the program

documents.t: The job logs of the test system are 132 characters wide, and a longer message goes on in the next log line. Where the break stands depends on who wrote the line. Measured on 2026-10-11 with the RAG steps and the ingestion job of release 2.3.0: A line a program of the accelerator writes with PUT - the ERROR line of a RAG step and of the ingestion job, a part of a step's summary - is cut after 132 characters, inside a word, and what follows has no prefix: ERROR: RAG - List Documents failed: another ingestion run holds the lock on this ledger - wait for it to finish, or retry in 30 minu tes if it crashed A long NOTE milestone and the WARNING lines of the steps were broken at a blank before column 132: the first log line ended with a word, in the logs of that day after 127 to 129 characters, and what followed was not indented. A message SAS writes itself is broken at a blank as well, and its next line is indented - as the second of the two connect messages above, which goes on with seven blanks and parameters and retry. Every log line of a message has the type of its first one: the three lines of a 311-character ERROR line of RAG - List Documents and the four of a 413-character ERROR line of the ingestion job were all of the type error, and the four lines of two WARNING messages of RAG - List Documents were all of the type warning. A search for the text of a message therefore has to expect a break in it - anywhere in a line written with PUT, at a blank in the others - and a check that counts lines counts a long message more than once.
documents.s: A long message goes on in the next line

documents.t: A run of the RAG ingestion job that failed ends as failed in SAS Job Execution from release 2.3.0 on. The record of the job does not hold the reason at its top level: measured on 2026-10-11, it held the error code 5713 with the message A procedure in the SAS program provided for the job completed execution with at least one error., and inside it, under errors, an error with the code 1012 - the SYSCC the program sets - and the text of the program's last ERROR line, for example RAG ingestion failed: another ingestion run appears active for this ledger (run lock held) - retry later. A monitor that wants the reason reads that inner message or the log. In the log the ERROR line is the last message of the program and not the last line: the timing lines of its DATA step and the echoed source of the last statement follow it. A job of the log parser that failed carried the same code 5713, with SYSCC 1012 in its log.
documents.s: A job of the accelerator that failed reports the error code 5713

documents.t: ERROR: There is no server connection to execute the action 'session.sessionId'., followed by ERROR: Unhandled Python exception. and ERROR: The log could not be parsed, the table <caslib>.<table> was left as it is., in a run of the step that follows an earlier run in the same SAS session: the earlier run had started a CAS session of its own and ended it, and the step of release 2.2 and earlier takes the macro variable _CASNAME_, which the ended session leaves behind, for a session. Nothing is written by such a run. Measured on 2026-10-11 with two runs of the step in one SAS Job Execution job whose session had no CAS session. The step of release 2.3.0 asks the SESSFOUND function instead - import it again with a PUT, which keeps its id. With that check the step was run on the same system later that day, twice and three times in one job whose session had no CAS session: every run started and ended a session of its own and wrote its table (Logging & Monitoring). With the older step, put a cas statement in front of the flow code: a step that finds a CAS session uses it and ends none.
